The apprentice’s letters made the school’s early years a living story of effort, friendship and unfinished hopes.
We wanted a living story of the street, so we paired the shop records with residents’ accounts of ordinary mornings.

advanced-native-1752.text: For me, the first worksheet was a graveyard of dates: it listed openings and closures but never explained who used the buildings or why the changes mattered to the neighbourhood.
The display need not be a graveyard of dates if each important year helps explain a change in people’s lives.
The introduction became a graveyard of dates when every year appeared without a person, question or consequence attached.
She kept the founding year but added the reason for the move, so the club history no longer felt like a graveyard of dates.

advanced-native-1753.text: The volunteers accepted the weekend project with their eyes open: they had read the tasks, asked about the time needed and knew the outdoor part might have to change if it rained.
I would like to make the choice with my eyes open, so could we discuss the time commitment before I say yes?
She joined the long rehearsal with her eyes open after the organiser explained the breaks and finishing time.
We went into the joint exhibition with our eyes open about the shared work, and reviewed the arrangement after the first week.

advanced-native-1755.text: In the essay, the old river crossings were a map behind the map: they helped explain why three present streets met at an apparently awkward angle, even though the riverbank had since changed.
The former market offers a map behind the map, helping us understand why the narrow lanes still lead towards the same square.
The old tram route became a map behind the map of the shopping street, explaining the unusual gap between the buildings.
She read the town’s earlier meeting places as a map behind the map of its present community life.

advanced-native-1757.text: I found the opening chapter heavy going because it introduced six unfamiliar terms without examples, though the later interview helped me understand why the subject mattered.
The first section was heavy going for me, but a worked example helped me follow the next part.
The dense introduction was heavy going for a first-time reader, so the tutor began with one familiar case.
Sorting the conflicting notes was heavy going, but the two interviews eventually helped us separate the events.

advanced-native-1758.text: The speaker moved beyond dry facts about the bridge’s length and opening year by explaining how it changed the daily journey to school, while keeping the measurements on the slide.
The figures need not remain dry facts if we explain which choices they helped people make.
The report’s dry facts became easier to follow once the writer connected the figures with one family’s weekly journey.
She kept the dry facts on the handout but used the talk to explain the choices behind the final design.

advanced-native-1759.text: The exhibition became a conversation with the past for me: I asked why the family had moved, read their letters and then reconsidered my first assumption that they had simply wanted a larger house.
Reading the diaries felt like a conversation with the past because each answer led me to a better question.
The old recipe notes opened a conversation with the past about who did the work behind each family meal.
Her questions turned the town walk into a conversation with the past, linking the street signs with older residents’ accounts.

advanced-native-1760.text: The local history room need not be a dusty shelf of dead facts, the tutor said; its records could help us ask why the public garden moved and whose walking routes were affected.
The archive was no longer a dusty shelf of dead facts once we used the records to trace a change in ordinary working lives.
The museum avoided becoming a dusty shelf of dead facts by asking visitors to trace who could enter the old school.
A cupboard of records became more than a dusty shelf of dead facts when the class used it to explain the lost bus route.

advanced-native-1762.text: In the story, the chair alone changed the entry rules and judged complaints about his own decisions; power went unchecked because the members had no independent way to question or review either choice.
In the novel, power goes unchecked when the ruler can silence the complaints and decide whether his own actions deserve review.
Power went unchecked in the fictional town because the official could block every request to examine his own decision.
The new appeals panel mattered in the story because power had gone unchecked under the former organiser.

advanced-native-617.text: The club’s weekday-only booking rule felt out of step with its members’ working patterns: several worked shifts, so the committee sought their available times before choosing a replacement rule.
The arrangement is out of step with the hours people actually work, so we should compare their availability before changing it.
The fixed timetable was out of step with the volunteers’ changing shifts, so they compared their available hours.
An old method is not necessarily out of step with present needs if it still serves the people using it.

advanced-native-618.text: I kept the interview notes close at hand while drafting the caption, so I could check the speaker’s exact words; the notes were available, but I still needed to ask permission before publishing the quotation.
The reference is close at hand, so I can check the wording, but I will still ask before using the quotation publicly.
She kept the map close at hand, checking it at each junction rather than guessing the route.
Help was close at hand when the volunteer offered to explain the unfamiliar controls.

advanced-native-619.text: The newsletter described a vertical community when residents on different floors began lending tools through a shared list; participation was voluntary, and the editor invited non-participants to say what other support they needed.
A vertical community can connect neighbours across floors while leaving room for different routines and ways of taking part.
The report explored how shared repairs helped neighbours form a vertical community without requiring everyone to attend the same meetings.
A vertical community includes people whose ways of helping and asking for help may differ.

advanced-native-620.text: The upstairs reading corner helped me rise above the rush of the festival: I spent ten quiet minutes with a poem, then returned to my stall, where the queue and my next shift were still waiting.
I can rise above the rush for a few quiet minutes and still return to the people and tasks that need my attention.
A quiet sketching session helped her rise above the rush before she returned to the day’s appointments.
He hoped to rise above the rush for a moment, not to pretend the unfinished work had disappeared.

advanced-native-621.text: The proposed coach park risked swallowing up too much land for the village fair, because its outline covered the only play area on the sketch; the organisers had asked for a smaller option before approving anything.
The plan could swallow up too much land if that outline removes the space needed for other activities, so we should compare the alternatives first.
The first layout risked swallowing up too much land, so the designers compared a smaller footprint before seeking approval.
The new road would swallow up the land used for the garden if the proposal went ahead.

advanced-native-622.text: We made more out of the short rehearsal by trying the difficult transition twice and discussing what changed, instead of running the whole piece again; the session still ended at the agreed time.
We can make more out of the time we have by choosing a clear focus and leaving room to discuss what we learn.
They made more out of the shared materials by letting each group explain a different use and compare the results.
We hoped to make more out of the visit by preparing questions, not by claiming we could see everything in one afternoon.

advanced-native-623.text: The writer feared that the holiday cabins would sprawl endlessly across the hillside if each new path led to another row; the sketch showed no agreed outer boundary, but only the first row had been built.
The development could sprawl endlessly without an agreed limit, but that is a concern about its direction rather than a claim that every planned building exists.
The map suggested that the estate might sprawl endlessly unless the next phase included a clear boundary.
The houses seemed to sprawl endlessly across the hillside, though the map showed a defined edge beyond the last row.

advanced-native-624.text: The designer called the courtyard human-scale because seats faced one another and short paths linked the entrances; visitors liked the easy conversations, though wheelchair users had not yet tested the narrow side gate.
The plan aims for a human-scale setting, but we still need to check how different people use its entrances, seats and paths.
The human-scale courtyard offered short routes between places to sit, but its entrance still needed a separate access check.
They asked what would make the square human-scale for different users instead of judging it only by the model’s appearance.

advanced-native-626.text: The rehearsal room was where the action was that afternoon: musicians were testing new arrangements and visitors could watch the changes, while the foyer remained the better place for a quiet interview.
I want to see where the action is, but I will choose a quieter space when the task calls for careful conversation.
The workshop was where the action was for visitors who wanted to see the first version being changed.
The festival room was in the middle of the action, though she chose a quieter corner to interview the organiser.

advanced-native-627.text: There was a certain buzz around the first display of student comics: people gathered to compare drawings and ask about the characters, though the organisers had not yet collected feedback or chosen work for the printed booklet.
There is a certain buzz around the project, but I want to hear the quieter reactions before describing what the group thinks.
The first shared reading created a buzz as people stayed to ask how the ending had changed.
There was a certain buzz in the foyer, though the formal feedback had not yet been collected.

advanced-native-628.text: The mood became almost contagious when one reader laughed at the unexpected ending and others began smiling, though a student beside me said she still found the scene sad and did not want to discuss it yet.
Excitement can be contagious, but I still want to ask how each person feels rather than assume that the whole group shares it.
Her excitement was contagious enough to draw curious questions, though not everyone wanted to try the activity.
The mood became contagious as the complaints spread, so he paused before adding his own impatient response.

advanced-native-629.text: By lunchtime the repair workshop was humming with life: volunteers compared broken toys, checked drawings and asked visitors what mattered to them, though several careful repairs happened quietly at the back bench.
The place was humming with life, not because everyone was loud, but because so many different exchanges and activities were under way.
The courtyard was humming with life as neighbours planted, repaired chairs and exchanged news in different corners.
The studio hummed with life even when some makers worked quietly, because ideas and materials were moving between the tables.

advanced-native-630.text: We stopped beside the musicians to soak up the atmosphere, listening to the tune and watching people greet one another; we bought nothing and still did not know what the song meant to the local performers.
I want to soak up the atmosphere without pretending that one enjoyable visit tells me everything about the people who live there.
They stayed by the open rehearsal to soak up the atmosphere, without claiming that they now understood every piece.
She soaked up the atmosphere in the courtyard, then asked a resident about the story behind the gathering.

advanced-native-631.text: The busy illustration table acted as social proof for me: I assumed other visitors had found it worthwhile, so I joined the queue before reading what the activity involved; only later did I check whether it suited beginners.
Social proof may draw my attention, but I still need to check what an activity involves and whether it fits my own purpose.
The full waiting room offered social proof, but she checked the session’s purpose before joining.
He noticed social proof influencing his first reaction and returned to the actual comments before deciding what he thought.

advanced-native-632.text: A river of people moved through the station towards the exits after the concert, but the view from the balcony did not tell us which trains they had taken or whether each person was going home.
A river of people passed beneath the balcony, though I could not know each person’s destination from the flow alone.
A river of people crossed the square, dividing towards two different exits at the far side.
She watched the river of people from the bridge without assuming that they all shared the same purpose.

advanced-native-633.text: A broken clock sprang to mind when the writer asked for an image of waiting, but I checked whether it fitted the character’s scene before suggesting it; the first image was a starting point, not a final choice.
The image sprang to mind immediately, but I still want to compare it with the scene before calling it the right choice.
A childhood scene sprang to mind, but she checked the details before including it in the memoir.
Nothing useful sprang to mind at first, so he took time to compare the examples in his notes.

advanced-native-634.text: In the narrator’s first view, the festival felt turned up to full volume: drums, flashing signs and people calling across the street all competed for attention; her companion enjoyed it, while she wanted a slower look from the edge.
The scene felt turned up to full volume, with several sensations competing for attention, though that was my impression rather than a sound measurement.
The opening felt turned up to full volume, then one still image gave the reader time to notice the character.
The narrator described the street as turned up to full volume without claiming that anyone had measured its noise.

advanced-native-636.text: On my first evening, the city seemed to come at me through bus announcements, bright windows and people crossing in every direction; my cousin knew the route and found the same street familiar rather than overwhelming.
The city seemed to come at me from every direction that evening, though I knew this was my first impression rather than everyone’s experience.
The city seemed to come at her through signs and voices until her friend helped her find one familiar landmark.
The city seems to come at you in his opening paragraph, but a later scene offers a calmer view from another character.

advanced-native-638.text: Updating the same attendance table every week felt like running on a treadmill to me: the records stayed useful, but I wanted to learn how to interview members, so I asked to share a different task next month.
The routine feels like a treadmill for my learning, though I know it has a useful purpose and want to discuss a manageable change.
The endless revisions felt like a treadmill until the group agreed what this version needed before it could be shared.
The useful routine still felt like running on a treadmill to her because she wanted a different kind of learning as well.

advanced-native-639.text: The team’s weekend plan looked like all work and no play: every hour was assigned to rehearsing or packing, so they asked members which duties could be shared to leave a little unplanned time rather than add another required outing.
I do not want the weekend to become all work and no play, but I would leave people free to choose what feels enjoyable to them.
The week had become all work and no play, so they discussed which duties could be shared to protect some free time.
Avoiding all work and no play did not mean everyone had to enjoy the same game.

advanced-native-640.text: A quiet hour sorting old photographs helped me recharge after hosting the reading group; my friend preferred a walk, so we made separate plans and agreed to meet later rather than insist on one shared way to rest.
I need a little time to recharge in my own way, and then I would like to return to the conversation.
She chose an evening with her sketchbook to recharge, while her friends enjoyed a lively outing.
He asked for time to recharge before returning to the discussion, rather than promising that one break would solve everything.

advanced-native-641.text: The plan needed a heartbeat rather than just a traffic system, the resident said: the routes were clear, but there was no place for the weekly story exchange, so she asked where neighbours could meet without blocking the paths.
A city needs a heartbeat rather than just a traffic system, with places for shared life as well as routes that people can use.
She wanted a heartbeat rather than just a traffic system, so the proposal included residents’ accounts of where they met.
The essay called for a heartbeat rather than just a traffic system without dismissing the need for clear, usable routes.

advanced-native-642.text: After the weekly reading corner closed, the library felt dull and grey around the edges to Mina: she missed the familiar greetings, though the shelves still held books she loved and other visitors enjoyed their quiet routines.
The place feels dull and grey around the edges to me now, though I can still name things I value and know others may feel differently.
The familiar place felt dull and grey around the edges after the shared meals ended, though other parts of daily life continued.
She described the week as dull and grey around the edges, then named the small exchange that had brought some warmth back.

advanced-native-643.text: For our reading group, the benefits outweighed the drawbacks of the free, quiet room, though chairs had to be carried upstairs; before confirming, we asked whether every member was comfortable with that arrangement.
For this purpose, the benefits outweigh the drawbacks, but I want to name the remaining costs and hear from the people affected.
For that group, the benefits outweighed the drawbacks, but the extra preparation still had to be shared fairly.
She asked whether the benefits outweigh the drawbacks for this purpose, rather than assuming everyone would value the trade-off equally.

advanced-native-644.text: Leah hoped the editing course would help her get ahead in community publishing by making her feedback clearer; she had begun practising with a colleague, but no new role had been offered or promised.
I hope to get ahead by developing this skill and learning with others, without assuming that one course guarantees a new role.
She wanted to get ahead in editing, so she asked for feedback on a skill she could actually practise.
Getting ahead did not require him to claim the whole project as his own; the shared work helped him learn.

advanced-native-645.text: Practising the short introduction gave Ben a better shot at explaining his project clearly at the interview, but it did not decide who would receive the workshop place; he still needed to bring the required sample.
This preparation gives me a better shot at explaining my idea, but I still need to meet the requirements and wait for the decision.
A clear example gave her a better shot at explaining the idea, although the audience could still disagree.
He had a better shot at completing the task with the missing instructions restored, but he still needed to do the work.

advanced-native-646.text: The pace of life felt slower during my week at my aunt’s house because I had fewer appointments and no morning commute; she, however, was managing two jobs, so I could not describe her days from my holiday routine.
The pace of life feels different during this holiday, but I would ask about residents’ routines before comparing it with their everyday experience.
The pace of life changed for him when the longer commute left less time between work and evening commitments.
She described the pace of life in her own household, not a rule about everyone living in the same town.

advanced-native-649.text: After choosing to help record her neighbours’ stories, Ada felt that life was moving somewhere: she had a purpose for her writing, although the project was still small and she did not know where it would lead.
I feel that life is moving somewhere when my next step serves something I value, even if I cannot yet see the final outcome.
He felt that life was moving somewhere after choosing a project he could explain in his own terms.
For her, life is moving somewhere through a quiet commitment, not because every uncertainty has disappeared.

advanced-native-650.text: The printing room was working at full speed before the exhibition, with two people feeding pages and another checking samples; the pace was high, but the final stack still needed counting before anyone could say the order was complete.
We are working at full speed, but I still need the final count before reporting that the whole order is ready.
The team worked at full speed until the first trial, then slowed down to examine what still needed changing.
Running at full speed did not tell them whether the final stack contained every required page.

advanced-native-1126.text: I wanted to grow something on the balcony but kept putting it off; my neighbour’s offer of one spare cutting was a small nudge in the right direction, and I chose a pot and asked how to begin.
Her short question was a small nudge in the right direction, helping me choose an opening without writing the story for me.
The note beside the unfamiliar tool was a gentle nudge in the right direction, prompting him to ask for a demonstration before trying it.
Her suggestion was a small nudge in the right direction, but the final choice about joining the group remained mine.

advanced-native-1127.text: Finishing our first shared story was already a pleasure; having it read aloud at the village evening was the icing on the cake, not the reason we had begun writing together.
The unexpected invitation was the icing on the cake, because we had already enjoyed making something together.
The friendly message was the icing on the cake after she had already enjoyed the afternoon’s music.
Finishing the garden mattered most; the invitation to show it to visitors was the icing on the cake.

advanced-native-1128.text: We agreed to put in more effort when comparing the two accounts: each of us would mark the claim, find its supporting detail and bring one uncertainty to the discussion, rather than simply read the pages again.
I will put in more effort by practising the part I find difficult and asking for feedback on that part.
She put in more effort on the unclear section, asking a reader which link was still missing.
Putting in more effort helped him notice the repeated error, although he still needed to test the correction.

advanced-native-1131.text: The recorded demonstration let Mira learn at her own pace: she paused at the unfamiliar turn and replayed it, while her partner moved through a part he already knew; both still planned to meet for practice on Saturday.
I can work at my own pace on this part, while agreeing a clear handover time with the people who need it next.
The quiet reading session let her follow the argument at her own pace instead of rushing to match the next reader.
They prepared at their own pace during the week, then brought their questions to the agreed group meeting.

advanced-native-1132.text: The teacher wanted feedback to lift children up rather than weigh them down, so she named one clear strength and one change they could try, without calling a confusing first draft proof that they were bad writers.
I want this feedback to lift children up rather than weigh them down, with an honest description of the problem and one possible next step.
The coach wanted the discussion to lift children up rather than weigh them down, so she separated the missed pass from a judgement about the player.
The comments can lift children up rather than weigh them down when they make a difficult next step understandable.

advanced-native-1133.text: The editor’s message was a pat on the back for Mira’s clearer ending: it praised the link she had added, but said the rest of the manuscript would be discussed at next week’s meeting.
I appreciated the pat on the back, and I still wanted to know which part of the work needed attention next.
The volunteers deserved a pat on the back for keeping the welcome calm when several guests arrived together.
Her message gave him a pat on the back for the revised question without claiming that the whole interview was ready.

advanced-native-1135.text: The workshop decided to invest in people by reserving paid learning time and pairing newcomers with experienced makers; the first sessions had begun, but the team had not yet evaluated what skills participants could use independently.
Investing in people means making useful support available, then listening to how they can use it and what else they need.
The organisation invested in people by giving experienced volunteers time to support the next group of newcomers.
They are investing in people, but they still ask participants whether the learning arrangements fit their circumstances.

advanced-native-1136.text: At the closing session, the leader handed out rewards for the agreed rehearsal tasks and explained the checklist used; one certificate stayed on the table because its recipient had left early and would collect it later.
Before we hand out rewards, let us make the criteria and collection arrangements clear to the people involved.
They handed out prizes after explaining which contributions the awards recognised.
The rewards were ready, but the organiser waited for the recipients before handing them out.

advanced-native-1137.text: Ravi took charge of the book exchange by agreeing the collection times and asking volunteers to cover each table; the committee still decided the membership rules, and he referred a new eligibility question back to them.
I can take charge of the practical arrangements while checking which decisions still need the group’s agreement.
She took charge of the workshop rota and asked each helper to confirm the time they could actually offer.
He was ready to take charge of the display setup, but wanted the group to agree the layout before he moved anything.

advanced-native-1138.text: The question about who was missing from the photograph acted like a spark for the archive group: members began listing people to interview, though they had not yet checked names or asked anyone for permission.
The small question acted like a spark for our enquiry, but the ideas still needed careful checking and willing participants.
The child’s question acted like a spark for a new ending, and the writer began trying a different final conversation.
The unexpected colour pairing acts like a spark for her sketches, though she chooses which ideas to develop afterwards.

advanced-native-1140.text: When the game organiser suggested ignoring an agreed pause because it might help the other team, Lee objected to winning at all costs; he wanted a serious match without breaking the rule both sides had accepted.
I want to win, but not to win at all costs by breaking the agreement that made the contest fair.
The captain rejected winning at all costs when a proposed shortcut would have broken the team’s agreement with its opponents.
She could enjoy the challenge without trying to win at all costs or treating a friend’s disappointment as irrelevant.

advanced-native-1142.text: After repeatedly interrupting, Tom decided to turn over a new leaf: at the next meeting he wrote down his question and waited for a pause, then asked others whether the new arrangement gave them enough space.
I want to turn over a new leaf, and I know I need to show that in what I do rather than ask people to forget the earlier harm.
She turned over a new leaf by returning borrowed materials when promised and asking before changing the collection date.
He hoped to turn over a new leaf, but his apology still needed to be followed by a different way of handling the next disagreement.

advanced-native-1143.text: For Noor, getting life back on track after the move began with a regular library visit and a weekly call to her sister; she still had boxes to unpack, but those two arrangements restored parts of the routine she valued.
Getting my life back on track means choosing which routines and relationships I want to rebuild, not simply filling every hour.
She began to get her life back on track by restoring contact with the friends she had missed, while leaving other decisions open.
Getting life back on track after the disruption took several small changes, not a single promise that everything was normal again.

advanced-native-1144.text: During the launch week, I felt swallowed up by work: even at dinner I kept returning to the unanswered messages, although I wanted to hear my brother’s news and knew the project was only one part of my life.
I felt swallowed up by work during that period, even though I still cared about the people and activities I was missing.
He felt swallowed up by work during the festival, then noticed how many personal messages he had left for another day.
The diary described her as swallowed up by work for that month, while still recording the friendships she wanted to return to.

advanced-native-1145.text: We set aside part of the display fund for replacement labels, but had not ordered any yet; the amount was reserved so that a later correction would not depend on taking money promised to the visitor guide.
We set aside time for checking the final version, but reserving that time did not mean the checking had already happened.
They set aside a quiet hour for reviewing the recordings before choosing what to publish.
The shared room was small, but the group set aside one table for materials that still needed checking.

advanced-native-1148.text: Trying to reduce disposable cups felt like swimming against the current when the festival’s own purchasing list kept specifying single-use packs; the volunteers asked to review the list rather than simply collect more cups afterwards.
I feel I am swimming against the current when the process rewards the opposite of the careful work we say we want.
Keeping the conversation open felt like swimming against the current when each interruption pushed the group towards a quick verdict.
She was swimming against the current of the usual programme, asking for a quiet observation period before the next public presentation.

advanced-native-1149.text: The extra printing ate into our budget for the display: the agreed total stayed the same, but after paying for corrected pages we had less left for mounts, so the group compared which ones could be reused.
The extra requests are eating into our rehearsal time, so we need to agree what can wait until after the practice.
The repeated copying ate into her time and energy, leaving less attention for the interview itself.
Sorting the mislabeled boxes ate into the day, so the team postponed the garden visit.

advanced-native-1226.text: My excitement about the first exhibition was wrapped up with worry about showing my drawings to my old teacher; I wanted her to see them, but her opinion mattered more to me than the visitor numbers.
My excitement was wrapped up with worry about how someone important to me would respond.
Her pride in the finished quilt was wrapped up with memories of the aunt who had taught her to sew.
His wish to keep the shop was wrapped up with concern for the neighbours who met there each morning.

advanced-native-1227.text: I made a quick sketch to capture the moment when Grandpa recognised his old schoolfriend at the gate; I kept their surprised smiles, rather than trying to draw everyone at the reunion.
I wanted to capture the moment in a few lines, especially the surprise on their faces.
Her two-line diary entry captured the moment the empty room filled with applause.
The blurred photograph still captured the moment our dog noticed us at the station.

advanced-native-1228.text: My cousins get their kicks from solving the trickiest clues at our weekly puzzle night; I prefer drawing the little maps, so we enjoy the same evening in different ways.
I get my kicks from finding an unexpected answer, though other people may enjoy a different part of the game.
She gets her kicks from spotting the tiny changes between the two drawings.
We got our kicks from inventing a different ending for each puppet-show rehearsal.

advanced-native-1229.text: Posting every rehearsal felt like putting my life on display, so I chose one short clip for the public page and kept the rest for the band; I still enjoyed sharing, but wanted a boundary around it.
I enjoy sharing an experience without always putting it on display for a public audience.
She chose one paragraph for the newsletter instead of putting the experience on display in every detail.
The public diary left him feeling that he was putting his life on display, so he changed who could read it.

advanced-native-1231.text: Reading my unfinished poem to the group had a sharp edge of risk for me: they might misunderstand the ending, and I could not edit their first reaction, though I wanted to hear it.
The sharp edge of risk came from sharing an unfinished idea without knowing how it would be received.
The sharp edge of risk was the possibility that the audience would hear a different story from the one I meant to tell.
Her first live demonstration had a sharp edge of risk because she would have to answer unexpected questions.

advanced-native-1232.text: Seeing my own missed line in the recording jolted me awake to how often I interrupted the other actor; I began marking where to wait, rather than blaming the noisy room for every overlap.
The unexpected example jolted me awake to something I had been overlooking, and I began to ask different questions.
One visitor’s question jolted us awake to the missing explanation beside the map.
Hearing the two recordings together jolted her awake to how much the narrator’s tone changed the ending.

advanced-native-1233.text: Hearing the audience sing our last chorus gave me an incredible high; on the quiet bus home I felt tired and ordinary again, but that did not make the shared moment any less special.
The shared applause gave me an incredible high, though I was ready for a quiet evening afterwards.
The final bow brought an incredible high after weeks of rehearsing in an empty room.
She remembered the incredible high of hearing her first story read on the school radio.

advanced-native-1234.text: I tested my limits by telling a longer story without my usual notes; I managed the opening, then lost the order near the end, which showed me where I needed another rehearsal.
I wanted to test my limits, then use what happened to choose a useful next step.
Writing a scene with no dialogue tested her limits and changed how she used small gestures.
He tested his limits by explaining the project without slides, then asked which part needed a clearer example.

advanced-native-1236.text: Cooking the festival meal with my mother felt like a rite of passage when she asked me to lead the preparations for the first time; I was taking a family role, not simply learning another recipe.
It felt like a rite of passage because I was trusted with a role I had only watched before.
Her first turn leading the neighbourhood walk became a rite of passage into the organising team.
For him, handing a finished key to the new tenant felt like a rite of passage into working life.

advanced-native-1237.text: The voice inside my head said the audience would notice every pause, but the first listener asked about the story instead; I began to separate my prediction from what people actually told me.
The voice inside my head was making a prediction, so I decided to listen to the response before treating it as fact.
The voice inside his head urged him to rush, but he chose to read the question once more.
She answered the voice inside her head with a reminder that one unfinished sketch was not her whole body of work.

advanced-native-1238.text: Asking my former classmate to read the draft felt like climbing over an inner barrier; I had feared seeming inexperienced, but now I could ask one honest question without pretending the whole story was finished.
I climbed over an inner barrier when I asked for help instead of pretending I already knew the answer.
She climbed over an inner barrier when she invited criticism of the scene she cared about most.
He was still hesitant, but asking his partner to slow down felt like climbing over an inner barrier.

advanced-native-1239.text: I wanted the prize, but not at any price: when the team suggested hiding our partner’s contribution, I chose to credit her even if it meant sharing the award.
I want the opportunity, but not at any price; the way we reach it matters to me too.

The narrator rejected a machine for storing people and began to show the choices made behind the numbered doors.
A city need not become a machine for storing people when its residents have a voice in how daily spaces are used.

advanced-native-660.text: The character’s careful folding gave away clues about an earlier job: she made the same precise crease without thinking, but the reader still needed another scene before knowing where she had learned it.
The detail gives away clues about her past, but I want more context before choosing one explanation.
The handwriting gave away clues about a shared habit, though the narrator waited before naming the connection.
Small details can give away clues without telling us everything about the person behind them.

advanced-native-662.text: The writer sketched the outline of the story, from the lost invitation to the final meeting, but left the middle scenes open; the group could discuss its direction without pretending that every character decision had been written.
I can sketch the outline of what happened, but I would like to decide which personal details I am comfortable sharing.
She sketched the outline of the visit, leaving the exact times for a later discussion.
The speaker could sketch the outline without being ready to explain every personal detail.

advanced-native-664.text: For the school play, Ravi dressed the part of the gardener in the apron named in the director’s notes, but he still needed to practise the scene; the costume made the role visible, not the lines automatically remembered.
I want to dress the part for this occasion, but I will check the actual expectations rather than assume that higher cost means a better fit.
The actor dressed the part with a simple costume, then worked on the gestures that made the character believable.
She asked what it meant to dress the part at that event instead of assuming every occasion required the same outfit.

advanced-native-665.text: I got the wrong end of the stick when “bring a draft” made me think a finished article was due; the editor meant rough notes for discussion, so I asked her to confirm the level of preparation before rewriting everything.
I may have got the wrong end of the stick, so could you explain whether you want rough notes or a complete draft?
He got the wrong end of the stick about the invitation and asked which part of the meeting was open to visitors.
She thought she had got the wrong end of the stick, so she checked the message before assigning blame.

advanced-native-666.text: Some volunteers doubted the newcomer because his shirt had paint stains, though his checklist helped organise the display; the coordinator said not to judge a book by its cover and asked them to examine his contribution.
I do not want to judge a book by its cover, so I will look at the work and the needs of this task before deciding.
She refused to judge a book by its cover and read the proposal before deciding whether it met the group’s needs.
Not judging a book by its cover means asking for relevant evidence, not assuming that every first impression must be wrong.

advanced-native-667.text: Their grandfather’s patched coat brought memories to the cousins, while a visitor saw only an old garment. “Clothes may speak,” my aunt said, “but what you hear can depend on what you already know.”
Clothes may speak, but I would rather hear the wearer’s own explanation than turn my first impression into a fact about them.
Clothes may speak through shared associations, but the meaning is not always the one a stranger first imagines.
She said clothes may speak, then asked the wearer what the borrowed jacket meant to him.

advanced-native-668.text: After her illustration won a prize, Nia kept the response low-key: she thanked the group in a short private note and said she was delighted, but preferred not to make a public announcement that week.
A low-key response can be sincere; I would ask how she wants to share the news rather than assume that quiet means unhappy.
Her low-key reply thanked the helpers without turning the prize into a public celebration.
They chose a low-key welcome with a short conversation, because their guest had asked for a quiet evening.

advanced-native-669.text: Attendance was one piece of the puzzle when we reviewed the open day: many visitors came, but we also needed to ask whether they could follow the activities and find someone to answer their questions.
That figure is one piece of the puzzle; I would connect it with people’s experiences before claiming to understand the whole situation.
The repair date was one piece of the puzzle; the old letters helped explain why the family had left before it.
Her account supplied one piece of the puzzle, and the interviewer asked what the other witnesses had seen.

advanced-native-670.text: I add an example when the moment calls for one, such as when a listener asks how an idea works in practice; if the question only concerns the meeting time, I answer that directly rather than give another long explanation.
I can offer more detail when the moment calls for it, but I first need to understand what the other person is asking.
She used a brief example when the moment called for one, then returned to the question about the plan.
We can change the arrangement when the occasion calls for it, after asking which need the change would address.

advanced-native-672.text: The worn handles and repeated repairs tell a story about how often the community used the old cupboard, but they do not identify who made each repair; the curator plans to ask former volunteers before naming anyone.
These marks tell a story about past use, but I would look for more evidence before naming the people behind them.
The patched sleeves tell a story of long use, though the label does not say who sewed them.
The notes in the margins told a story of changing plans as the writer reconsidered the ending.

advanced-native-673.text: In the imagined town, shared bread has moved from the centre of everyday life to the edges of ceremony: it is no longer part of ordinary meals, but families still prepare it to welcome a new household.
The practice has moved from the centre of everyday life to the edges of ceremony, but its place in that welcome still matters to the family.
In the fictional village, the greeting moved from the centre of everyday life to the edges of ceremony, surviving mainly at naming celebrations.
Their song moved from the centre of everyday life to the edges of ceremony, yet the grandmother still chose its final verse for the farewell.

advanced-native-674.text: The initial excitement faded away as the group’s messages became less frequent over several weeks, but one member still wanted to try again; she asked what had made joining difficult rather than assume nobody cared.
The excitement may fade away, but I want to ask what people need before assuming that a quieter response means nobody cares.
The laughter faded away down the corridor, while she stayed behind to finish the note.
His early excitement began to fade away after several cancelled meetings, so he asked whether the group wanted to change its plans.

advanced-native-675.text: First impressions count at our new reading group: a clear welcome and a named contact helped two newcomers ask questions, but we still needed to learn from their later visits rather than judge the whole group from one evening.
First impressions count, but I want our welcome to be followed by the same clear help during later visits.
First impressions count, so she greeted the new volunteers clearly and showed them whom to ask for help.
He knew first impressions count, but he listened again before letting one awkward introduction define his new colleague.

advanced-native-676.text: When the label date conflicted with the notebook, Ella turned to the archive volunteer for guidance; he suggested checking the original register, which she had not yet seen, rather than choosing whichever date looked neater.
I can turn to someone for support while being clear about what I need and what I still want to decide myself.
She turned to the old programme for information about which performers had appeared in the first production.
He turned to his friend for comfort after the rejection, asking whether she had time to listen.

advanced-native-677.text: The welcome team became the public face of the museum during the open day, answering visitors’ first questions and collecting feedback; they passed requests about membership changes to the committee rather than promise new rules themselves.
Being the public face of the group means meeting people openly, while being honest about which decisions belong to others.
The receptionist was the public face of the company for first-time visitors, though the training team worked behind the scenes.
As the public face of the project, she introduced the helpers rather than accept every compliment as her own.

advanced-native-678.text: With the apron and display badge, Sami looked the part of a workshop guide, but he was still learning the route; he welcomed visitors, then asked an experienced colleague when someone needed directions to the second room.
Looking the part can shape a first impression, but I would ask what the person can actually do before judging their ability.
The borrowed coat helped him look the part, while the rehearsal taught him how to move and speak as the character.
She looked the part at the desk, but asked for help rather than invent an answer to a visitor’s unfamiliar question.

advanced-native-679.text: Training helped Lila perform the part of an archive helper: she showed visitors how to request a file and referred a damaged-page question to the conservator, rather than improvise advice outside her role.
I want to perform the part through what I actually do, including asking for the expertise the task needs.
The practice helped him perform the part of a facilitator, inviting a quiet participant without requiring an immediate answer.
She performed the part of a guide by giving clear directions and checking the question she could not yet answer.

advanced-native-680.text: Our invitation designs shifted from following the rules to bending them: after using the same formal template, we tried a handwritten opening and an uneven border, while keeping the date and reply details easy to find.
We moved from following the rules to bending them, but we still asked which choices helped the work communicate.
The designer moved from following the rules to bending them, combining a formal layout with a playful handwritten heading.
Their poems shifted from following the rules to bending them as shorter lines began to echo the hesitations in the speaker’s voice.

advanced-native-681.text: The new club timetable kept a sharper line between rehearsal and social time than last term: announcements moved to the opening ten minutes, while the break remained open for conversation, with urgent changes still agreed separately.
We need a sharper line between what the witness said and what I inferred, while checking the evidence for both.
The revised caption drew a sharper line between the date in the register and the later family recollection.
They kept a sharper line between group decisions and personal suggestions, while leaving room to discuss exceptions.

advanced-native-682.text: At the small gallery, scientific diagrams rubbed shoulders with personal poems on neighbouring panels; visitors could move between them, but the curator had not claimed that every writer had worked with a scientist.
Different styles can rub shoulders in one place without losing their separate histories or becoming the same thing.
Old shopfronts rub shoulders with new studios on the fictional street, and the narrator notices what each brings to the scene.
At the workshop supper, beginners rubbed shoulders with experienced makers and asked about the pieces on the table.

advanced-native-683.text: We chose a mix-and-match outfit for the character: an old school jacket, a borrowed skirt and a scarf from the costume box; we tested them together rather than assume different origins made the character convincing.
A mix-and-match approach can be deliberate, but I still want to explain why these particular pieces belong together.
Her mix-and-match display combined family drawings with recent photographs, with a date beside every piece.
The group tried a mix-and-match layout, then removed one element that distracted from the visitor’s question.

advanced-native-685.text: Publishing selection criteria before applications opened helped level the playing field for newcomers without personal contacts; organisers still needed to check whether everyone could access and understand the examples.
The change may help level the playing field, but I want to name the barrier it reduces and ask what still remains.
Providing the same instructions early helped level the playing field for applicants who could not attend the private briefing.
The shared equipment helped level the playing field, though each student still needed to develop and explain a design.

advanced-native-686.text: After the host explained where to leave her bag and whom she could ask, Ina felt more at ease and raised a question about the first activity; she still needed the instructions, but no longer worried about interrupting the wrong person.
I felt more at ease once I knew I could ask, even though I still had questions about what to do next.
He felt more at ease after the group let him choose whether to read aloud or share the page privately.
She felt more at ease with her brother once he listened without finishing her sentences for her.

advanced-native-687.text: Without the usual bright lanyard, the guide blended into the crowd near the ticket table; two visitors walked past before recognising her voice, so she asked for the sign that normally marked the meeting point.
I may blend into the crowd in these clothes, but that does not say how much I have contributed to the work.
He blended into the crowd near the door until his friend recognised the tune he was humming.
She chose to blend into the crowd at the celebration, while keeping her name in the list of contributors.

advanced-native-688.text: Flexible arrival times came with trade-offs for the open studio: more families could visit, but volunteers needed to cover a longer welcome period; the group compared shifts before deciding how many hours it could offer.
The change may come with trade-offs, so I want to explain both what it offers and what someone would have to give up.
The simpler ending came with trade-offs: the main decision was clearer, but one friendship received less attention.
The extra evening session comes with trade-offs, so the organisers asked who could cover it before announcing the time.

advanced-native-689.text: After many patient conversations, the volunteers’ blue pin became a badge of trust for regular visitors, who felt able to ask for help; volunteers still checked unfamiliar questions with the coordinator.
The card became a badge of trust because of the help people associated with it, not because it removed the need to check.
The shared notebook became a badge of trust when members began recording questions they were not yet ready to ask aloud.
For the former apprentice, the worn key was a badge of trust from a teacher who had let her open the workshop.

advanced-native-690.text: The coloured calendar showed the room change at a glance, but it did not explain why the change was made; I checked the organiser’s message for that and noticed that the start time had stayed the same.
I could see the difference at a glance, but I still needed to read more before explaining what caused it.
She recognised the changed heading at a glance, then read the paragraph to understand the new argument.
The two keys looked different at a glance, but he checked their labels before choosing which one to return.

advanced-native-691.text: During the fast-moving situation around the delayed rehearsal, the room booking changed twice; the coordinator dated each update, kept the confirmed start time visible and marked the final room as pending rather than send a guess.
In a fast-moving situation, I need to say when the information was checked and which part still needs an answer.
The organiser dated each notice in the fast-moving situation, so helpers could distinguish the latest plan from earlier versions.
A fast-moving situation made the final location uncertain, while the agreed reporting time remained clear.

advanced-native-692.text: Choosing the final poem mattered to Noor, but it was not life-and-death serious: either choice would leave the reading intact, so she asked for a short pause rather than cancel the evening.
The choice mattered to me, but it was not life-and-death serious, and I could ask for time without treating it as a crisis.
The costume decision felt important, but it was not life-and-death serious, so the actors agreed to try both versions.
She reminded herself that the typo was not life-and-death serious before sending a calm correction to the group.

advanced-native-693.text: Saying how to pronounce each name smoothed interaction at the reading circle: newcomers could address one another without guessing, although they still disagreed about the story’s ending.
A clear introduction can smooth interaction without making different opinions disappear.
The host’s explanation of when guests could ask questions smoothed interaction during the shared meal.
Checking what her partner meant by the word smoothed interaction before they discussed the disagreement itself.

advanced-native-695.text: Seeing an unfamiliar name on the reading list, Finn made a snap judgment that the story would be difficult; after reading the opening, he found the sentences clear and decided to judge the work by more than its title page.
I made a snap judgment from one detail, and I want to hear the rest before deciding what that detail means.
He avoided a snap judgment about the unfinished drawing and asked the artist what she was still trying to change.
Her snap judgments about the unfamiliar voices softened when she listened to the full conversations.

advanced-native-696.text: When Mei asked about one unfamiliar editing term, the tutor talked down to her, saying that people like her could not handle the whole task; she asked him to explain the term without judging her ability from one question.
I do not want to talk down to you; please tell me which part you want explained and what you already know.
The editor answered the newcomer’s question without talking down to her or pretending that she should already know every term.
He apologised for talking down to his partner and asked what kind of support would actually be useful.

advanced-native-698.text: To reserve the club’s rehearsal room, Asha had to jump through hoops: three forms repeated the same details and two people requested separate copies; approval was still pending when she asked which steps could be combined.
I felt I had to jump through hoops, so I asked which requirements served a purpose and which repeated information already supplied.
The applicants felt they were jumping through hoops when each reviewer asked them to resubmit the same explanation in a different form.
He asked whether the club could stop making returning members jump through hoops to renew a simple equipment loan.

advanced-native-699.text: The indexed rehearsal notes put last week’s decisions at our fingertips: we could find the chosen opening without searching every message, but a later change still needed confirmation from the director.
Having information at my fingertips helps me find it, but I still need to check whether it answers the question I am asking.
The small reference card put the unfamiliar editing terms at her fingertips while she read the manuscript.
He had the recorded dates at his fingertips, but he asked the interviewee before attributing a reason to the move.

advanced-native-700.text: The repair workshop and the reading club met under one roof after the old hall reopened, using different rooms; sharing the building made visits easier, but they kept separate membership and booking arrangements.
Living under one roof gives us shared spaces, but we still need to ask how each person wants to use them.
The library and the small theatre now operate under one roof, with their own opening hours and separate bookings.
The sisters lived under one roof that summer, but they still asked before borrowing things from each other’s rooms.

advanced-native-1129.text: An invitation to show a short scene lit a fire under the group: they stopped hesitating, booked a practice and chose roles, though they still needed props before rehearsing the full piece.
The challenge lit a fire under the group, but we still checked that they had the time and materials to take the next step.
The approaching exhibition lit a fire under the team, and they finally agreed on which pieces to practise first.
A challenge she can actually meet may light a fire under a student who has lost momentum.

advanced-native-1139.text: The short deadline woke the group up to a missing permission note: they stopped polishing the title and asked the photographer what could be shared, but the answer had not arrived when the meeting ended.
The conversation woke me up to the missing information, but I still needed to ask rather than fill the gap with a guess.
The unexpected question woke the team up to a gap in the visitor guide, and they asked newcomers to test that section.
The former pupil’s letter woke the team up to the missing names in the school display, and they asked the archive for the original register.

advanced-native-1803.text: The bags are put away, but the memories stay with us: a month after the journey, we still talk about the stranger who helped us find the family’s old street.
The bags are put away, but the memories stay with us whenever that song reminds us of our first evening together.
The bags are put away, but the memories stay with us: the smell of oranges still brings back our conversation in the market.
The bags are put away, but the memories stay with us, including the awkward mistake we can now laugh about together.

advanced-native-1804.text: Although we shared a flat, we were running on different tracks: I left for work before dawn and Leah came home after midnight, so most of our conversations were notes beside the kettle.
We have been running on different tracks lately, so I would like to agree on one time when we can talk properly.
The two committees were running on different tracks until they compared the dates on their separate invitations.
We ran on different tracks during the busy season, but a weekly call helped us keep some time together.

advanced-native-1807.text: The harbour was picture-perfect in the evening light, but our visit was less smooth: we missed the last boat and had to wait for a bus, laughing about the wrong timetable.
The room looked picture-perfect in the photograph, but I still wanted to know how the tables would work for our discussion.
They chose the picture-perfect square for the opening photograph, then added a separate note about the steps at its entrance.
Our picnic was not picture-perfect after the rain, but we found shelter and enjoyed the conversation.

advanced-native-1809.text: I enjoyed the postcard view across the lake, but the part I kept talking about afterwards was our long conversation with the woman who ran the ferry office.
The postcard view attracted us to the village, but I wanted our account to include more than the scenery.
The postcard view filled the first page, while the next page explained how the harbour’s working hours shaped local routines.
The brochure shows the postcard version of the fishing village; the interviews tell a fuller story.

advanced-native-1810.text: For our account of the ferry crossing, we wanted the human view as well as the coastline, so we asked a regular passenger how the service fitted around her weekly visits to her father.
I wanted the human view of the market, so I listened to how one stallholder described returning there each morning.
The human view of the station emerged in a porter’s story about helping a family find their first train home.
The human view mattered in her diary: she recorded the guide’s patient explanation alongside the mountain scene.

advanced-native-1811.text: We had barely spoken during the busy month, but cooking together helped bring us back to one another: we began asking about the days we had missed, although we still needed to discuss the household rota.
The shared afternoon brought us back to one another, giving us time to listen before returning to the question we still disagreed about.
Reading their old letters brought them back to one another and started a conversation about the years they had spent apart.
The neighbourhood meal helped bring people back to one another after months of passing without stopping to talk.

advanced-native-1813.text: Travelling alone, I could change course on a whim: a song from an open doorway made me leave the planned square and spend the afternoon listening nearby, with no companion’s plans to rearrange.
I sometimes change course on a whim when I am exploring alone, but shared plans call for a conversation first.
She changed course on a whim after seeing a pottery display and spent her free hour talking to the maker.
Maya did not sign up for the night course on a whim: she compared the timetable and costs first.

advanced-native-1814.text: Choosing my own afternoon felt like breathing with my full lungs after a week of following everyone else’s timetable; I could stop at the small gallery without asking the group to change its plans.
Writing without a fixed topic felt like breathing with my full lungs after weeks of fitting every sentence into the same format.
An afternoon with no expected performance felt like breathing with her full lungs; she could paint simply because she wanted to.
For him, choosing a small project of his own was like breathing with his full lungs after months of completing only assigned work.

advanced-native-1815.text: Nora wanted to join the exhibition on her own terms: she was happy to show two drawings, but asked not to give a public speech, and waited for the organisers to confirm that arrangement.
I would like to return to the project on my own terms, with a role I can agree to rather than the one others assume I want.
She returned to the choir on her own terms, attending rehearsals before deciding whether to take part in the concert.
They wanted to explore the town on their own terms, so they agreed which parts of the group programme were optional before booking.

advanced-native-1817.text: The long train ride became a conversation with myself about why I kept accepting work I no longer enjoyed; I wrote down two questions, without deciding the answer before I reached home.
Keeping the notebook became a conversation with myself about what I valued, rather than a list of answers I had to produce for someone else.
The solo walk became a conversation with herself about what she missed, without giving her an immediate plan.
He described the sketchbook as a conversation with himself, returning to one question through different drawings.

advanced-native-1818.text: Leaving the group chat alone for an hour gave me some inner space to notice what I wanted from the visit, instead of answering each suggestion before I had considered it.
I need a little inner space to think about the invitation before the conversation turns into a confirmed plan.
A few minutes with the window open gave her inner space to consider the question before replying.
He wanted inner space during the journey, so he left the first page of his notebook for questions rather than a finished plan.

advanced-native-1819.text: Our club trip has gone from being a yearly coach outing to something people can shape: members now suggest dates and choose a shared activity, although the budget still limits the options.
The event has gone from being a fixed annual programme to something people can shape by suggesting how they want to take part.
The festival has gone from being a single staged show to something people can shape through neighbourhood performances and workshops.
Our newsletter has gone from being a notice sheet to something people can shape by proposing questions for interviews.

advanced-native-1820.text: We were saving up for a small recording session, putting part of each club sale aside; by June we had enough for the room, but still needed to ask whether the engineer was available.
I am saving up for a short course, but I still need to check the dates before I make a booking.
She saved up for the workshop over several months, then checked that the final session did not clash with her exams.
They are saving up for a replacement projector and keeping the amount raised separate from the everyday club budget.

advanced-native-1821.text: When my cousin said on Thursday that she could host us that weekend, we arranged a last-minute trip, checking the train times before accepting rather than assuming we could leave whenever we liked.
We considered a last-minute trip after receiving the invitation, but waited until we had checked the journey home.
A last-minute trip became possible when a cancelled booking left room for us at my aunt’s house.
Do not leave the seating plan until the last minute; the ushers need it before rehearsal.

advanced-native-1822.text: It seemed that modern life follows us wherever we go: even at the lakeside cabin, work requests filled the morning chat, and we spent our first hour deciding what needed a reply.
Modern life tends to follow people wherever they go when their usual work messages remain part of each day.
Modern life follows us wherever we go, we joked, as the familiar committee reminder arrived just after we reached the island.
Modern life seemed to follow me wherever I went: even at my cousin’s kitchen table, the school committee kept asking me to approve the same notices.

advanced-native-1823.text: I had hoped for time together, but the holiday became a change of scenery with Wi-Fi: we kept the same work calls and ate separately beside our laptops, just with the sea outside the window.
I wanted a shared break, not just a change of scenery with Wi-Fi and the same work meetings at a different desk.
The new location could become a change of scenery with Wi-Fi if we simply move the entire working timetable there.
She called it a change of scenery with Wi-Fi after spending the first two days on the same reports she had hoped to leave behind.

advanced-native-1824.text: We had travelled far without fully arriving: although we were sitting beside the harbour, I kept planning Monday’s meeting and missed most of what my brother said about the boats.
It is possible to travel far without fully arriving when the task left at home still takes all of our attention.
They travelled far without fully arriving, discussing the next deadline throughout the walk they had once looked forward to.
I did not want to travel far without fully arriving, so I asked for an unhurried hour with my cousin instead of adding another stop.

advanced-native-1825.text: Since the arts centre linked us with online workshops, the world has opened up for our rural club: we can hear artists we could not previously reach, although live visits still depend on time and cost.
The world has opened up for us through these new connections, but I want to choose an opportunity we can give enough time to.
The world had opened up for her through the library’s new recordings, and she began asking which speaker she wanted to hear next.
The world may have opened up for the exchange students, but they still needed help choosing a project that fitted their stay.

advanced-native-697.text: Calling all newcomers beginners built invisible walls in the drama group: experienced newcomers stopped offering ideas after repeated dismissals without a hearing, so the chair proposed asking about each person’s experience.
We can build invisible walls through habits we have not questioned, so I want to ask who finds it hard to join the conversation.
Using unexplained jokes built invisible walls between the returning members and those attending for the first time.
The host asked whether the group’s habits were building invisible walls that a more open invitation could help address.

advanced-native-1176.text: My motivation dipped midway through sorting the archive, although I still cared about the stories; a short regular session helped me return to the next folder without pretending I felt excited every day.
My motivation dips sometimes, but I can explain what I still value and ask what arrangement would help me continue.
Her motivation dipped after the third draft, so she asked for time to decide which part still interested her.
When our motivation dips, we discuss what remains meaningful before agreeing another commitment.

advanced-native-1177.text: The new club project offered a clean slate: roles would be based on what people could offer now, rather than last term’s mistakes, but borrowed materials still had to be returned.
I would like a clean slate for this conversation, while still taking responsibility for what I need to put right.
The new tutor offered a clean slate and asked to read the revision before discussing last year’s mark.
She began the letter with a clean slate, choosing what she wanted to say now rather than repeating their old argument.

advanced-native-1178.text: We held ourselves accountable for the wrong labels by telling the curator which files we had used and correcting our entries; the missing donor information still needed checking with someone else.
I want to hold myself accountable for what I promise, while being honest about what I can and cannot control.
The editors held themselves accountable by naming the unchecked claim and telling readers when the correction would appear.
I hold myself accountable for asking before I use her photograph, so I will check the permission rather than assume it.

advanced-native-1179.text: After the first exhibition weekend, we took stock of visitor questions and the tasks volunteers had found difficult; we wanted to understand the pattern before choosing changes, not simply repeat the busiest session.
I want to take stock of what has happened before I promise what comes next.
She took stock of the questions still unanswered before sending the interviewer a new plan.
We are taking stock of the materials and time we can offer, so the next promise will be based on what is actually available.

advanced-native-1180.text: I had turned one comment about the opening into a stick to beat myself with, saying I could never write well; the editor had actually asked only for a clearer first scene, which gave me something specific to revise.
I do not want this to become a stick to beat myself with; I want to understand the specific change I can make.
She refused to make the missed rehearsal a stick to beat herself with and asked how she could prepare for the next one.
The old result had become a stick to beat himself with, until he began to name the skills he was still learning.

advanced-native-1181.text: Our final afternoon was a book launch and a farewell all rolled into one: we showed the stories we had made and thanked the tutor who was leaving, while different people handled reading, refreshments and packing.
This can be a record and a gift all rolled into one, if we explain both purposes rather than expect it to do everything.
The workshop was a lesson and a reunion all rolled into one, with time both to practise and to catch up.
Her annotated map was a route guide and a memory book all rolled into one, though she kept private addresses out of it.

advanced-native-1182.text: At the old hall, the faded banner and familiar song made it feel like a room full of shared memories; former pupils recalled different moments, while new guests listened without pretending they had been there.
It feels like a room full of shared memories, although each person brings a different part of the past.
The old kitchen became a room full of shared memories when the siblings compared the meals they remembered.
She described a room full of shared memories, then let each guest choose which story to tell.

advanced-native-1183.text: The audience burst into applause when the reader finished the last line, interrupting the chair’s next announcement; the judges had not yet given their decision, so the clapping was a reaction, not the result of the competition.
They burst into applause at the final line, while the speaker waited for the room to quieten.
The volunteers burst into applause when the repaired clock began to chime again.
A small group burst into applause at the farewell, and the host waited before reading the next name.

advanced-native-1184.text: Maya missed the reunion because she was tied up with work on Saturday; she sent a note asking about the photographs, but had not yet checked when she could meet us another day.
I am tied up with work this afternoon, but I can tell you when I will check my availability rather than promise a time I have not confirmed.
He was tied up with work until six, so he asked whether the discussion could wait rather than tell the group he would be there early.
I was tied up with work during the call, but her message helped me arrange a time to listen afterwards.

advanced-native-1185.text: We drifted apart over several months: messages became brief, and we stopped knowing the small details of each other’s days, although neither of us remembered a single argument that had ended the friendship.
We may have drifted apart, but I would like to ask how you are now rather than assume that everything must return to the old pattern.
The sisters drifted apart while their calls became shorter, then one asked whether they wanted to make time for a proper conversation.
They feared they might drift apart, so they discussed how to stay in touch without promising a call every night.

advanced-native-1186.text: At the reunion, we picked up old conversations about the stories we used to read, but stopped to ask what each person enjoyed now; the familiar topic helped us begin without assuming our tastes had stayed the same.
Could we pick up our old conversation when you have time, while making room for anything that has changed?
They picked up old conversations at the kitchen table, then asked which plans had changed since their last visit.
She wanted to pick up their old conversation about the ending, but first asked whether her partner was ready to return to it.

advanced-native-1187.text: After a few minutes together, the former choir members slipped back into a familiar rhythm of listening and answering each other; the new ending still needed discussion, even though the old pattern of working returned easily.
We slipped back into a familiar rhythm, then paused to ask which parts still suited us.
The partners slipped back into a familiar rhythm of drafting and questioning, but agreed to check what their new reader needed.
They slipped back into a familiar rhythm at breakfast, with room for the quieter morning one of them had requested.

advanced-native-1189.text: I felt torn between joining the choir’s extra rehearsal and keeping the evening I had promised my sister; I wanted to sing, but I also valued that time with her, so I asked about another practice slot before deciding.
I am torn between two things I value, so I want to explain both before deciding.
He felt torn between accepting the solo and leaving room for the family visit he had promised.
She was torn between the two endings, so she asked a reader what each one suggested before choosing.

advanced-native-1190.text: My head and my heart pulled me in different directions over the old desk: the smaller one would give us working space, but the old one held memories of writing with Dad; I had not decided what to keep.
My head and my heart are both part of this choice, and I want to explain what each concern means to me.
His head and his heart seemed to agree when he found a way to help that also fitted the time he could offer.
She named what her head and her heart each valued before asking whether a shorter visit might work.

advanced-native-1192.text: Before offering a second workshop, we wanted to think it through: the room was available, but we still had to ask who could prepare materials and whether the extra session would clash with the volunteers’ existing shifts.
I need to think it through, so I would like to ask about the parts that could affect other people before I agree.
She thought it through by comparing the two routes and asking who would be affected by the earlier departure.
We are thinking things through before accepting the role, including what support the new member would need.

advanced-native-1193.text: Accepting the first solo was a leap of faith for Lina: she had practised with the accompanist, but could not know how the audience would respond; she agreed to try without calling it a guaranteed success.
It is a leap of faith, but I want to know what I am trusting and what I can still check.
Starting the shared notebook was a leap of faith, though the members first agreed what would remain private.
She called the move a leap of faith and explained both the support she had found and the questions still open.

advanced-native-1194.text: I listened to both tutors, then made up my own mind about which workshop to join; I chose the smaller group because I wanted time to discuss a draft, not because either tutor had told me to follow a friend.
I would like to hear your reasons, then make up my own mind about the part that is mine to choose.
She made up her own mind after reading the options, then checked which arrangements still needed the group’s agreement.
He asked for advice to help him make up his own mind, not to hand over the choice entirely.

advanced-native-1195.text: A reader’s question became a turning point in my revision: before it, I kept changing adjectives; afterwards, I began asking whose viewpoint each scene followed, though the whole manuscript still needed work.
