It was a turning point, and I can explain what changed without claiming the whole story was finished.
Moving out became a valuable turning point when she began agreeing household responsibilities rather than waiting for others to decide.
The missing photograph was a turning point in the investigation, sending the narrator back to an account she had ignored.

advanced-native-1196.text: I can stand behind the revised route plan because we tested the first section with new visitors; I will explain that support to the committee while making clear that the gate opening still needs confirmation.
I can stand behind my choice while explaining its limits and listening to information that might change it.
She stood behind the correction because it named the checked date and openly explained the earlier mistake.
The partners stand behind the invitation they wrote, while asking guests which parts still need clarifying.

advanced-native-1197.text: Rehearsing the new scene was not plain sailing: a missing cue interrupted the first attempt, and the timing needed another try; after we marked the page together, the next run was clearer, though not every problem had gone.
It may not be plain sailing, but I want to understand the difficulties rather than assume that none of the work is worthwhile.
The first month was not plain sailing, but they learned which shared tasks needed a clearer agreement.
Finding the missing date was plain sailing once she had the correct register in front of her.

advanced-native-1251.text: Our interview drifted off course when we began comparing cameras instead of asking about the old cinema. I returned to the question about its first audience, because equipment was not the purpose of this conversation.
I think our discussion has gone off course; could we return to the question we agreed to answer?
The rehearsal went off course when the cast began debating a different play.
A disappointing review threw her off course for a week, but she returned to the chapter she wanted to finish.

advanced-native-1252.text: I felt out of my depth when the discussion turned from the play’s costumes to the sound desk. I could sew the jackets, but I had never operated that equipment, so I asked the technician to show me the controls.
I am out of my depth with this part of the project, so I would like someone experienced to guide me through it.
She knew the village’s history but felt out of her depth when asked to restore the damaged painting.
The new editor was out of his depth with the unfamiliar printing system and asked for a supervised practice session.

advanced-native-1253.text: Although I knew the music, I felt like a fish out of water at the choir’s first supper: everyone seemed to share stories I had never heard. One singer introduced me to her table, and I began to feel more at ease.
I felt like a fish out of water at first, but a simple introduction helped me join the conversation.
The experienced dancer felt like a fish out of water at a reception where she knew nobody.
He was a fish out of water during his first week at the club, until a member explained its routines.

advanced-native-1256.text: I kept second-guessing myself about the exhibition title, changing it after every conversation even when nobody had offered a new reason. My partner suggested returning to the purpose we had already agreed before making another change.
I keep second-guessing myself, so I want to separate a new reason to change from the return of the same doubt.
She second-guessed herself after choosing the final photograph, then checked it against the brief rather than changing it again.
They kept second-guessing themselves about the ending until they agreed what the scene needed to show.

advanced-native-1257.text: The two dates on the rehearsal sheet tripped me up: I copied the costume fitting time into my calendar instead of the performance time. The labels looked alike, so I asked the organiser to separate the headings.
The similar wording tripped me up, so I would like to check which instruction applies before trying again.
The unfamiliar abbreviation tripped her up, so she asked what it stood for.
A small change in the diagram can trip people up if the old labels are left in place.

advanced-native-1258.text: We ran into practical problems with the outdoor reading: the benches were fixed too far from the power point for the microphone lead. The poems were ready, but we needed to agree on a different arrangement for the audience.
We have run into practical problems with the setup, so I would like to agree on an alternative before inviting people in.
They ran into practical problems when the display stand would not fit through the doorway.
We may run into practical problems with the room layout, so let us measure the tables before confirming the plan.

advanced-native-1259.text: The editing program came with a learning curve: I could cut a clip, but matching the sound took several practice sessions. The tutor helped me compare two versions rather than expect me to remember every control after one demonstration.
This comes with a learning curve, so I would like time to practise the unfamiliar parts with someone who can answer questions.
Using the new archive came with a learning curve, but the practice search helped her find the right records.
The role comes with a learning curve, so the outgoing editor offered a supervised first issue.

advanced-native-1261.text: The gap between expectation and reality became clear at the workshop: I had pictured silent drawing, but the advertised plan involved sharing sketches in pairs. I had skimmed the description and missed that part.
I want to explain the gap between expectation and reality by saying what I assumed and what actually happened.
The gap between expectation and reality was smaller once the invitation clearly explained the format.
Her account of the gap between expectation and reality compared her imagined studio with the shared space she actually joined.

advanced-native-1262.text: Our plan for a short local-history booklet grew arms and legs: first came an exhibition, then a recorded tour and a launch concert. Each idea was interesting, but we had not agreed who would do the extra work.
The plan has grown arms and legs, so I would like to agree which additions we can actually support.
A simple class survey grew arms and legs when three groups requested separate reports.
The reunion plan was growing arms and legs, so they listed the original aim before agreeing to more events.

advanced-native-1263.text: The bill can climb if we add colour pages to every copy, the printer explained. Our current quote was for black-and-white pages only, so I asked for a revised total before agreeing to the change.
The bill could climb with these additions, so I want to check the full amount before we confirm anything.
The bill climbed after they added delivery and a second display board.
The bill can climb when optional extras are included, so she asked which items the quote covered.

advanced-native-1264.text: We went all out for the final reading, rehearsing the transitions and making individual invitations. The room was simple, but we wanted each guest to feel expected; spending more on decorations was not our priority.
I want to go all out on the preparation while keeping the promises I can realistically make.
The cousins went all out to prepare a recorded greeting in the language their grandmother missed hearing.
She went all out on the first draft, then asked readers which parts still needed work.

advanced-native-1265.text: For once, Mina splashed out on a hand-bound sketchbook instead of her usual plain pad. She had chosen it as a personal treat after finishing the illustrations, not because the old pad had become unusable.
I do not usually splash out on stationery, but this book felt like a special way to mark the finished project.
He splashed out on a first edition after reading the same novel from the library for years.
They decided not to splash out on the party and spent the afternoon making personal greetings instead.

advanced-native-1266.text: The price tag on the folding table was lower, but it could not hold the display boards. We compared the size and strength as well as the cost, rather than choosing the cheaper table before checking what it had to support.
I would like to compare the price tag with what we actually need, rather than treat the cost as the whole decision.
The price tag caught her attention, but the missing parts changed her decision about the second-hand desk.
He asked about the price tag before ordering, then checked whether the book included the drawings he wanted.

advanced-native-1267.text: When my name was misspelled on the draft programme, I asked for a correction without making a big song and dance about it. The organiser fixed the file before printing, so there was no need for a public complaint.
I want the mistake corrected, but I do not need to make a big song and dance about it if we can resolve it calmly.
She corrected the invitation without making a song and dance about it in front of the guests.
He made a big song and dance about the small delay, then apologised when he learned the revised arrival time had already been sent.

advanced-native-1268.text: The custom frame would cost an arm and a leg, so I asked whether the drawing could fit a standard one. I still wanted to protect it, but had not agreed to the custom order.
It would cost an arm and a leg, so I would like to compare the alternatives before committing.
The rare printing would cost an arm and a leg, so the student asked to consult the library copy.
She found a suitable second-hand cabinet that did not cost an arm and a leg.

advanced-native-1269.text: After labelling the first three boxes, we called it a day and left a note about the fourth for tomorrow. The labels were checked, but the archive was not finished; stopping that evening was part of the plan.
Let us call it a day and write down what we need to return to tomorrow.
They called it a day after the second rehearsal and agreed to review the recording in the morning.
She called it a day on the draft, leaving herself a note about the unfinished ending.

advanced-native-1270.text: Three paragraphs is a guide, not a hard-and-fast rule, our editor said. A clear two-paragraph letter was acceptable, but naming the source of a quotation remained a requirement.
I understand that this is a guide rather than a hard-and-fast rule; could you tell me which requirements still apply?
There is no hard-and-fast rule about the number of sketches, but each submission needs the artist’s name.
He treated the suggested order as a hard-and-fast rule until the organiser explained that participants could choose.

advanced-native-1271.text: The team pulled out all the stops for the visiting storyteller: they found a quiet room, checked the recording setup and gathered readers’ questions. They could arrange a welcome, but not predict every response.
We can pull out all the stops in our preparation while being honest that we cannot guarantee the outcome.
The volunteers pulled out all the stops to find a venue that the whole group could enter comfortably.
She pulled out all the stops for the recording, then listened to the editor’s suggestions about the final cut.

advanced-native-1272.text: Joining the live radio team felt like stepping into the unknown. I knew the books we would discuss, but had never answered callers on air; rehearsing the opening helped without telling me what every caller would ask.
I am stepping into the unknown, but I can recognise what I have prepared without pretending to know the outcome.
He stepped into the unknown when he began interviewing people outside the familiar school group.
They were stepping into the unknown together, with a plan for the first week but no certainty about the year ahead.

advanced-native-1274.text: As the only person who chose the photographs, I had no one to hide behind when a reader questioned the selection. I could explain my reasons and ask for advice, but I could not say that a committee had made the decision.
I have no one to hide behind for that decision, so I want to explain what I chose and how I will check it.
With no one to hide behind, she explained why she had rejected the final chapter.
He had no one to hide behind for the invitation he sent, but a friend helped him write an honest correction.

advanced-native-1275.text: We planned three questions for the museum walk, then adapted as we went when the children noticed details we had overlooked. Their questions changed the examples we used, while the aim remained learning to describe what they could see.
We can adapt as we go, using what people tell us while keeping the purpose of the activity clear.
The facilitators adapted as they went, changing the examples when participants asked more specific questions.
We can adapt as we go without forgetting the conditions we agreed before starting.

advanced-native-1826.text: I had packed six activities into two days, leaving no time for the conversation I most wanted with my aunt; by the second evening, I wished I had chosen fewer stops.
We are packing too many activities into three days if nobody has time to finish the project the visit is meant to support.
The organisers packed eight activities into three days, then realised that participants needed time between them to travel and compare their notes.
She did not want to pack several activities into a few days just to fill the brochure; she asked what visitors actually hoped to do.

advanced-native-1828.text: I chose somewhere that fits me rather than the farthest destination: the small town had a library, short walks and time to read, which was what I wanted after the busy term.
I am looking for somewhere that fits me at this point, with time to read rather than a timetable I have to rush through.
She wanted somewhere that fits her, so she compared the reading spaces rather than count the attractions on each brochure.
We agreed to ask what each person needed before choosing somewhere that fits us for the shared weekend.

advanced-native-1829.text: After the festival’s long final day, I felt wrung out and left the messages until morning; I had loved the performances, but I did not have the energy for another late conversation.
I feel wrung out after today, so I would like to rest before deciding whether I can help with another session.
She felt wrung out after answering questions all afternoon and asked to read the remaining notes the next day.
He was wrung out by the time the visitors left, although he was pleased that the long-planned gathering had happened.

advanced-native-1830.text: At the local storytelling workshop, I stepped out of my usual bubble by listening to parents whose school experiences differed from mine; I began to question what I had assumed everyone found easy.
I want to step out of my usual bubble by listening to an account that challenges what I have taken for granted.
She stepped out of her usual bubble when she asked the evening staff how they experienced the same building after visitors left.
The exchange project pulled people out of their usual bubble by pairing neighbours from different streets.

advanced-native-1832.text: I came home from the garden visit with a fuller mind: the growers had shown how weather, time and family routines affected their choices, leaving me with more thoughtful questions about the food we buy.
I returned with a fuller mind, able to see more connections even though I still had questions to explore.
The exchange left him with a fuller mind about the town, because he could now connect the buildings with people’s memories of using them.
She hoped to return with a fuller mind, carrying a few carefully considered questions rather than a bag of unexamined brochures.

advanced-native-1835.text: We asked whether we wanted a change of world or simply a change of pace; this time, an unhurried weekend in our own town mattered more to us than an unfamiliar destination.
I want to ask whether I need a change of world or a change of pace before choosing where to spend the break.
She asked for a change of world or a change of pace, then realised she first needed a week without the usual early meetings.
The letter asked whether its writer wanted a change of world or a change of pace after hearing two friends’ very different summer plans.

advanced-native-1836.text: After the third booking problem, the weekend stopped feeling like a break and started feeling like a test: I spent each evening solving the next day’s arrangements instead of resting.
The afternoon stopped feeling like a break and started feeling like a test when every game became another performance to be judged.
The walk stopped feeling like a break and started feeling like a test when we kept checking whether we had beaten yesterday’s time.
For her, the visit stopped feeling like a break and started feeling like a test after each meal brought another argument to manage.

advanced-native-1839.text: The cancelled boat ride took the shine off the trip because it was the outing I had most looked forward to, though the evening meal with our cousins was still a highlight.
I worry that leaving the argument unresolved could take the shine off the trip, so I would like us to talk before we go.
The long wait took the shine off the trip for him, although he still enjoyed seeing his old school friend.
Lin had looked forward to the exhibit opening. A last-minute room change took the shine off it, though she still enjoyed the art.

advanced-native-1840.text: There was a slow build-up of discomfort during the shared stay: at first I missed one familiar meal, then I began avoiding the noisy evenings, without yet knowing how to explain what felt wrong.
The diary suggests a slow build-up of discomfort, but I would like to understand the separate moments before naming a cause.
The letters reveal a slow build-up of discomfort as the writer becomes less willing to discuss the shared plans.
She noticed a slow build-up of discomfort over the rehearsals and asked for time to describe what was changing for her.

advanced-native-1841.text: The unanswered question about our friend’s absence cast a shadow over the whole experience; even during the lively reunion, we kept wondering why nobody had heard from her.
The unresolved disagreement could cast a shadow over the whole experience if we leave it unspoken before the event.
The unexplained change in the agreement cast a shadow over the whole experience, even though the visitors praised the finished display.
She feared that leaving the apology unheard would cast a shadow over the whole experience of returning to the club.

advanced-native-1842.text: Our life has outgrown this space in one important way: the table we once used only for dinner now has to hold two people’s work throughout the day, leaving nowhere to eat together.
Our life has outgrown this space, so I would like us to describe the competing needs before deciding what to change.
Our life has outgrown this space since the evening lessons and family meals began needing the same room at the same time.
I wrote that our life has outgrown the space now used for both the twins’ drawing lessons and their grandmother’s afternoon rest.

advanced-native-1843.text: The flat once felt like a nest, with our books beside the lamp and room for two quiet evenings a week; I still loved those memories, even as the new working hours changed how we used it.
The old room once felt like a nest to me, and I want to describe the small routines that made it comforting.
The tiny kitchen once felt like a nest during winter evenings when everyone brought a story to the table.
The room once felt like a nest, though she could remember the narrow doorway as clearly as the welcome inside.

advanced-native-1844.text: After the cancelled project, we were ready to turn the page by planning a smaller event, while still sending the promised explanation to the people who had helped with the first one.
I am ready to turn the page, while keeping the lessons and responsibilities that still belong to me.
She turned the page after the rejected application and began preparing a different proposal, using the feedback she had received.
We hoped to turn the page on the disagreement by listening to the explanation rather than pretending it had never happened.

advanced-native-1845.text: When the recording file was lost, we had to start over with the interview, but the questions and notes from the first conversation helped us prepare a clearer second session.
Before we start over, I would like to identify which part needs rebuilding and which earlier work we can still use.
They started over with a new outline after discovering that the interviews did not support the original question.
Starting over at the new workshop felt less daunting once she found a role that used the skills from her earlier team.

advanced-native-1847.text: The argument sounded as if it was about chairs, but at bottom it was about whether newcomers could join the discussion without asking for special permission each time.
At bottom, I want people to understand the choice they are being asked to make, not simply sign the form quickly.
The disagreement was, at bottom, about who had been included in the decision rather than the colour of the notice.
At bottom, she wanted a chance to explain her work in her own words before others summarised it for her.

advanced-native-1848.text: My first week at the workshop felt like starting a chapter with the map missing: I knew the tools, but not who approved the orders or where the shared materials were recorded.
It feels like starting a chapter with the map missing, so I want to ask which local procedures I need to learn first.
The new role felt like starting a chapter with the map missing until she learned where questions about the rota should go.
For us, joining the shared studio was like starting a chapter with the map missing: the tools were familiar, but the booking rules were not.

advanced-native-1849.text: We worked out a fair rota by comparing the hours each helper could actually offer; the first draft was agreed, but we still needed to check whether the room was available for those sessions.
We need to decide whether the plan still fits; we can work that out after checking which detail is missing.
They worked out why the two totals differed after noticing that one list included visitors and the other counted members only.
She asked us to work out a possible route through the exhibition before deciding where the first explanation should go.

advanced-native-1850.text: For us, everyday life became harder before it became easier after the move: the new opening hours first disrupted our errands, then a shared list helped us plan them without repeated wasted journeys.
Everyday life may become harder before it becomes easier with a new routine, but I still want to ask for the help I need now.
Everyday life became harder before it became easier when we changed schools; a clear list of the new bus times eventually made the mornings less rushed.
In her account, everyday life became harder before it became easier after the new timetable, as she gradually found a way to combine lessons and family meals.

advanced-native-847.text: During dinner, they were glued to their screens, following the match so closely that they missed most of the conversation around the table.
We were glued to our screens, so I would like us to make some room for conversation too.
They were glued to their screens as the final results appeared.
During the meeting, each guest was glued to a different screen instead of joining the discussion.

advanced-native-1199.text: Curiosity nearly got the better of me when I noticed the sealed letter, but I put it back unopened and asked its owner whether there was anything they wanted to share.
Anger nearly got the better of me, but I paused long enough to choose a reply that addressed the problem without attacking my friend.
Impatience got the better of him, and he interrupted before his partner could explain the missing page.
Her excitement almost got the better of her, but she checked whether the news was hers to announce before speaking.

advanced-native-1200.text: I knew the museum introduction so well that I could say it in my sleep, but a visitor’s question about one family’s missing photograph still made me stop and check the catalogue.
I could say it in my sleep after so many rehearsals, but I still wanted to notice whether the listener needed a pause or a clearer explanation.
He had given the welcome so often that he could say it in his sleep, yet he changed the final invitation when the new group needed more time.
She could say it in her sleep after years of telling the same family story, but her grandchild’s question led her to add a detail she had never included before.

advanced-native-1276.text: Translating a fresh paragraph without the completed example stripped away the training wheels. I had to choose the wording myself, although I could still ask the tutor about a sentence I could not untangle.
Removing the completed example can strip away the training wheels while leaving room for specific questions.
The independent interview stripped away the training wheels of the prepared question sheet.
The final exercise strips away the training wheels, but the teacher still reviews the choices afterwards.

advanced-native-1278.text: I signed up for the Saturday pottery session and received a confirmation email. The class has not happened yet; I am checking what to bring, rather than describing something I have already made.
I have signed up for the workshop, but I still need to check the time and what to bring.
She signed up for the choir workshop after checking that it fitted around her evening shift.
We can sign up for the tour now and ask about the meeting point before we travel.

advanced-native-1279.text: The interview was awkward, and I came out of it tired but clearer about the work I did not want. I had not received an offer; understanding my preferences was the result I could honestly describe.
I came out of it with a clearer preference, although parts of the experience were uncomfortable.
The group came out of it disappointed by the low turnout but grateful for the conversations that did happen.
She came out of it with two useful questions and a stronger wish to try a different subject.

advanced-native-1281.text: I am finding my own footing in the new bookshop: I can arrange a display and explain my choices, even when they differ from the old assistant’s. I still ask the manager about unfamiliar orders.
I am finding my own footing, and asking a specific question can be part of working more independently.
He found his own footing in the workshop once he began explaining why he preferred one material to another.
She is finding her footing as a host while still asking the producer for feedback after each programme.

advanced-native-1282.text: Our neighbourhood advice programme lives or dies by callers being able to explain their questions. Clear sound matters, but a polished opening is little use if the host interrupts before anyone can finish.
The project lives or dies by useful participation, so we should check what people need before promising a launch date.
The weekly exchange lives or dies by members bringing things that others can actually use.
Our reading circle lives or dies by people feeling able to ask about passages they do not understand.

advanced-native-1283.text: The retreat looked expensive on paper: the room and meal charges were both high. When we visited, the manager listened carefully to our needs; that welcome mattered, but it did not change the figures in the quote.
It looks expensive on paper, but I want to distinguish the quoted cost from what we still need to learn about the experience.
The studio looked expensive on paper, so we asked what the quoted hire fee included before booking.
The package was expensive on paper, while the visit helped us understand why some families still preferred it.

advanced-native-1284.text: Money can buy the setting, but the reunion still needs a way for new partners to join the conversation. We hired a comfortable room, then asked each family to bring a story rather than expect the decorations to introduce everyone.
Money can buy the setting, but we should also ask what will help these particular guests feel able to join in.
Money can buy the setting, but we asked the guest of honour what kind of evening she actually wanted.
Money can buy the setting, while a thoughtful invitation can explain how a first-time guest might take part.

advanced-native-1287.text: The concert tickets would not break the bank, but the last train left before the encore. I asked about an earlier performance so the evening would fit both my spending limit and the journey home.
We can choose something that will not break the bank without assuming everyone wants to spend the same amount.
The picnic would not break the bank, but they still asked each guest what they were happy to bring.
The custom cover would break the bank for me, so I asked whether a plain one could protect the same pages.

advanced-native-1290.text: During the festival, our new neighbours mostly kept to themselves, taking a quiet walk after dinner. They greeted us at the gate and said they enjoyed the lights, but preferred not to join the crowded games.
She tends to keep to herself, so I would ask what kind of contact she prefers rather than guess how she feels about us.
He kept to himself during the break, then joined the discussion when he felt ready.
They prefer to keep to themselves on holiday while still exchanging a friendly greeting with the people next door.

advanced-native-1291.text: As relatives began singing by the open door, the celebration spilled out of the home and into the shared courtyard. Two neighbours joined the chorus, while other residents continued their own evening upstairs.
The festive mood spilled out of the home, but I would name the people who actually joined rather than speak for the whole street.
The excitement spilled out of the home when the children showed their new puppets to people passing the gate.
The celebration was spilling out of the home into the lane, where a few neighbours stopped to listen.

advanced-native-1293.text: We listed three quiet places to gather with family or friends over the holiday. The map offered possibilities, not confirmed meetings; each group still needed to decide who wanted to come and when.
We could gather with family or friends, but I would like everyone to choose the company and timing that suit them.
They gathered with family or friends in small groups, with each group choosing a time that suited its members.
The hall offered a place to gather with family or friends, though some residents preferred a quiet evening at home.

advanced-native-1294.text: Around the dinner table, we compared two ideas for the family visit. My aunt explained why she preferred the shorter trip, but we left the date undecided until everyone had checked their time off.
We can talk around the dinner table without treating every suggestion as a promise that has already been agreed.
Stories passed around the dinner table, though the cousins remembered the same holiday differently.
She asked about the new rota around the dinner table, then waited for her flatmates to check their calendars.

advanced-native-1296.text: My cousin became an emotional anchor during the move: she listened when plans changed and helped me name one thing I could do next. She did not choose the new flat for me or pretend I would never feel uncertain.
You have been an emotional anchor for me, and I want to thank you without assuming you are always available.
The regular conversation became an emotional anchor, giving her space to explain a worry before choosing what to do.
He called his aunt an emotional anchor because she could listen without demanding that he hide every doubt.

advanced-native-1298.text: Support works both ways in our family: Dad helps me practise recipes, and I help him organise the photographs he wants to share. We offer different skills, rather than count the minutes to see who owes the next favour.
Support can work both ways without becoming a demand for an identical favour at the same moment.
The agreement worked both ways: each neighbour asked before borrowing, and each could say when an item was needed back.
Their care works both ways, with one offering company and the other sharing a skill when time allows.

advanced-native-1301.text: Jo moved out of her parents’ flat when she rented a room near college. They still meet for dinner on Sundays; the change shortened her journey, rather than ending her contact with the family.
I plan to move out at the end of the month; could we agree when I should return the keys?
She moved out of the shared house after finding a flat closer to work.
We agreed to photograph the empty room before I moved out, so we had a record of its condition.

advanced-native-1851.text: Taking the job in another town meant leaving familiar people behind, especially the neighbours I saw each morning; I still wanted to call them, but knew the everyday encounters would change.
Leaving familiar people behind does not mean I want to end the relationships, but I know the ordinary ways we meet will change.
She was leaving familiar people behind when she moved for the course, so she asked which weekly conversations they wanted to keep.
They left familiar people behind in the old village, but the shared recipe book gave them something to discuss on later calls.

advanced-native-1852.text: I missed the quiet comfort of the shopkeeper greeting me by name each morning; the new street was pleasant, but those small recognitions were not part of my day yet.
There is quiet comfort in a familiar greeting, even when the rest of the day still holds things I need to learn.
She found quiet comfort in the familiar sound of her uncle making tea while she worked on the difficult letter.
The old recipe offered quiet comfort on the first evening, even though the new kitchen still felt unfamiliar.

advanced-native-1853.text: The boxes were easy to arrange, but the emotional gap after a move surprised me: I no longer had the evening walk with my old neighbour, and had not yet found someone to share those ordinary stories with.
I want to describe the emotional gap after a move without suggesting that I regret every part of the choice.
The emotional gap after a move became clear when she reached for the phone to share the day’s news with a neighbour who no longer lived next door.
He wrote about the move and the emotional gap that comes after it, especially the missing afternoon conversations in the shared garden.

advanced-native-1854.text: Through years of helping at the garden and asking neighbours about their stories, we built deep roots in the area; people began coming to us with ideas, not just recognising our address.
I hope to build deep roots here by taking part consistently, rather than expecting one visit to make every connection.
She built deep roots in the town through years of sharing the library work with people from different streets.
They were building deep roots as neighbours began sharing not only requests for help but ideas for the next community event.

advanced-native-1856.text: The neighbourhood gave me roots, rhythm, and a stronger sense of home through the people I met at the garden, the Saturday market routine and the feeling that someone noticed when I returned.
I want roots, rhythm, and a stronger sense of home, but I know those feelings need time and real relationships rather than an address alone.
The evening choir gave her roots, rhythm, and a stronger sense of home as familiar voices became part of each week.
He found roots, rhythm, and a stronger sense of home in shared breakfasts and the neighbours who began asking how his work was going.

advanced-native-1857.text: Our neighbourhood routines once helped people feel secure, but roots can sometimes turn into ruts if we stop asking whether the meeting times still suit those who work late.
Roots can sometimes turn into ruts when we treat a useful old arrangement as a reason never to hear new questions.
The club secretary warned that roots can sometimes turn into ruts when a long-standing rule prevents new members from suggesting an activity.
Their shared history was valuable, but roots can sometimes turn into ruts if the committee mistakes familiarity for evidence that a plan still works.

advanced-native-1858.text: Joining the student journal did not stop Lea calling her family on Sundays; she wanted strong roots without becoming afraid to branch out into interests they had not shared before.
Our group wants strong roots without becoming afraid to branch out, so the new collaboration will begin with local stories and invite other ways of telling them.
Her weekly visits to the old neighbourhood helped her keep strong roots without becoming afraid to branch out into work in a different city.
The choir encouraged strong roots without becoming afraid to branch out, keeping its shared songs while inviting members to introduce music they had discovered elsewhere.

advanced-native-1860.text: Moving nearer the evening college felt like a fresh page rather than just a new address: I could finally begin the course I had postponed, while keeping the friendships that mattered to me.
The move could be a fresh page rather than just a new address, but I want to decide which plans to begin and which connections to keep.
The new placement gave her a fresh page rather than just a new address when it allowed her to return to the design work she had missed.
He hoped for a fresh page rather than just a new address, so he named the evening classes he wanted to make time for.

advanced-native-1861.text: The workshop group had planned around a promised room, so cancelling it without warning pulled the rug out from under them just before rehearsals; they now had to find another place.
Withdrawing the agreed editing help without telling my partner pulled the rug out from under her when she was preparing the final version.
The unexpected loss of the agreed transport pulled the rug out from under us on the morning of the exhibition.
Closing the only evening clinic without notice would pull the rug out from under local people.

advanced-native-1862.text: After three borrowed rooms in one month, we felt as if we were living out of a suitcase; I kept the work notebook packed because I never knew where I would have space to use it next.
I have been living out of a suitcase between short assignments, so I would welcome a week in one place to organise an ordinary routine.
They were living out of a suitcase between festival jobs, finding a different kitchen and bus route every few days.
She had lived out of a suitcase during the recording tour and was glad to leave her notes on one desk again.

advanced-native-1863.text: The first month of the touring job felt exciting, but the excitement began to wear thin as each evening became another hurried check-in, and I missed having time to talk to people.
The novelty has worn thin, but I would like to discuss a different schedule before deciding whether to leave the project.
The joke wore thin after the host repeated it between every performance, and the audience became less responsive.
Her patience was wearing thin after several unanswered messages about the missing equipment.

advanced-native-1864.text: After several temporary placements, the couple wanted to put down roots in the town, joining ordinary weekly activities and making plans that did not depend on leaving again next month.
We are thinking about putting down roots here, so we would like to know which local activities we could join regularly.
She began to put down roots by joining the weekly repair group and getting to know the people on her street.
They were putting down roots in the village, but still wanted to visit the friends they had left in the city.

advanced-native-1865.text: In the story, Maya felt at the mercy of rent increases because she could not predict what the next renewal would cost; she wanted clearer information before choosing how long to stay.
They felt at the mercy of rent increases, so their first request was for clear information about the proposed renewal.
The tenants in the play felt at the mercy of rent increases when no one could tell them what the next agreement would cost.
Her character describes feeling at the mercy of rent increases while waiting for the renewal proposal, rather than claiming she already knows its terms.

advanced-native-1866.text: To the character, each rent payment felt like money disappearing into someone else’s pocket because she was not building an asset, though she acknowledged that it paid for the place she was living in.
The payment felt like money disappearing into someone else’s pocket to him, but that was his frustration, not a full comparison of the available arrangements.
In his letter, the annual fee felt like money disappearing into someone else’s pocket when he thought only about ownership, not the shared studio access it provided.
She used money disappearing into someone else’s pocket to describe her frustration with the payments, then listed the services they actually covered.

advanced-native-1868.text: The short placement let me keep my feet light while I learned which kind of archive work suited me; I still had agreed hours to complete before deciding where to apply next.
I would like to keep my feet light for the next few months, so I am choosing a short project with a clear finish and handover.
A three-week exhibition project helped her keep her feet light while she waited to learn where the next course would take place.
They wanted to keep their feet light, so they agreed a short trial and a review date before considering a longer partnership.

advanced-native-1869.text: We did not want to have all our eggs in one basket, so alongside the main interview request we asked a different archive about written accounts; either source might still say no.
We do not want to have all our eggs in one basket, so we will prepare another route while continuing to work carefully on the first plan.
The editor did not want to have all her eggs in one basket, so she sought permission for a second image while waiting for the first photographer’s reply.
By booking three venues, the theatre avoids putting all its eggs in one basket.

advanced-native-1870.text: I asked when the application decision was needed because I wanted to keep my options open until I had seen the other course timetable; I had not accepted either place yet.
I would like to keep my options open until Friday; please tell me if you need a firm answer before then.
She kept her options open by asking about both interview dates before accepting either invitation.
We are keeping our options open until the room measurements arrive, but have told the designer when we will choose a layout.

advanced-native-1871.text: A year-long duty at the same workshop would tie me down when I am still waiting to hear where the field placement will be; I want to discuss a shorter role before agreeing.
The fixed weekly visits could tie us down during the research trip, so we need to agree how the responsibility would be shared.
The daily collection duty would tie him down to one location during a period when his work often took him elsewhere.
She asked whether the partnership would tie her down to fixed weekends before agreeing to help with the travelling exhibition.

advanced-native-1872.text: For the exhibition opening, I had to juggle three things at once: answering the guests, checking the captions and helping the volunteers find their stations; each needed attention during the same hour.
I need to juggle three things at once this week, so could we agree which part of the preparation you can take over?
The coordinator had to juggle three things at once when the speakers arrived, the slides stopped working and the welcome desk needed instructions.
During the gallery move, Priya was juggling work and family duties, so she asked for help with packing.

advanced-native-1873.text: We have one afternoon for three long interviews and checking the recording, so something has to give; we need to shorten the interviews or add another session rather than promise it will all fit.
Something has to give if we want both careful checking and an earlier finish, so we should agree which task can move to tomorrow.
With a fixed rehearsal end time and two extra scenes, something has to give, so the cast is comparing possible cuts before the next meeting.
The editor said something has to give when the full interview and large photographs would not fit on the agreed pages.

advanced-native-1874.text: The fee for the larger exhibition stand was eye-watering compared with our small group’s event budget, so we asked what a simpler display would cost before choosing.
The full installation has an eye-watering price for our small project, so could we see a quote for a simpler version?
The custom case had an eye-watering price beside the standard one, so the curator asked which features accounted for the difference.
She described the festival’s late booking fee as eye-watering, then gave the actual figure so readers could judge it for themselves.

advanced-native-1875.text: Of the three teams, the evening crew had the least room to manoeuvre because its transport ended at ten, while the others could change their finishing times more easily.
The volunteers with the least room to manoeuvre over travel times should be asked about workable alternatives before we fix the end of the event.
Of the applicants, those relying on a single daily bus had the least room to manoeuvre when the interview time changed.
An extra guide on call gives the museum team room to manoeuvre if a scheduled guide falls ill.

advanced-native-1877.text: For this voluntary move, I wanted to discuss my cooking routine and how I would manage shared bills, rather than decide only by a number on the calendar; my birthday did not answer those questions.
A number on the calendar tells you my age, but I would also like to discuss the experience I have and the support I still need.
For the optional speaking role, a number on the calendar mattered less to the group than her preparation and wish to take part.
He did not want a number on the calendar to decide the conversation about independence before anyone had asked about his actual routines.

advanced-native-1880.text: The unfurnished room felt like a blank canvas for the flatmates, but they still had to agree how to use the shared wall and keep a clear route to the kitchen.
The new story setting is a blank canvas, but we have agreed to keep the two central characters and build the world around them.
The first issue was a blank canvas for the new editorial team, within the agreed theme and page limit.
They treated the unused courtyard as a blank canvas, then asked the neighbours which everyday uses the design should support.

advanced-native-1883.text: The newsletter began as a page of notices, then took on a life of its own as members sent stories and began answering one another; the editor had not planned that continuing conversation.
The story took on a life of its own when readers began exchanging interpretations that I had never considered while writing it.
The classroom question took on a life of its own as students began interviewing relatives and comparing the answers outside the lesson.
Their shared reading list has taken on a life of its own, with members organising discussions the founders never scheduled.

advanced-native-1884.text: We hung the photos up in the hall after choosing them together, so visitors could see the family history rather than find the pictures only in a folder.
We can hang the photos up after we agree the order, with enough space beside each one for its caption.
They hung the photos up beside the interview extracts so visitors could connect the faces with the stories.
We are hanging the photos up in the order agreed by the group, with a short caption beneath each picture.

advanced-native-1885.text: As neighbours began leaving notes and sharing tea at the new centre, the whole place began to soften; the furniture had hardly changed, but the conversations made it feel less impersonal to me.
The whole place is beginning to soften as familiar conversations become part of its ordinary afternoons.
The whole place began to soften when the shared noticeboard filled with thanks, invitations and familiar names.
The whole place is beginning to soften for him as the evening meal becomes a time for neighbours to exchange stories.

advanced-native-1887.text: Launching a public magazine before we had tested one issue felt like trying to leap three steps at once; we needed to check the editing process and what readers found useful first.
It feels like trying to leap three steps at once, so could we test the smallest workable version before promising the full service?
Offering a daily programme after one trial afternoon felt like trying to leap three steps at once without knowing the staffing needs.
She thought accepting the full translation project would mean trying to leap three steps at once, so she proposed testing one section with readers first.

advanced-native-1299.text: Hearing how Grandma had begun her first shop gave me a sense of identity. Her stories helped me understand why repairing things mattered in our family, without deciding that I had to open a shop of my own.
A sense of identity can grow from several parts of my life without requiring them all to stay the same.
The workshop gave her a sense of identity as a maker, not simply as someone who bought finished objects.
His sense of identity changed as he began to value the patient work he had once dismissed.

advanced-native-1300.text: Although we now lived in different towns, the bond was still there: she remembered my difficult first week and asked what had become easier. We spoke less often, but the conversation still felt attentive on both sides.
The bond is still there, but we can recognise it without asking every part of the relationship to stay unchanged.
The bond is still there, even while the sisters discuss a different way to share the work.
He felt the bond was still there when his old friend asked about a small detail from their last conversation.

advanced-native-1305.text: Mina carried the whole burden of organising the reading event: she booked the room, contacted every reader and dealt with changes herself. The other members arrived to watch, but had not taken on any of the preparation.
She did a great deal, but she did not carry the whole burden; we should also acknowledge the work done by the others.
She carried the whole burden of the booking after the other organiser withdrew.
He carried the whole burden for the first week, then agreed a division of duties with the team.

advanced-native-1876.text: When one district has an evening library and the other closes before workers return, the gap can be quite stark in access after work, even if the buildings look equally impressive.
The gap can be quite stark when we compare who can use the service after work, rather than just the number of hours on the poster.
The gap can be quite stark between the advertised journey time and the time a passenger needs when the connecting bus runs only twice a day.
The gap can be quite stark in usable workspace, even when two rooms have similar floor areas but very different layouts.

advanced-native-1878.text: Planning her own bus journey gave the family a sense of forward movement towards greater independence, even though they still needed to practise what to do if the connection was missed.
The first test gave us a sense of forward movement, because we learned which part failed and what to try next.
The clearer list of unanswered questions gave the researcher a sense of forward movement towards a more focused interview.
A sense of forward movement came when the group agreed its first shared task, though the wider partnership was still being discussed.

advanced-native-1882.text: For me, the kitchen is where I exhale after a demanding day, because I can admit that something went badly without having to sound confident; the problem may still need attention tomorrow.
The workshop is where I exhale for a while, because I can show an unfinished piece without pretending that I know the next step.
The small reading group is where I exhale, because an uncertain question is welcome there instead of being treated as a failure.
For us, the evening walk is where we exhale and talk honestly about the day before deciding what still needs doing.

advanced-native-1886.text: For the housemates, cooking the first shared meal helped turn the house into a home; the rented rooms were still simple, but they now had a memory and a routine they wanted to continue.
The objects matter to us because of their stories, but it is our shared routines that help turn the house into a home.
The weekly cooking rota helped turn the house into a home as the new flatmates learned what each person enjoyed.
She said the familiar notes on the fridge helped turn the house into a home more than the expensive fittings had.

advanced-native-1888.text: Borrowing the spare recorder bought us time to arrange a repair, but it did not fix our damaged one; we still needed to decide how the next interviews would be recorded.
A short extension would buy us time to check the figures, but we should explain what we can finish before the new deadline.
The organisers put up a temporary sign that bought them time to replace the damaged display without leaving visitors unsure where to go.
The editor asked for one extra day to buy time for a source check before approving the disputed quotation.

advanced-native-1889.text: The added night shifts were stretching them to breaking point: the two volunteers were already covering the daytime desk and had no remaining hours for the preparation they had promised.
The new deadline is stretching us to breaking point alongside the work already agreed, so we need to discuss what can be reassigned.
Covering both the morning deliveries and the evening preparation was stretching her to breaking point before another task was even discussed.
During the winter surge, the small clinic was stretched to breaking point by extra admissions.

advanced-native-1890.text: The temporary room gave them a roof over their heads while repairs continued, but it was crowded and they still needed somewhere to study quietly.
They have a roof over their heads for now, but we should ask what arrangements they still need for the coming weeks.
The family had a roof over their heads at the guesthouse, but still had to decide where the children could do their homework.
A roof over her head was the first need the temporary placement met; building an ordinary routine came later.

advanced-native-1892.text: The short internship gave me a foot in the door at the archive, because I could learn the cataloguing routine and meet the staff; it was an introduction, not an offer of a permanent job.
The placement is a foot in the door, and I want to use it to learn how the team works rather than assume a job will follow.
A short volunteer shift gave her a foot in the door at the community theatre, where she began learning the backstage routine.
The poster got its foot in the door when shoppers stopped to read it, but they still compared prices before choosing.

advanced-native-1893.text: Their account of the housing journey began with sharing a rented room, then a longer stay near work; they described changes in needs rather than a rule that every household must follow the same route.
The housing journey in this interview changes with work and family needs, rather than moving neatly through one standard sequence.
The housing journey in her memoir includes several returns to shared accommodation as her work locations change.
The curator asked visitors to add their own dates to the housing journey instead of choosing from a fixed list of life stages.

advanced-native-1894.text: During her formative years, the reading group showed her that asking an uncertain question was welcome; she later recognised that early experience in the way she listened to younger learners.
The coach mattered during my formative years, but I have also revised some of those early habits through later experience.
The patient explanations he heard during his formative years influenced how he later welcomed questions in his own workshops.
She described the school library as important in her formative years, while also naming teachers she met much later.

advanced-native-1895.text: The student panel had a strong say in the exhibition themes: its proposals changed the shortlist, though the staff still shared the final decision about space and staffing.
The families should have a strong say in the programme, and we need to show which choices their feedback can genuinely change.
The trainees had a strong say in the examples used, although the teacher retained responsibility for the final lesson plan.
She wanted residents to have a strong say in the garden design rather than simply approve a finished drawing.

advanced-native-1897.text: With that quiet mentor, the influence is not loud, but it runs deep: years later, I still pause to ask whose account is missing before I describe a group’s history.
The influence is not loud, but it runs deep in the way our group makes room for uncertain questions before choosing an answer.
For her former tutor, the influence is not loud, but it runs deep in the patient comments she now gives her own learners.
The influence is not loud, but it runs deep when the family still compares several accounts before accepting a story as settled.

advanced-native-1898.text: We grew up on screens, following stories and talking to friends through devices, but our teachers and family conversations also shaped the way we questioned what we saw.
Many of us grew up on screens, yet we used those screens in different ways and brought different family experiences to what we watched.
They grew up on screens, but the interview showed how differently they used games, messages and short videos.
She said she had grown up on screens while also remembering the long conversations that followed family film nights.

advanced-native-1899.text: The rumour about the cancelled club meeting spread at the speed of light through the group chat, while the organiser was still checking whether the room booking had changed.
The preview travelled at the speed of light through our friends’ messages, but it was still an unfinished version.
The rehearsal clip spread at the speed of light among the cast, long before the edited version was ready.
News of the extra tickets travelled at the speed of light through the club, though members still had to check which dates were available.

advanced-native-2001.text: The timetable tool could land on everyone’s phone by Friday, but our trial only showed that six volunteers could open it; we still needed to ask the other club members whether they wanted to use it.
A new tool may land on everyone’s phone in our group, but I still want to ask who can access it and who chooses to use it.
The revised address landed on everyone’s phone in the rehearsal group, and the organiser asked for a separate reply about arrival times.
The guide might land on everyone’s phone before the visit, though the tutor also brought copies for those sharing a device.

advanced-native-2002.text: The full booking list suggested a packed reading, but the entry count told a different story: only forty of the hundred places were used, and we had not yet asked why the others stayed empty.
The details may tell a different story from the first impression, so I want to name what changed and what remains uncertain.
The repair log told a different story from the claim that the machine had never failed during the trial.
Her notes tell a different story about the rehearsal: the long pause was planned, rather than caused by a forgotten line.

advanced-native-2003.text: In our family app it was the same stage, but not quite the same dance: Gran left voice messages about her garden, while my brother mainly used the calendar to arrange visits; neither use described the whole family.
We share the same stage, but not quite the same dance: the common space can hold different purposes if we discuss how to use it.
The shared notebook was the same stage, but not quite the same dance: one member sketched possibilities while another recorded decisions.
For the two visitors it was the same stage, but not quite the same dance, as one studied the building while the other traced a family memory.

advanced-native-2004.text: The reminder spread at lightning speed through the festival group: within minutes people were forwarding it, though it still showed last year’s entrance and had not been checked against the new map.
The ideas came at lightning speed, but I still wanted time to choose which one answered the question we were working on.
She sorted the familiar cards at lightning speed, then slowed down to read the handwritten note she did not recognise.
The invitation travelled at lightning speed through the choir, while decisions about the rehearsal date still needed replies.

advanced-native-2005.text: The first post was the first draft of events: it said the outdoor reading had stopped, but later interviews showed that the group had moved inside; the time of the move still needed checking.
This is the first draft of events, so I want to mark what we know now and explain any later correction clearly.
The hurried diary entry was the first draft of events, and she returned to the timetable before quoting it in her memoir.
He labelled the recording the first draft of events and invited the other witnesses to add what they had actually seen.

advanced-native-2006.text: The edited version compared two witnesses’ times and corrected the name of the organiser, but the reporter still marked one quotation as unconfirmed instead of making the smoother account sound final.
I want to compare the edited version with the original account before deciding whether an important qualification has been lost.
The edited version restored the speaker’s “if”, so readers could see that the plan depended on permission.
She checked the edited version against her notes and asked why a question had been presented as a decision.

advanced-native-2007.text: The post was throwing a dramatic headline at people with “Library closes”, while leaving out that only one room would shut for two days; the notice underneath explained the repair and the rooms that remained open.
I do not want to keep throwing dramatic headlines at people; I want the important point and its limits to be clear together.
The editor rejected throwing a dramatic headline at people and asked the reporter to state which part of the route was affected.
She avoided throwing dramatic headlines at people by putting the agreed facts beside the warning, rather than hiding the issue.

advanced-native-2008.text: The interview became click-worthy fragments in the feed: the clip kept the startled reaction but ended before the speaker explained that the change was only a proposal, making the plan sound decided.
I want more than click-worthy fragments when a missing qualification changes what the speaker seems to have agreed to.
The profile offered more than click-worthy fragments by keeping the speaker’s reservation beside the striking quote.
He compared the click-worthy fragments with the full recording before deciding what the speaker had actually promised.

advanced-native-2009.text: The local paper could not live on reputation alone: its old awards mattered, but readers still needed clear corrections and checked local reports, not simply the same prize list beside every new article.
Our group cannot live on reputation alone, so we want newcomers to see how we work now rather than only hear what we won before.
The festival could not live on reputation alone when returning visitors wanted to know how this year’s programme had been chosen.
The gallery cannot live on reputation forever; visitors also need to know what its current programme offers.

advanced-native-2010.text: We tried to separate real information from noise by checking the organiser’s dated update against the repeated screenshots; it confirmed a later start, while the claim about cancellation still had no named source.
To separate real information from noise, I want to know which details are confirmed and which are still suggestions or unsupported claims.
She separated real information from noise in the interview notes by marking which times had been checked against the diary.
At the archive, the curator separated facts from noise by checking labels against the accession records.

advanced-native-2011.text: The chair offered a cooler head in a very noisy world by asking each neighbour what the garden needed before comparing the plans; she did not treat the loudest reaction as the whole group’s view.
A patient question can offer a cooler head in a very noisy world without pretending that the disagreement does not matter.
The librarian offered a cooler head in a very noisy world by separating the question about access from the argument about personal taste.
His short reflection became a cooler head in a very noisy world when it acknowledged the worry before asking what could be checked.

advanced-native-2012.text: Our monthly calls helped keep that relationship alive after my aunt moved: we asked about each other’s current projects, and later letters gave us another way to respond when a call was difficult.
I want to keep our relationship alive through attention to what matters to us now, not only by repeating how we used to talk.
They kept their relationship alive by asking about the new routines rather than assuming the distance had changed nothing.
The shared sketchbook helped keep that relationship alive because each drawing invited a response from the other person.

advanced-native-2013.text: Although I missed the planning meeting, the short summary helped me stay in the loop about the confirmed room and the questions still open; it did not ask me to approve decisions I had not discussed.
I would like to stay in the loop about the decisions that affect my role, without needing to read every informal message as it arrives.
She stayed in the loop through the agreed weekly note, then asked a separate question before accepting a new responsibility.
The coordinator helped volunteers stay in the loop by separating confirmed dates from suggestions still under discussion.

advanced-native-2015.text: I opened the feed to find one exhibition photo, then got caught in the endless scroll as more posts followed without a clear finish; by the time I closed it, I had forgotten which caption I wanted to check.
I want to find the caption I came for, rather than lose it in the endless scroll of posts that keep leading somewhere else.
The endless scroll made it hard for him to find the one dated notice he had opened the page to read.
She left the endless scroll for a captioned album with a final page, choosing to finish the family sequence before browsing anything else.

advanced-native-2016.text: Their posts were highlight reels of the workshop: smiling portraits and the finished pieces were real, but the late repairs and quiet disagreements were not shown, so the feed was not a complete record of the week.
A highlight reel can show something genuinely joyful without showing what every ordinary day involved.
Her travel photographs formed a highlight reel, so he asked what the ordinary working days had been like before comparing their experiences.
The class shared a highlight reel of the performance and kept a separate record of the changes they wanted to discuss later.

advanced-native-2017.text: Comparing unrelated poster styles pulled us off track while we were meant to prepare interview questions; by the end of the session, we had chosen colours but still had no opening question for the guest.
A useful question can change what I do next without pulling me off track, if it helps the purpose we agreed to pursue.
The debate over the cover pulled them off track from checking the permissions that had to be settled before printing.
She asked whether the new example helped the central question or was pulling the class off track towards a different topic.

advanced-native-2018.text: I will come off the app after reading the rehearsal update tonight, then leave tomorrow’s question for our agreed email exchange; I am not deleting the group or promising to answer every message before I stop.
I am going to come off the app for the evening, but I will be clear about which messages can wait and how to reach me for the agreed task.
She came off the platform for a month and told her collaborators which email address she would check instead.
He planned to come off the app after sending the agreed note, without treating that pause as a decision to leave the choir.

advanced-native-2020.text: Jin took to it like a duck to water when shown the basic recording controls, but still asked how to obtain permission before publishing another person’s voice; easy controls did not settle that separate question.
I took to it like a duck to water when I first tried the simple controls, but I still asked for help with the unfamiliar settings.
