She got her act together by checking the promised tasks with her partner before accepting another one.
He was getting his act together for the exhibition, but still asked a colleague to check the final labels.

advanced-native-1161.text: Answering one newcomer’s question helped us build momentum on the guide: her follow-up revealed a missing example, and another reader then offered a clearer map, though the final route still needed checking.
We are building momentum when one useful step gives us information and support for the next one.
Finishing the first panel helped the painters build momentum as they could show volunteers exactly what needed doing next.
The repair campaign gathered real momentum once three local groups offered volunteers.

advanced-native-1162.text: The archive project threw us two curveballs: the reader we had booked was suddenly unavailable, and a box arrived with letters we had not known existed; we paused the programme to agree what needed a new decision.

pronunciation.phonemesBefore: ðɪ ˈɑːɹkaɪv pɹˈɑːdʒɛkt θɹˈuː ˌʌs tˈuː kˈɜːvɪbˌɔːlz: ðə ɹˈiːdɚ wiː hæd bˈʊkt wʌz sˈʌdənli ʌnɐvˈeɪləbəl, ænd ɐ bˈɑːks ɚɹˈaɪvd wɪð lˈɛɾɚz wiː hæd nˌɑːt nˈoʊn ɛɡzˈɪstᵻd; wiː pˈɔːzd ðə pɹˈoʊɡɹæm tʊ ɐɡɹˈiː wʌt nˈiːdᵻd ɐ nˈuː dᵻsˈɪʒən.
pronunciation.phonemesAfter: ðɪ ˈɑːɹkaɪv pɹˈɑːdʒɛkt θɹˈuː ˌʌs tˈuː kˈɜːɹvbˌɔːlz: ðə ɹˈiːdɚ wiː hæd bˈʊkt wʌz sˈʌdənli ʌnɐvˈeɪləbəl, ænd ɐ bˈɑːks ɚɹˈaɪvd wɪð lˈɛɾɚz wiː hæd nˌɑːt nˈoʊn ɛɡzˈɪstᵻd; wiː pˈɔːzd ðə pɹˈoʊɡɹæm tʊ ɐɡɹˈiː wʌt nˈiːdᵻd ɐ nˈuː dᵻsˈɪʒən.

advanced-native-1162.text: Life threw us a curveball, so we checked what had changed before deciding which part of the plan to revise.

pronunciation.phonemesBefore: lˈaɪf θɹˈuː ˌʌs ɐ kˈɜːvɪbˌɔːl, sˌəʊ wiː tʃˈɛkt wɒt had tʃˈeɪndʒd bɪfˌɔː dɪsˈaɪdɪŋ wˌɪtʃ pˈɑːt ɒvðə plˈan tə ɹɪvˈaɪz.
pronunciation.phonemesAfter: lˈaɪf θɹˈuː ˌʌs ɐ kˈɜːvbˌɔːl, sˌəʊ wiː tʃˈɛkt wɒt had tʃˈeɪndʒd bɪfˌɔː dɪsˈaɪdɪŋ wˌɪtʃ pˈɑːt ɒvðə plˈan tə ɹɪvˈaɪz.

advanced-native-1162.text: The unexpected question threw the panel a curveball, and they asked for a moment to check the figures.

pronunciation.phonemesBefore: ðɪ ˌʌnɛkspˈɛktɪd kwˈɛstʃən θɹˈuː ðə pˈanəl ɐ kˈɜːvɪbˌɔːl, and ðeɪ ˈaskt fəɹə mˈəʊmənt tə tʃˈɛk ðə fˈɪɡəz.
pronunciation.phonemesAfter: ðɪ ˌʌnɛkspˈɛktɪd kwˈɛstʃən θɹˈuː ðə pˈanəl ɐ kˈɜːvbˌɔːl, and ðeɪ ˈaskt fəɹə mˈəʊmənt tə tʃˈɛk ðə fˈɪɡəz.

advanced-native-1162.text: Each permit review threw curveballs at us, so we scheduled extra time for revisions.

pronunciation.phonemesBefore: ˈiːtʃ pˈɜːmɪt ɹɪvjˈuː θɹˈuː kˈɜːvɪbˌɔːlz at ˌʌs, sˌəʊ wiː ʃˈɛdjuːld ˈɛkstɹə tˈaɪm fɔː ɹɪvˈɪʒənz.
pronunciation.phonemesAfter: ˈiːtʃ pˈɜːmɪt ɹɪvjˈuː θɹˈuː kˈɜːvbˌɔːlz at ˌʌs, sˌəʊ wiː ʃˈɛdjuːld ˈɛkstɹə tˈaɪm fɔː ɹɪvˈɪʒənz.

advanced-native-1163.text: The lost script showed me what my partner was made of: she stayed patient, helped each actor reconstruct a cue and asked for a pause when we needed it, rather than blaming the newest member.
What someone is made of can show in patient cooperation as well as in an individual attempt, so I want to describe the actual actions.
The difficult rehearsal showed what they were made of when they listened to the quietest member and shared the unfinished work.
She wanted to show what she was made of by keeping her promise and asking for the help the task needed.

advanced-native-1164.text: In the story, I felt I was falling apart after my closest friend left: I could not finish a simple reply and kept losing my place, so I asked my sister to sit with me while I decided what to say.
I felt as if I was falling apart, but I can describe what became difficult without treating one moment as my whole character.
He felt he was falling apart when the news arrived, and asked his friend to stay while he found the words for a reply.
The narrator said she was falling to pieces, but another scene showed her slowly finding a way to ask for support.

advanced-native-1165.text: We stepped back from arguing about the poster’s headline and asked what visitors actually needed to know first; that changed the question from whose wording sounded cleverer to whether the entrance instructions were clear.
I want to step back from the immediate argument and ask what our decision needs to achieve.
The facilitators stepped back from counting answers and asked whose questions had not yet been heard.
She was stepping back to review her own assumptions, not leaving the group without an agreed handover.

advanced-native-1167.text: The quiet discussion turned out to be more useful than I had expected: two people wrote questions instead of speaking, and those notes showed us where the guide still confused its readers.
It turned out differently from what I expected, so I want to describe what happened rather than keep my first assumption.
The rough sketch turned out to be the clearest way to explain the scene’s two viewpoints.
It turned out that both writers had kept the same letter, but remembered its last sentence differently.

advanced-native-1168.text: In our fictional media club, the team drew a line in the sand over identifiable portraits: no public posting without the person’s agreement, even if a last-minute photograph would improve the layout.
I want to draw a line in the sand about that behaviour while making clear how we can still work together.
She drew a line in the sand over personal jokes in the rehearsal while remaining open to criticism of the scene.
The organisers had drawn a line in the sand about changing the agreed names without asking the people involved.

advanced-native-1169.text: The idea of turning the notes into a play was only a passing thought while I packed the box; I returned to the archive list and did not ask anyone to begin rehearsing it.
It was a passing thought rather than a commitment, so I want to clarify that before anyone acts on it.
A passing thought about the old photograph returned later when she found the matching letter.
He gave the new title a passing thought before returning to the question the readers had asked.

advanced-native-1170.text: We are leaving the date up in the air until Friday, when the caretaker can confirm which room is free; the reading itself is still planned, and we can choose the passages meanwhile.
The date is up in the air while we wait for the room information, but we can still prepare the parts that do not depend on it.
Her job plans were up in the air while she considered two offers with different working hours.
The editor left the question up in the air until both writers had explained which version they wanted to keep.

advanced-native-1171.text: The promise of weekly feedback was backed up by action: the mentor reserved time in the first two sessions and returned annotated drafts, although we still needed to agree the dates for the rest of term.
The promise was backed up by action, and I want to name what was done without pretending that the whole commitment is complete.
Her promise to listen was backed up by action when she changed the meeting order to make room for the unanswered question.
They backed up the promise with action by making the agreed materials available before the first workshop.

advanced-native-1173.text: A short film about old radio broadcasts lit the spark for my reading: I borrowed a book about the announcers and began asking why certain voices had been preserved, though I had never studied radio before.
One question lit the spark for a new idea, and I still need to find out what it would take to develop it.
The old photograph lit the spark for a story, and she began by asking who the people beside the gate were.
Their first conversation lit the spark for a collaboration that they later shaped through several very different drafts.

advanced-native-1174.text: Trying one new harmony with friends each month helped keep the fire burning for our choir; we enjoyed discovering how the voices fitted, even when we had no concert planned for that season.
The shared practice kept the fire burning for me, even when I was not preparing anything for a public audience.
Reading each other’s unfinished scenes kept the fire burning during a year when they had no time to stage a full play.
She wanted to keep the fire burning without turning every drawing into a competition entry.

advanced-native-1175.text: Our poster plan was all talk and no follow-through: we kept promising to ask the printer, but by the agreed check-in nobody had contacted her or prepared the file; we needed to assign that first step instead of announce another deadline.
I want to compare the promise with the actions before calling a plan all talk and no follow-through.
The repair proposal remained all talk and no follow-through until someone agreed to ask which parts could actually be fixed.
A pledge with no follow-through will not repair the damaged equipment.

advanced-native-1326.text: Dad passed on values through stories about returning borrowed tools on time. He explained how a late return could interrupt someone else’s work, then asked what we thought rather than demanding the same answer from everyone.
We can pass on values through what we explain and do, while leaving room for questions about those beliefs.
She passed on values through the way she credited every person who had helped make the book.
The retiring guide passed knowledge on to new volunteers by walking them through the old maps.

advanced-native-1327.text: The Sunday calls helped hold the family together after our work hours changed. Each person could explain what the week had been like, and we used the conversation to share jobs rather than leave every arrangement to Mum.
We can help hold the family together by sharing the arrangements, not by expecting one person to carry every job.
Their regular letters held the family together through a year of different working hours.
Shared decisions can help hold the family together even when relatives prefer different ways of spending their time.

advanced-native-1328.text: After the puppet workshop, my brother picked the children up at the library and walked home with them. Their bags were already packed, but they still stopped to return a storybook before leaving the building.
Could you tell me where to pick the children up, and whether we need to return anything before leaving?
She picked them up after the reading group, then stayed while they put the borrowed cushions away.
We will pick the children up at the museum entrance and take the tram together.

advanced-native-1330.text: One complaint about the late opening did not give us the whole picture of the fair. We checked the opening log and heard from visitors at different times; the delay was real, but it was not the only part of the day we needed to understand.
I want to understand the whole picture without treating a missing detail as proof that someone else’s experience was false.
The two letters helped her see the whole picture of why the plan changed, including the request she had not received.
He asked for the whole picture before accepting the description of the disagreement as one person’s fault.

advanced-native-1331.text: I was short-tempered during the final rehearsal, answering simple questions with an irritated sigh. The missing props had worried me, but I needed to acknowledge how my replies made it harder for the new actor to ask for help.
I was short-tempered when you asked, and I want to give you a proper answer rather than use my busy day as an excuse.
She became short-tempered as the calls piled up, then asked for a pause before answering the next person.
His short-tempered reply left the question unanswered, so he returned later to explain it more patiently.

advanced-native-1332.text: After the audition, our quiet conversation offered emotional shelter. My friend listened without asking me to turn the disappointment into a lesson straight away; the result still hurt, but I no longer had to hide how I felt.
The group offered emotional shelter by letting me listen quietly without requiring me to share a personal story.
The familiar songs offered emotional shelter during a week when she could not yet explain what was troubling her.
He found emotional shelter in a friendship where silence did not have to be filled with advice.

advanced-native-1333.text: I tried not to snap or rush them when the new volunteers asked how to sort the books. I let them finish each question, then explained one step at a time rather than treating their hesitation as unwillingness to help.
I will not snap or rush you, but I need to explain when I must leave so we can agree what to do next.
She chose not to snap or rush them when they needed another moment to explain the missing page.
I will not snap or rush you while you work out which part of the instructions is unclear.

advanced-native-1334.text: Our story tutor showed a warm heart and a long fuse when I lost my place three times. She welcomed each attempt and waited while I found the line, then checked whether a shorter passage would make the next turn easier.
A warm heart and a long fuse can make a welcome gentler, but people still need time and support to offer that care.
She showed a warm heart and a long fuse, helping newcomers ask again when they had missed a step.
He brought a warm heart and a long fuse to the discussion, while still explaining when the room had to close.

advanced-native-1335.text: The residents are being spoken to as if their opinions no longer count: the host dismisses their questions about the seating plan. A volunteer asks for their preferences before the plan is finalised.
We should not be spoken to as if our opinions no longer count just because we cannot attend the meeting in person.
The volunteers objected to being spoken to as if their opinions no longer count after years of working on the collection.
Please make room for questions, so people are not spoken to as if their opinions no longer count when plans change.

advanced-native-1336.text: The welcome desk needed a soft touch and a steady pair of hands. Lena listened calmly to worried newcomers, then checked each booking against the list instead of promising places she had not confirmed.
This role needs a soft touch and a steady pair of hands, including the confidence to explain a limit without dismissing the person asking.
The reading group needed a soft touch and a steady pair of hands when new members brought questions and unfinished forms.
He offered a soft touch and a steady pair of hands, listening to the complaint and keeping a clear record of what still needed checking.

advanced-native-1338.text: Clear updates matter more than ever now that the building has two temporary entrances. Visitors have received different directions, so we agreed to check the route each morning and put the same current information at both doors.
Rest matters more than ever during this crowded week, but I still need to agree which tasks can wait.
A clear handover matters more than ever now that three people share the same role on different days.
Her familiar routine mattered more than ever during the move, when so many other parts of the day were changing.

advanced-native-1340.text: For me, home is not just a place: it is the evening when we put our phones aside and cook together. We rent a small flat, but the shared attention matters more to this description than whether we own the walls.
Home is not just a place, but I want to hear what gives it meaning for you rather than assume we feel the same.
Home is not just a place in her account; it includes the neighbour who always asked how her day had gone.
Home is not just a place, he said, while carefully keeping the letters that made the old room feel connected to his family.

advanced-native-1342.text: A single meeting may sound ideal in theory but leave out the volunteers working evenings. We have not abandoned the idea; we are checking whether a written discussion could let those members contribute before the decision.
The plan may sound ideal in theory but need a small trial before we promise it will work for everyone.
The rota sounded ideal in theory but left no time for handing over the equipment between groups.
The shared cupboard may sound ideal in theory but needs a clear agreement about which items everyone can use.

advanced-native-1343.text: The outdoor exhibition will have round-the-clock supervision while the displays remain in the courtyard. Different attendants will cover the shifts, with a handover at each change; nobody is being asked to stay awake for the whole weekend.
Round-the-clock supervision can be shared across shifts, provided we confirm who is responsible at each change.
The festival arranged round-the-clock supervision through a rota that included handovers and rest periods.
They asked whether round-the-clock supervision would continue until the last display had been collected.

advanced-native-1344.text: The library’s evening computer access became a real lifeline when my laptop stopped working before the application deadline. It let me send the portfolio on time, although I still had to prepare the work myself.
The weekly delivery was a real lifeline during the closure, even though the volunteers could not meet every request.
The shared workshop became a real lifeline when her own workspace was closed for repairs.
His patient explanations were a real lifeline during the first week, when the unfamiliar routine made every task difficult.

advanced-native-1345.text: The volunteers were dropping things at the door rather than carrying them into the reading room. They left the labelled bags by the entrance and sent a message, so the organiser knew there were supplies still waiting to be collected.
Please drop the supplies at the door marked for deliveries, then let me know which bags you have left there.
They dropped the supplies at the door and waited for a reply before leaving the building.
She was dropping things at the door while her colleague checked which bags had arrived.

advanced-native-1347.text: I felt cut off from others when the art room closed, even though my phone still worked. I missed the small conversations while we cleaned the tables; a weekly message helped, but it was not quite the same kind of contact.
A quiet place can let me rest without making me feel cut off from the world, provided I can choose when to reconnect.
The letter helped her feel less cut off from the world while the familiar group could not meet.
He felt cut off from others after losing the shared routine, although he could still phone the people he knew.

advanced-native-1348.text: The rumour about a cancelled rehearsal spread like wildfire through the student groups, but the organiser had not confirmed it. We paused the reposts and checked the current notice before deciding whether to change our plans.
A claim can spread like wildfire without becoming more reliable, so I want to check its source before passing it on.
News of the extra performance spread like wildfire, so the theatre published the booking details in one clear notice.
The unconfirmed story was spreading like wildfire before anyone had asked the person concerned what had happened.

advanced-native-1349.text: The former members had not been forgotten: the tutor named their earlier work and invited them to the anniversary reading. Some could not attend, but the invitation made clear that their contributions were still remembered.
Your contribution has not been forgotten, and we would like to ask how you want it acknowledged rather than choose for you.
The request had not been forgotten; she brought it back to the agenda when the missing information arrived.
Their contribution has not been forgotten, although the group now meets in a different place.

advanced-native-1350.text: We set up a lunchtime reading club after asking who wanted to take part. The first session is next week; creating the group did not mean every interested student had already attended or promised to come all term.
Before we set up the group, let us agree its purpose and ask who wants to take responsibility for the first meeting.
They set up a small exchange group so members could offer spare materials without promising to attend every week.
She is setting up a meeting to discuss the shared space before anyone publishes a timetable.

advanced-native-1353.text: For us, kindness is the oil that keeps everyday life running smoothly: a neighbour tells us when a parcel arrives, and we return borrowed chairs promptly. These small acts avoid confusion, though bigger disagreements still need discussion.
Consideration can be the oil that keeps everyday life running smoothly, without making one person responsible for everyone’s arrangements.
A thoughtful reminder was the oil that keeps everyday life running smoothly in their shared studio, preventing a clash over the only workbench.
Her small offers of help were the oil that keeps everyday life running smoothly while the neighbours adjusted to new routines.

advanced-native-1355.text: The judges discussed the poems behind closed doors, then published the winners and a short explanation. The discussion was private, but the result was not hidden; the entrants could read how the final choices had been described.
Could we discuss the concern behind closed doors before agreeing what, if anything, should be shared with the wider group?
The committee met behind closed doors to compare the proposals, then released a summary without naming the speakers.
They agreed to speak behind closed doors before deciding which parts of the disagreement they wanted to discuss publicly.

advanced-native-1356.text: The manager’s human side came through when I explained the missed train. She listened to why I was worried about the group, then helped me work out whom to call rather than simply repeating the departure time.
His human side came through when he asked what the delay meant for us before suggesting the next step.
The guide’s human side came through when she noticed that the visitor needed a moment before asking another question.
His human side comes through in the careful way he asks what help would actually be welcome.

advanced-native-1357.text: The shared garden project began to knit the social fabric back together after the dispute. Neighbours who had stopped speaking exchanged tools again, although they still needed a separate meeting about the disputed boundary.
A shared task may help knit the social fabric back together, but we should ask which relationships have actually begun to change.
The reopened workshop helped knit the social fabric back together as neighbours began sharing tools again.
Their joint newsletter may knit the social fabric back together by giving groups a way to hear one another’s concerns.

advanced-native-1358.text: The new members were left out in the cold when the revised rehearsal time went only to the old mailing list. They wanted to join but arrived after it ended; we checked the list rather than assume they had lost interest.
We do not want anyone left out in the cold, but we should ask which updates they want rather than add them to every list.
The separate invitation meant the former members were not left out in the cold when the main list changed.
She felt out in the cold after the discussion moved to a channel she had never been invited to join.

advanced-native-1359.text: I showed up in body but not in spirit at the planning meeting. I signed in and stayed, yet spent the discussion thinking about my own essay instead of listening; afterwards I could not explain what the group had agreed.
I do not want to show up in body but not in spirit, so I will check the agenda and choose a useful way to contribute.
He showed up in body but not in spirit, then admitted that his attention had been on the unfinished work at home.
She did not want to show up in body but not in spirit, so she chose a smaller role she could prepare for properly.

advanced-native-1361.text: I came to the visit with an open heart, ready to hear why the old workshop mattered to the residents. I asked about the unfamiliar tools instead of assuming I knew their stories; listening did not mean promising to keep every object.
I want to listen with an open heart and ask what I do not understand, without making a promise before we discuss the practical limits.
She brought an open heart to the conversation, asking about the unfamiliar custom before explaining her own view.
He listened with an open heart and still asked for time to decide what help he could honestly offer.

advanced-native-1362.text: I treated the museum visit as another box to tick for the course: I collected the attendance stamp but barely looked at the exhibits. The form was complete, yet I had little to say when we discussed what we had learned.
I do not want the reflection to become another box to tick, so I will explain one actual change in my work rather than only sign the form.
The workshop became another box to tick when he focused only on collecting the certificate and ignored the practice.
She wanted the review to be more than another box to tick, so she brought a specific problem for the team to examine.

advanced-native-1363.text: The trial reading group was encouraging, but I would stop short of saying it suits every age. We heard from six older students only, so I suggested another small session before making a school-wide recommendation.
I would stop short of saying the problem is solved, but the first trial gives us a useful question to test next.
She praised the rehearsal but stopped short of saying the group was ready to perform without another run-through.
He would stop short of saying the new arrangement had solved the disagreement, even though the first conversation was constructive.

advanced-native-1364.text: The gallery guides were on their feet for long hours, walking between rooms and standing beside the displays. The office team also worked hard, but mainly seated at computers; the two roles had different physical demands.
Before I agree to the role, could you explain whether I would be on my feet for long hours or sharing several kinds of tasks?
She was on her feet for long hours during the exhibition, moving between visitors who needed directions.
They expected to be on their feet for long hours, so they asked what the role involved before agreeing to a full day.

advanced-native-1365.text: The exhibition plan could not be finished from behind a desk alone. We used the drawings, then walked through the room to check what a visitor could actually see; the paperwork remained useful, but it did not replace the visit.
I would like to understand both the work behind a desk and the observations that have to be made in the room itself.
She prepared the questions behind a desk, then visited the workshop to see how the process actually worked.
The role involves work behind a desk as well as conversations with people using the shared space.

advanced-native-1366.text: Physical work is not all muscle and mud. The costume maker spent hours controlling small movements with a needle, where precision mattered more than lifting heavy loads; the absence of soil did not make the work purely mental.
Work does not have to be muscle and mud to involve physical skill, precision and effort.
The craft room challenged his picture of physical work as nothing but muscle and mud.
She described both muscle and mud on the building site and the precise hand skills needed to finish the small fittings.

advanced-native-1367.text: We will be on the move between three towns next week, visiting small theatres for the project. Our home address will stay the same, but we asked for the meeting details in writing so we could check them between journeys.
I will be on the move tomorrow, but I can read a short written message when I stop between visits.
She was on the move throughout the morning, carrying questions from one display team to another.
They will be on the move for several days before returning to their usual home and routine.

advanced-native-1368.text: During the room closure, volunteers kept the wheels turning by answering book requests and arranging collections from the foyer. The reading sessions stopped, but the lending service continued in a smaller form until the room reopened.
We can keep the wheels turning in a limited way while being clear about which activities still have to wait.
The small team kept the wheels turning by answering the existing requests while the coordinator was away.
A clear handover can keep the wheels turning without assuming that one substitute will take every decision.

advanced-native-1369.text: The talk introduced conservation and exhibition design. Some students wanted to go into those fields, but they asked about training first; interest in a career did not mean they had already accepted a job.
Before saying they will go into those fields, we should ask which work areas interest them and how far their plans have developed.
They wanted to go into those fields after hearing about conservation and design, but kept asking questions before choosing training.
The visitors discussed education and publishing before asking what it meant to go into those fields in practice.

advanced-native-1370.text: The scenery team needed skilled pairs of hands to repair the folding panels. Several volunteers could carry materials, but only two had practised the joinery; we asked about their time before putting their names on the repair rota.
We need skilled pairs of hands for this part, so let us ask about relevant experience and availability before dividing the work.
The project found skilled pairs of hands when two former makers offered to demonstrate their repair techniques.
A skilled pair of hands helped us finish the delicate detail, while the rest of the group prepared the materials.

advanced-native-1371.text: Experienced sound operators were in short supply. Two could help, but some simultaneous festival performances had no operator; the organiser asked about new times instead of calling the rota complete.
The right-sized clips are in short supply, so we should check which groups actually need them before promising a set to everyone.
Suitable storage boxes were in short supply, although the cupboard held plenty of smaller containers.
Trained helpers were in short supply that morning, so the team asked which activities could wait.

advanced-native-1372.text: The club’s cost-cutting plan combines print orders to reduce repeated delivery charges. No new bill has arrived yet, so we described the intended saving rather than announce that spending had already fallen or anyone’s pay had changed.
Before describing the cost-cutting result, I want to distinguish the proposed measure from the saving shown by the actual bill.
The cost-cutting exercise combined two deliveries, while the team checked whether the new timing still met users’ needs.
She asked what the cost-cutting measures involved before repeating a claim that jobs had already been lost.

advanced-native-1373.text: The report said wages may remain flat next term, not that a decision had been confirmed. We kept the word may in the summary and asked when the updated figures would be available rather than publish a definite outcome.
If wages remain flat, we still need separate evidence about why, rather than infer a cause from the unchanged figure alone.
The published figures showed that wages remained flat, while the report left the reasons for a separate discussion.
The note warned that wages might remain flat, so she kept that uncertainty in her account of the forecast.

advanced-native-1374.text: The new search tool may not lift every boat equally. Experienced users can try it at once, while newcomers still need an introduction; we planned to hear from both groups before describing how much it had helped.
The change may not lift every boat equally, so we need to ask whose experience is missing from the first positive reports.
The new timetable may not lift every boat equally, since some members still cannot attend the earlier start.
Extra practice did not lift every boat equally; both groups improved, but their progress was different.

advanced-native-1375.text: There was a widening gap in completed reading tasks: one group rose from eight to twelve, while the other rose from five to six. Both improved, but the difference grew, so we kept the two results separate in the report.
Before calling it a widening gap, I want to know what was compared and whether the difference has changed over time.
The figures showed a widening gap between the two groups, even though both had completed more tasks than before.
She asked for earlier figures before describing the current difference as a widening gap.

advanced-native-2297.text: Episode one drew on interviews; episode two used recorded diaries. Despite that change, I found the diary-led episode every bit as compelling as its predecessor.
The new exhibition was every bit as compelling as last year’s, although it focused on different artists.
The radio drama was every bit as compelling as its stage version.
A small cast can still make a sequel every bit as compelling.

advanced-native-2298.text: The film follows the actual rescue of hikers trapped by a sudden storm. Their difficult choices make it a gripping real-life story.
The volunteers’ account of the mountain rescue is a gripping real-life story, not an invented adventure.
Recorded interviews turn the dockworkers’ rescue into a gripping real-life story.
A gripping real-life story needs both a factual basis and a way to hold attention.

advanced-native-2306.text: For months, the same song played at every rehearsal and on the bus home. It became a soundtrack to the dancers’ final year together.
That old song became a soundtrack to our summer at the youth centre because we played it every evening.
One song became a soundtrack to the team’s long train journeys.
For us, the melody is a soundtrack to our first year at university.

advanced-native-2308.text: Tara was pleased that her choir had been invited abroad, but worried about missing her family celebration. She had mixed feelings about the trip.
I had mixed feelings about the new timetable: the later start helped me, but the shorter lunch break did not.
She had mixed feelings about leaving the team: the new role was exciting, but she would miss her friends.
Mixed feelings are easier to explain when you name both the hope and the concern.

advanced-native-2310.text: The repair meeting was scheduled for twenty minutes, but a repeated argument made it drag on for nearly two hours, delaying the workshop.
The discussion dragged on past closing time because nobody settled the final question.
The complaint dragged on for weeks after the promised reply date.
A long event need not drag on if its length was planned and welcome.

advanced-native-2319.text: The short story showed a new pupil quietly studying a map of the school before asking for help. That small hesitation rang true to many students who remembered their first day.
Her account of the first rehearsal rang true because she included the small mistakes everyone remembered.
The dialogue rang true to former students, but no one claimed it was a transcript.
A familiar detail can make a story ring true without proving it happened.

advanced-native-2327.text: The film follows two sisters who restore their father’s old radio and hear a recording of his voice at the end. Many viewers called it a tearjerker.

pronunciation.phonemesBefore: ðə fˈɪlm fˈɑːloʊz tˈuː sˈɪstɚz hˌuː ɹᵻstˈɔːɹ ðɛɹ fˈɑːðɚz ˈoʊld ɹˈeɪdɪˌoʊ ænd hˈɪɹ ɐ ɹᵻkˈɔːɹdɪŋ ʌv hɪz vˈɔɪs æt ðɪ ˈɛnd. mˈɛni vjˈuːɚz kˈɔːld ɪɾ ɐ tˈɪɹdʒɚkɚ.
pronunciation.phonemesAfter: ðə fˈɪlm fˈɑːloʊz tˈuː sˈɪstɚz hˌuː ɹᵻstˈɔːɹ ðɛɹ fˈɑːðɚz ˈoʊld ɹˈeɪdɪˌoʊ ænd hˈɪɹ ɐ ɹᵻkˈɔːɹdɪŋ ʌv hɪz vˈɔɪs æt ðɪ ˈɛnd. mˈɛni vjˈuːɚz kˈɔːld ɪɾ ɐ tˈɪɹdʒˈɜːkɚ.

advanced-native-2327.text: The final reunion made the drama a tearjerker for many viewers, although others stayed dry-eyed.

pronunciation.phonemesBefore: ðə fˈaɪnəl ɹˌiːjˈuːniən mˌeɪd ðə dɹˈɑːməɹ ɐ tˈiədʒəkə fɔː mˈɛni vjˈuːəz, ɔːlðˈəʊ ˈʌðəz stˈeɪd dɹˈaɪˈaɪd.
pronunciation.phonemesAfter: ðə fˈaɪnəl ɹˌiːjˈuːniən mˌeɪd ðə dɹˈɑːməɹ ɐ tˈiədʒˈɜːkə fɔː mˈɛni vjˈuːəz, ɔːlðˈəʊ ˈʌðəz stˈeɪd dɹˈaɪˈaɪd.

advanced-native-2327.text: The novel is a tearjerker because its reunion is built on years of separation.

pronunciation.phonemesBefore: ðə nˈɒvəl ɪz ɐ tˈiədʒəkə bɪkˈɒz ɪts ɹˌiːjˈuːniən ɪz bˈɪlt ˌɒn jˈiəz ɒv sˌɛpəɹˈeɪʃən.
pronunciation.phonemesAfter: ðə nˈɒvəl ɪz ɐ tˈiədʒˈɜːkə bɪkˈɒz ɪts ɹˌiːjˈuːniən ɪz bˈɪlt ˌɒn jˈiəz ɒv sˌɛpəɹˈeɪʃən.

advanced-native-2327.text: Calling a film a tearjerker does not mean every viewer reacts in the same way.

pronunciation.phonemesBefore: kˈɔːlɪŋ ɐ fˈɪlm ɐ tˈiədʒəkə dʌznˌɒt mˈiːn ˈɛvɹɪ vjˈuːə ɹɪˈakts ɪnðə sˈeɪm wˈeɪ.
pronunciation.phonemesAfter: kˈɔːlɪŋ ɐ fˈɪlm ɐ tˈiədʒˈɜːkə dʌznˌɒt mˈiːn ˈɛvɹɪ vjˈuːə ɹɪˈakts ɪnðə sˈeɪm wˈeɪ.

advanced-native-2332.text: The short film has a quiet opening, yet the newcomer’s lively expressions immediately light up the screen and draw viewers into the scene.
In the final scene, the actor lights up the screen with a small, hopeful smile.
The supporting actor lit up the screen in a brief scene at the station.
An expressive face can light up the screen without a long speech.

advanced-native-2335.text: Mina meant to be efficient, but her one-word email replies came across as impatient to the new volunteers.
His careful questions came across as thoughtful, not critical, during the interview.
Her comment came across as supportive because she offered a useful suggestion.
A direct question can come across as rude if the tone is too sharp.

advanced-native-2342.text: The film’s story received mixed reviews, but tickets sold quickly after the well-known singer joined the cast. The producer credited her star power.
The concert sold out on star power, but the arrangements still had to satisfy the audience.
Star power filled the opening night, though critics still judged the play on its writing.
The campaign borrowed a singer’s star power to draw attention to the charity.

advanced-native-2350.text: At the festival, teenagers sang the chorus while their grandparents shared memories of hearing the song years earlier. The tune still crosses generational lines.
The comedy crosses generational lines: children enjoy the jokes, and grandparents recognise the family stories.
The board game crossed generational lines at our family gathering.
A shared story can cross generational lines even when each age group notices different details.

advanced-native-2351.text: In the play, a child waits for a parent who is late. Audiences with very different lives recognise the wish to feel cared for. The scene taps into something universal.
The film taps into something universal when its characters try to find a place where they belong.
By showing a choice the speaker wishes she could undo, the poem taps into something universal.
A specific scene can tap into something universal when it reveals a widely shared fear.

advanced-native-2353.text: The characters joke through dinner, but each pauses when their absent sister’s name is mentioned. An emotional undercurrent of grief runs beneath the humour.
An emotional undercurrent of worry runs beneath the family’s cheerful preparations.
The bright dialogue hides an emotional undercurrent of uncertainty.
An emotional undercurrent can make a cheerful scene feel quietly sad.

advanced-native-2358.text: The theatre director spoke with sweeping gestures, turned every rehearsal note into a vivid story, and filled the room with energy. To the cast, she seemed larger than life.
The local guide was larger than life, bringing every old harbour tale alive with his voice.
Her larger than life personality brought warmth to the small café.
A larger than life character can be memorable without being well known.

advanced-native-2360.text: The club treasurer showed receipts with a clear accounting error, but a few members refused even to look because they trusted the chair unconditionally. Their blind devotion made review difficult.
Blind devotion made the board ignore repeated warnings about the damaged equipment.
Blind devotion can make a group ignore evidence it ought to examine.
The volunteers avoided blind devotion by checking every claim against the records.

advanced-native-2354.text: At the community kitchen, Hana joined early but did not become shift lead for that alone. Over several weekends, she kept accurate stock notes, handled a delayed delivery and trained newcomers. She had earned her stripes.
After a month of careful fieldwork, the survey volunteer earned her stripes by checking disputed measurements and explaining the corrections to the team.
A title may open the door, but repeated reliable work is how a new team member earns their stripes.
The translator earned her stripes after checking difficult terms across several public notices.

advanced-native-2361.text: The team first teased their captain about a harmless mistake, but the jokes went too far when they mentioned a private family matter in front of guests.
The criticism went too far when the reviewer quoted a private message unrelated to the play.
The interview went too far when the host pressed for details about a family dispute.
A joke can go too far when it reveals information shared in confidence.

advanced-native-2362.text: The young musician admired the violinist’s technique. Later, he insisted she could never make a poor choice and copied even her unrelated opinions. His admiration had become hero worship.
Hero worship began to replace thoughtful listening when every comment about the singer was treated as an insult.
Hero worship can make a fan confuse admiration with unquestioning approval.
A respectful interview can avoid hero worship by asking thoughtful questions.

advanced-native-2366.text: After winning the regional contest, the robotics team celebrated, then checked the parts that still failed in testing. Their coach said they had kept their feet on the ground.
Even after the prize, she kept her feet on the ground and asked how to improve the next film.
After her first exhibition sold out, the artist kept her feet on the ground and planned the next one carefully.
You can keep your feet on the ground and still be proud of your achievement.

advanced-native-2394.text: In chapter one, the author mentions a scratched brass key on the desk. Only at the end do we learn it opens the locked studio. She planted a tiny clue early in the story.
The playwright planted a tiny clue when a character checked the station clock twice.
A mystery can plant a tiny clue in a casual remark that matters later.
She planted a tiny clue on page two without revealing the answer.

advanced-native-2397.text: Mina opened the school portal to find her timetable. The links had unclear labels, so she got lost among the pages and asked a classmate where to click.
Visitors get lost in the museum app because the ticket link is hidden under an unclear label.
People can get lost when several menu labels point to similar pages.
A clear menu helps users avoid getting lost in the booking site.

advanced-native-2399.text: The club found two different dates on the concert posters. Instead of guessing, its members played detective and checked the venue records to find the correct date.
We played detective with the old emails and found where the meeting time had changed.
Students can play detective when two records disagree.
She played detective with the delivery notes to find the missing parcel.

advanced-native-2400.text: The printer broke before the school fair. A nearby shop printed the signs overnight, and that quick help kept preparations moving.
Clear handover notes kept the project moving while our manager was away.
A replacement laptop kept the newspaper moving when the office computer failed.
Small contributions can keep a local service moving until regular funding returns.

advanced-native-2410.text: The museum had misplaced a photograph from its archive. When visitors began checking old exhibition lists, they joined the hunt for the missing image.
Several readers joined the hunt for the missing page by comparing copies of the old journal.
Families joined the hunt for the lost dog by checking nearby parks.
The first clue made readers join the hunt for the thief’s identity.

advanced-native-2398.text: The reveal arrives too quickly; let the mystery breathe by showing the torn ticket before the detective explains it.
We can let the mystery breathe by showing the photograph before the investigator explains why it matters.
A useful clue can let the mystery breathe before the final answer arrives.
Letting the story breathe requires meaningful development, not extra minutes alone.

advanced-native-2714.text: The quieter song clicked emotionally with Mira: it reminded her of music her grandmother used to play, and its gentle mood suited the old photographs.
The old recording clicked emotionally with our classmates because it brought back the school choir.
A song can click emotionally even when another track is more polished.
What clicks emotionally for one audience may leave another unmoved.

advanced-native-2844.text: On the library's online board, dozens of residents debated a proposed bus route, sometimes talking over one another. For this issue, the board was a crowded town square; moderators kept replies on topic.
The tenants' online forum became a digital town square when neighbours debated how to use the shared roof.
A moderated forum can still be a digital town square if people exchange views in public.
A one-way announcement feed is not an online town square, even if many people read it.

advanced-native-3013.text: The theatre group has enough rehearsal space for either a weekend children's workshop or a new evening show, not both this term. Choosing the workshop opens one door and closes another: children gain a class, but the show must wait.
Using the only exhibition budget for new lighting opens one door and closes another: the gallery upgrade can start, while the audio tour waits.
Opening one door and closing another describes a real trade-off, not a promise that the second path is lost forever.
With one available slot, a choice may open one door and close another until more resources arrive.

advanced-native-2411.text: The sports team received one message about a changed match time and another about a different venue. By comparing both notices with the official schedule, they pieced the puzzle together and found the correct plan.
The volunteers pieced the puzzle together by comparing old photographs with the building records.
Investigators pieced the puzzle together from the receipts and delivery notes.
Mara wanted to understand her family’s move. Two dated postcards and a tenancy letter helped her piece it together.

advanced-native-2414.text: The play shows a town leader hiding food from struggling families so his friends can profit. It explores the darker side of human nature through greed and betrayal.
The drama examines the darker side of human nature when a friend betrays the group for money.
A trusted official’s betrayal reveals the darker side of human nature.
The darker side of human nature appears when the character profits from a neighbour’s loss.

advanced-native-2415.text: At first, the club blamed the treasurer for a missing payment. Then the bank statement showed the payment had been sent to the wrong account, and the truth rose to the surface.
The truth rose to the surface when the caretaker's log showed that the keys had been moved to storage, not stolen.
The truth rose to the surface when the signed form was found.
Weeks later, the truth rises to the surface through the archived messages.

advanced-native-2416.text: The volunteers could not explain why the old shop had two opening dates. Then they found a letter showing it had moved to a new street, and the two dates fell into place.
Once the archivist found the transfer note, the two dates fell into place.
The timetable fell into place when the missing booking email arrived.
With the final witness account, the sequence of events fell into place.

advanced-native-2419.text: Lena planned to read one chapter of the mystery before bed, but each chapter ended with a fresh question. She stayed up to finish it and called the book a page-turner.
The novel is a page-turner because each new clue changes what we think happened.
That detective story is a page-turner from its first clue to its final answer.
A page-turner gives readers a reason to keep reading, not merely a quick page count.

advanced-native-2428.text: The community kitchen had waited for its food delivery all morning. Once the ingredients arrived, the cooks got on with the job of preparing lunch for the residents.
Once the safety check was complete, the team got on with the job of setting up the stage.
When the permit arrived, the organisers got on with the job of preparing the event.
We got on with the job after the missing equipment was replaced.

advanced-native-2438.text: The school fair team kept copying names into three separate lists. They made one shared form with a final check for errors, helping everyone work smarter rather than harder.
A shared template let the editors work smarter rather than harder while keeping the final proofread.
A single schedule helped the staff work smarter rather than harder without dropping the review step.
We can work smarter rather than harder by checking the form once instead of copying it three times.

advanced-native-2443.text: The local paper lost access to its files, and its backup system also failed. With no pages ready to print, production ground to a halt for the day.
The ticket system ground to a halt when both the server and its backup went offline.
The repairs ground to a halt when the replacement parts ran out.
Without a valid permit, the construction work may grind to a halt.

advanced-native-2449.text: The new bicycle needs little maintenance, which matters to commuters who ride every day. That low upkeep is one of its strongest selling points.
For busy parents, the lunch box’s easy-clean lid is one of its strongest selling points.
A quiet motor is one of the strongest selling points for people in small flats.
A useful feature becomes a key selling point when it answers a buyer’s real concern.

advanced-native-2452.text: The new library tablet comes loaded with an offline dictionary, audio instructions and large-text settings. Visitors can use all three without installing anything.
The reader comes loaded with language guides and audio controls that work offline.
The camera comes loaded with editing tools that are ready on day one.
The new display came loaded with accessibility settings at no extra cost.

advanced-native-2457.text: A budgeting app helped Noor spot waste, but its strict limits made her skip necessary groceries. She revised them around her needs: the app was a brilliant servant, but a poor master.
A navigation app can be a brilliant servant, but a poor master if drivers follow it past a clear road-closure sign.
As a tool, technology is a brilliant servant, but a poor master if it replaces a person’s judgment.
Money can be a good servant, but a poor master when saving begins to crowd out time with family.

advanced-native-2458.text: At first, the fitness tracker helped Eli remember walks. Then he began cancelling family visits whenever it ordered another workout. The alerts were running his life.
The study timetable was running her life when she stopped seeing friends just to satisfy every reminder.
The reminder app began running his life when it replaced choices he wanted to make himself.
A timetable can help, but it should not end up running your life.

advanced-native-2462.text: A child enjoyed trying robotics, but heard for months that it was not a hobby for girls. She gradually stopped attending. The teacher discussed how social conditioning can shape a child’s choices.
Social conditioning can affect the activities students feel free to try, even when no rule forbids them.
Social conditioning may narrow what children believe they are allowed to enjoy.
Questioning social conditioning can help a student make a freer choice.

advanced-native-2479.text: A neighbourhood bookshop could not match the chains’ advertising budget. It trained staff to take online orders, helping the shop stay in the game without claiming it would outsell the chains.
Local bakeries can stay in the game by offering a service their customers value.
A small grocer stayed in the game by adding a reliable delivery option.
Training can help workers stay in the game when industry skills change.

advanced-native-2483.text: The clinic staff had to copy each patient detail onto three separate forms, and simple requests were taking days. They were drowning in paperwork until the forms were combined.
The team was drowning in paperwork before it replaced three forms with one shared record.
The office was drowning in paperwork before it simplified its application process.
When forms repeat the same questions, a small team can quickly drown in paperwork.

advanced-native-2490.text: The actors were already rehearsing late for opening night. A new daily report was then required from each of them, and the extra task piled on pressure during the final week.
Adding another report piles on pressure when the small team is already working late.
A new fee can pile on pressure for families already facing high rents.
Replacing duplicate forms with one form does not pile on pressure; it removes work.

advanced-native-2494.text: During the museum tour, Leo grouped facts about each room by period and theme. At revision time he could retrieve them easily; the groupings served as a mental filing system.
Grouping memories by place gave her a mental filing system for recalling the trip.
A mental filing system helps me find the right example when I speak.
Categories can create a mental filing system, but they work only if I can use them to recall details.

advanced-native-2500.text: After three crowded school fairs, the committee compared where queues formed each year. They realised the entrance needed a second ticket desk. The comparison helped turn memory into insight.
By comparing old feedback, the organisers turned memory into insight and changed the next event.
Old records can turn memory into insight when we use them to find a pattern.
Remembering a mistake is useful, but reflecting on it can turn memory into insight.

advanced-native-2501.text: At the event desk, two volunteers had to answer calls, check registrations and explain directions at the same time. Their minds were overloaded, so they asked a third person to handle the calls.
Their minds were overloaded by the instructions arriving all at once.
A single clear task may be easy even when our minds are overloaded by several simultaneous tasks.
The students’ minds were overloaded when every new instruction arrived together.

advanced-native-2502.text: Mei had ideas for a short speech, but she mixed examples, dates and side stories without a plan. Her thinking got cluttered, so she grouped the notes around one main point.
When unrelated examples filled my notes, my thinking got cluttered and I lost the main point.
An outline helps me when my thinking gets cluttered by unrelated details.
Grouping the notes by topic stopped my thinking from getting cluttered.

advanced-native-2511.text: A club secretary sent members the wrong meeting date twice. Even after the correction, some members checked her next notice elsewhere. The repeated errors dented her credibility.
Repeated timetable errors can dent your credibility with the people relying on your updates.
A false claim can dent your credibility even if you later correct it.
Checking a figure before publication can prevent it from denting your credibility.

advanced-native-2516.text: After Priya volunteered to lead the display, the coordinator wrote, “We need someone more reliable.” Priya had worked on every earlier display, so the message stung.
The message can sting when it seems to erase someone’s effort.
The message can sting even if its writer intended to offer feedback.
His message stung the volunteer, so the manager explained what was meant.

advanced-native-2519.text: Nora apologised for sharing her friend’s private news. Even after saying “all right,” her friend avoided personal conversations with Nora for weeks. The hurt may run deeper than that reply suggests.
After the apology, the hurt may run deeper if the person still avoids sharing personal news.
The hurt may run deeper when the same betrayal changes what a friend feels safe sharing.
A quick apology matters, but the hurt may run deeper than words alone can repair.

advanced-native-2521.text: The theatre’s online ticket scanner usually moves queues quickly, but a damaged code sometimes will not scan. Staff keep a printed booking list because the scanner is helpful but not foolproof.
The attendance app is convenient but not foolproof when a student’s phone has no power.
A useful map app is not foolproof when a road closes without warning.
The reminder system is not foolproof, so a second person checks important deadlines.

advanced-native-2524.text: A ferry information service promised alerts before schedule changes. During a sudden cancellation, no alert reached waiting passengers, and the service let them down when they needed it.
The booking platform let them down when the promised confirmation never arrived.
The weather service let us down when the warning arrived after the storm.
When a team expects help, a promised helper who does not arrive can let them down on a busy day.

advanced-native-2527.text: A calculator gave the correct total for a class trip. The organiser still had to decide whether every student could afford the cost; it could calculate, but it could not think on her behalf.
A map can show routes, but it cannot think on your behalf about what matters most on the trip.
Search results can inform us, but they cannot think on our behalf.
A calculator cannot think on your behalf when the question involves people’s needs.

advanced-native-2553.text: The town council was deciding whether to close the only evening bus route. Workers who finish late might lose a reliable way home. Their access to transport was at stake in the vote.
When the only accessible route is threatened, more than convenience is at stake.
A trusted service is at stake when a council considers closing it.
At stake here is access to the only free class in the area.

advanced-native-2563.text: The residents’ online group had spam posts, but its archive held useful repair advice. Deleting the entire group would throw the baby out with the bathwater; the moderators chose to remove spam and keep the archive.
Removing useful lessons along with one error would throw the baby out with the bathwater.
When just one section needs fixing, do not throw the baby out with the bathwater.
They threw the baby out with the bathwater by deleting the archive to remove a few spam posts.

advanced-native-2554.text: The ramp has lost an edge guard. A wheelchair wheel nearly slipped off it this morning. It is downright dangerous until the guard is replaced.
Mocking a learner after they ask for help is downright rude; the tutor should intervene.
A blocked exit can be downright dangerous; use this forceful wording when the evidence supports serious risk.
A late reply may be annoying, but calling someone downright dishonest needs evidence that they meant to mislead.

advanced-native-2341.text: At the rehearsal, Tessa stopped sounding as if she were reading a script. She inhabited the role of the anxious nurse, reacting to each new question as the nurse would.
On stage, she inhabited the role of a tired doctor and responded naturally to every question.
A strong actor can inhabit a role through believable reactions, not just accurate lines.
She inhabited the character so fully that even an improvised reply felt natural.

advanced-native-2343.text: At the photography exhibition, Mina gave only a short introduction. The work did the talking: visitors could see the care in every portrait.
After the trial, the results did the talking: the new system caught errors that earlier checks missed.
When a product works reliably, let the work do the talking.
The results do the talking when people can inspect clear evidence.

advanced-native-2418.text: Three witnesses changed their accounts after the fire. Once the reporter checked the phone records, she untangled the lies and saw how the false timelines supported one another.
The investigator untangled the lies by placing every claim beside the train records.
The reporter untangled the lies by checking each false timeline against the call logs.
To untangle their lies, the auditor compared the receipts with the bank records.

advanced-native-2435.text: Every Monday, Nora worked through the maintenance forms. New requests arrived before she finished the last pile, and by Friday it felt like a never-ending chore.
When I call the daily expense checks a never-ending chore, I mean each new claim creates another round of work.
A task feels like a never-ending chore when new work arrives before the last round is done.
Sorting the weekly returns became a never-ending chore, not just a long afternoon job.

advanced-native-2564.text: A library asked visitors to keep voices low, which protected quiet study. A proposal to record how often each visitor took a water break went much further and would police every habit.
A sensible rule can protect safety without trying to police every habit.
A school should address real harm rather than police every habit.
A rule that polices every habit can make a minor routine feel like misconduct.

advanced-native-2566.text: The community café once served only seated customers. When it began delivering hot drinks by bicycle, packaging safety entered the picture alongside taste and price.
Once the workshop moved outdoors, the weather entered the picture.
When tickets went digital, phone access entered the picture.
A new audience may make translation enter the picture.

advanced-native-2575.text: Hana enjoyed the robotics club, but she began refusing every family plan and stopping the music lessons she had valued. The club had become the centre of her world.
A hobby can become the centre of your world if it consistently pushes everything else aside.
She can love the band without making it the centre of her world; friends and study still need her time.
For a while, exams may be the centre of our world, but we should notice what we postpone.

advanced-native-2591.text: Iris set aside part of her earnings each month. When her washing machine broke, the saved amount covered most of the repair, giving her a small financial cushion.
Even a modest financial cushion can help with a sudden repair bill.
A financial cushion can soften a temporary loss of income.
The family kept a financial cushion for costs they could not predict.

advanced-native-2603.text: At a neighbourhood festival, a large sponsor paid for the stage and was offered first choice of advertisement space. Smaller donors noticed that money talks in such negotiations, although the sponsor did not control the whole programme.
When a donor’s large gift secures a meeting with organisers, money talks.
Money talks when a large sponsor receives more negotiating time.
Money talks, but funding alone does not guarantee the final vote.

advanced-native-2604.text: Residents obtained the full air-quality data before a planning meeting. They used it to challenge an incomplete report and secure another public hearing. Access to the data translated into power in the discussion.
Clear evidence translated into power when residents used it to win a review.
Reliable data can translate into power when a group uses them to negotiate.
Expertise translates into power only when it helps people act effectively.

advanced-native-2610.text: Lina’s craft guide was read by thirty club members. A community website featured it, and hundreds more visitors opened the page. The feature amplified her reach, although not every reader followed the guide.
A library newsletter amplified a poet’s reach by sharing her work with new readers.
A radio interview can amplify a volunteer’s reach beyond her own club.
The new page amplified their reach, though it did not guarantee agreement.

advanced-native-2611.text: The coach explained the warm-up steps before each practice. The players nodded but repeatedly began without warming up, so the advice seemed to go in one ear and out the other.
Without a follow-up task, the advice may go in one ear and out the other.
Safety advice should not go in one ear and out the other when the task begins.
The reminder went in one ear and out the other until the team used a checklist.

advanced-native-2614.text: Leo wants a second pair of expensive trainers this month, but the family has set aside money for his school trip. His mother says money does not grow on trees and asks him to choose which purchase matters more.
Money does not grow on trees, so we should keep the school-trip money before buying extra shoes.
Money does not grow on trees; let us budget for the rent before buying another lamp.
She reminded him that money does not grow on trees when he wanted a third tablet.

advanced-native-2618.text: After a tiring shift, May opened her phone to check bus times and saw a flash-sale alert from a shopping app. She bought three accessories she had not planned to get. Her friend said she often buys things on impulse when worn out.
She bought things on impulse after seeing the alert, though she had only opened her phone to check bus times.
She sometimes buys things on impulse when an online countdown appears.
Buying things on impulse is different from paying for an item already on your list.

advanced-native-2636.text: At the school fair, pupils may choose their own stall games, but they cannot use sharp tools without a teacher. The organiser says they have freedom up to a point and explains the safety limit.
Pupils can choose their fair games up to a point, but sharp tools still need teacher supervision.
The team may change the poster up to a point, but the safety notice must stay.
I agree with the plan up to a point; its cost still needs checking.

advanced-native-2637.text: Nora planned to keep her working headphones. After adverts promised better sound, she put a new pair on her shopping list. She says she was swayed by advertisements, though she has not bought them yet.
Nora was swayed by advertisements and considered new headphones, although her old pair still worked.
She was swayed by advertisements and added the museum to her weekend plans.
Seeing one advert does not prove a customer was swayed by advertisements.

advanced-native-2644.text: One librarian wants every room silent; another suggests allowing conversations everywhere. The team keeps quiet reading rooms and opens one discussion room. Their solution lies somewhere in the middle.
The library's plan lies somewhere in the middle: quiet rooms remain, but one room allows discussion.
A moderate rule may lie somewhere in the middle of two strict alternatives.
The answer was somewhere in the middle, with one quiet space and one discussion space.

advanced-native-2648.text: Rain stopped the community mural for six weeks. When the weather cleared, volunteers returned twice a week and completed the first new section. The mural project regained momentum, although the whole wall was not finished.
The mural project regained momentum when the volunteers returned and completed a new section.
The repair team regained momentum after the missing parts arrived.
Regular rehearsals helped the band regain momentum after the break.

advanced-native-2649.text: Grandpa owns newer cookbooks, but he keeps using a worn recipe book from his first café. He smiles when he opens its marked pages and says he has a soft spot for it, even though some recipes need updating.
Grandpa has a soft spot for his old recipe book because it reminds him of his first café.
My uncle has a soft spot for that old cinema because he went there as a child.
Having a soft spot for a café does not mean thinking every drink there is perfect.

advanced-native-2672.text: After sorting books for hours, Iris kept mixing up labels. She took a short break, drank water and returned more focused, finishing the shelf correctly. The break did her a world of good, though she still had more shelves to sort.
The short break did Iris a world of good: she returned focused and finished the shelf correctly.
Installing a gentle ramp did a world of good for visitors who had struggled with the entrance steps.
The quiet room did the group a world of good, although practice was still needed.

advanced-native-2646.text: At an annual harbour workshop, retired dockworkers demonstrate old cargo knots to apprentices. The practice belongs to the port's cultural memory, although the workers recall some steps differently.
The annual seed exchange is part of the village's cultural memory because families still explain it to newcomers.
Cultural memory is shared remembrance passed through a community, not proof that everyone recalls the past alike.
The old mural symbols live in the town's cultural memory because residents still explain them at gatherings.

advanced-native-2675.text: A school required every child to attend three paid rehearsals a week, even when families had transport problems. Parents called it a heavy-handed requirement because it left no room for exceptions.
The daily reporting rule feels like a heavy-handed requirement because the same details are submitted three times.
A heavy-handed requirement can discourage the very people it aims to help.
Before criticising a heavy-handed rule, explain which part is excessive and suggest a fairer alternative.

advanced-native-2681.text: The town recorded old folk songs and invited teenagers to arrange them for new instruments. The organiser said that keeping the songs alive did not mean freezing the past.
The choir keeps the original score but tries new arrangements, so it is not freezing the past.
Preserving an original does not always require freezing the past.
Avoid freezing the past: label new interpretations clearly so audiences can see both continuity and change.

advanced-native-2683.text: After ticket sales collapsed, the small theatre could pay staff only because a local fund covered its rent. The manager said it was on life support, not ready to operate independently.
The gallery is on life support because an emergency grant is covering its rent.
A service on life support is still operating, but only with critical outside help.
An institution on life support has survived temporarily; it has not necessarily recovered financially.

advanced-native-2689.text: The organiser thanked volunteers for their work but then cancelled the promised travel refunds. Her praise rang a little hollow when the volunteers had to pay their own fares.
The promise to help volunteers rings a little hollow after the travel fund is withdrawn.
Praise can ring hollow when practical support is withdrawn.
An apology can sound a bit hollow when the same harmful rule remains in place.

advanced-native-2698.text: A student copied a local illustrator’s poster for a paid event without asking. The organiser called it a victimless act, but the illustrator lost the fee she would normally charge.
Copying the photographer’s image for a paid poster is not a victimless act if she loses a licensing fee.
Before calling something a victimless act, check who may bear a real cost.
To challenge the label victimless act, name the affected person and the specific loss.

advanced-native-2703.text: The official archive stopped offering a legal download and gave no alternative. Some users began looking for the back door through unofficial sharing groups.
When the official replay vanished, some viewers started looking for the back door through private links.
Looking for the back door describes a workaround, not permission or safety.
People may look for the back door when a reliable official route disappears.

advanced-native-2708.text: The streaming service changed its payment rules and paid small musicians less for the same plays. The musicians lost out while the platform kept more revenue.
Small performers lose out when a new booking charge cuts their pay per ticket.
When someone loses out, name the benefit or advantage they no longer receive.
Creators lose out when a rule cuts their pay for the same work.

advanced-native-2718.text: Maya used to hear the song as a cheerful tune. After moving away from home, its lyrics about familiar streets hit differently: they now made her miss her neighbourhood.
The same childhood song hits differently after I moved away from my old neighbourhood.
A familiar song can hit differently when the listener’s life changes.
A story hits differently in a new personal context; the phrase does not automatically mean better or stronger.

advanced-native-2684.text: The older neighbours started a weekly storytelling night. Now teenagers are recording the stories and will carry it forward next year.
The community garden began with our grandparents, and we can carry it forward by teaching new families to plant.
A useful practice can be carried forward without copying every old detail.
When the founders leave, younger volunteers may carry it forward through fresh ideas.

advanced-native-2705.text: A student returned a borrowed camera one day late, and the club banned her from borrowing equipment for the whole year. The punishment does not fit the crime.
For one accidental form error, a permanent ban seems extreme; the punishment does not fit the crime.
When a minor first mistake brings a permanent ban, the punishment does not fit the crime.
A warning may be fairer if the punishment does not fit the crime.

advanced-native-2711.text: Both bus routes reach the library before nine. Route A has a slight edge on reliability because it was on time three more days last month, although Route B is cheaper.
The evening train has a slight edge on price, but the earlier service suits my schedule better.
The express train has a slight edge on journey time, but its seats are less comfortable.
One plan may have a slight edge on convenience without being best for everyone.

advanced-native-2724.text: Several neighbours felt lonely after the last local café closed, but none had said so publicly. A short poem gave voice to feelings they recognised at once.
The letter gives voice to feelings many volunteers share but rarely discuss.
A poem can give voice to feelings without claiming to speak for every reader.
To give voice to feelings, name the experience the words make recognisable.

advanced-native-2726.text: When Ella heard the old school bell recording, it took her straight back to mornings outside her first classroom. She could almost picture her friends queuing beside her.
That familiar whistle takes me straight back to my first swimming lessons.
A familiar sound can take you straight back to a specific time without literal travel.
Explain which cue takes them straight back and what memory it unlocks.

advanced-native-2737.text: The small jazz festival invited a singer known across the country. Even people who had never attended before recognised her as a big name in jazz.
The invited chef is a big name in regional cooking, so many visitors recognise her.
A big name is widely known in a field; it is not a promise of quality.
When calling someone a big name, identify the field and avoid guaranteed outcomes.

advanced-native-2739.text: The game publisher sold new character packs every month for years. Those recurring sales turned the franchise into a money-making machine, although the illustrators’ fees stayed fixed.
The yearly licence renewals have made the character brand a money-making machine for its owner.
A money-making machine earns repeatedly; one successful sale alone is not enough.
Calling a franchise a money-making machine does not prove every contributor receives the proceeds.

advanced-native-2741.text: After one televised hit, the singer was interviewed constantly. Over the next five years, the interviews became rare, and she slowly faded from the spotlight while continuing to record music.
The actor faded from the spotlight as national interviews grew less frequent.
To fade from the spotlight is to lose public attention gradually, not necessarily to stop working.
Evidence of fading from the spotlight should show a change in visibility over time.

advanced-native-2742.text: The television series sold well, but its junior writers were paid a fixed fee. They earned a living, yet they were not rolling in money as viewers assumed.
The show earns millions, but its junior staff are not rolling in money on fixed wages.
Not rolling in money denies great wealth; it does not mean earning nothing.
A project can succeed while its staff are not rolling in money.

advanced-native-2744.text: The evening library opens just after nearby workers finish their shifts, so they can visit without taking time off. Its new hours fit their routine like a glove.
The evening bus fits her work schedule like a glove because it leaves just after her shift.
When something fits a person like a glove, name the precise need it suits.
A service that fits one routine like a glove need not suit everyone.

advanced-native-2736.text: After a storm damaged the concert hall, separate day and night crews repaired the sound system for two days. They worked around the clock, but the hall was not ready to reopen yet.
The updates team works around the clock, while editors review submissions only in the daytime.
Teams can work around the clock in shifts; the phrase follows the work verb.
Saying people work around the clock does not prove round-the-clock supervision or a finished result.

advanced-native-2745.text: Pocket music players were everywhere during the early festival years. They had their moment in the sun, even though some collectors still use them today.
The neighbourhood choir had its moment in the sun, but a smaller audience still follows it.
A product can have its moment in the sun without vanishing when the trend fades.
Had a moment in the sun points to a limited period of attention, not literal sunlight.

advanced-native-2746.text: The store used to choose stock by the owner’s taste. Now customer orders decide which products are restocked, so demand calls the tune.
In the new timetable, passenger demand calls the tune more than the manager’s preference.
Who calls the tune is the person or factor that determines the decision, not merely contributes an idea.
Evidence that sales data calls the tune should show the final plan follows that data.

advanced-native-2753.text: The town invited artists from neighbouring regions to share techniques, while local craftspeople also presented their own work. The exchange made the festival more outward-looking.
The museum became more outward-looking by inviting curators from other towns to compare collections.
An outward-looking group engages with outside ideas without necessarily discarding its own traditions.
Use outward-looking when there is evidence of attention beyond the usual circle.

advanced-native-2754.text: The paper pass costs less at first, but the digital pass includes free changes and saves frequent travellers more over a month. For daily trips, the digital option comes out ahead.
The monthly pass comes out ahead for regular riders because free changes offset its higher starting price.
An option can come out ahead overall without winning on every single measure.
Before saying it comes out ahead, compare the costs or benefits that matter to the user.
