advanced-native-2758.text: The old theatre had worn seats, but it hosted the first play that Lina performed with her father. It still holds a special place in her memory.
The small rehearsal room holds a special place in my memory because our band first played there.
Something can hold a special place because of a memory, not because it is objectively best.
To explain why something holds a special place in memory, name the person or community and the experience behind it.

advanced-native-2760.text: The town-hall vote was broadcast live. Viewers watched each result arrive and the debate unfold in real time, without knowing the final count yet.
The audience watched the final round unfold in real time as judges announced each score.
An event can unfold in real time without happening quickly or having a known ending.
Unfolding in real time differs from an edited recap shown after the event.

advanced-native-2764.text: The underdog team has won two knockout matches and hopes to go all the way, although the semi-final is still ahead.
The young team hopes to go all the way, but its semi-final is not until next week.
Hoping to go all the way names a goal, not a title already won.
In sports, go all the way should be grounded in actual competition stages.

advanced-native-2766.text: A band from a quiet port town released a song that reached listeners across the region. The hit put their town on the map, even though visitor numbers had not been measured yet.
The choir’s national broadcast put its village on the map for listeners beyond the region.
Putting a place on the map means making it better known, not adding it to an actual map.
A film may put a town on the map without proving tourism has increased.

advanced-native-2768.text: The class heard three local songs during a ten-minute visit. It got a glimpse of the region’s musical tradition, not a complete history of it.
A short radio clip let listeners get a glimpse of the town’s storytelling tradition, not its whole history.
Getting a glimpse of something gives an initial impression, not complete expertise.
Music, stories or a brief demonstration can help visitors get a glimpse of a culture.

advanced-native-2774.text: The children did not know the words, but they recognised the tune in the waiting room and began to hum along softly.
The visitors hummed along when the pianist repeated the familiar theme.
Hum along means quietly following a tune, even if you do not know its words.
A silent listener is not humming along; the person must make the tune.

advanced-native-2775.text: The drums were fairly simple, but listeners kept repeating the short melody after the advert ended. That tune was a catchy hook.
The short piano phrase became a catchy hook that listeners repeated after the performance.
A catchy hook is a memorable musical fragment, not necessarily the entire chorus.
A strong beat can support a song without creating a catchy hook on its own.

advanced-native-2783.text: Many parents worked late, so the clinic added evening sessions and translated the forms. The team tried to meet families where they are.
The mentor met students where they were and built on the skills they already had.
Meet people where they are means starting from their current circumstances, not merely locating them on a map.
A plan can meet people where they are and still help them reach a more advanced goal.

advanced-native-2788.text: Both reading clubs meet on Fridays and have the same number of members. One discusses novels; the other writes its own stories. Activity is the real dividing line.
The real dividing line between the routes is reliability, not distance.
The real dividing line is the feature that materially separates two otherwise similar options.
The real dividing line need not be a visible line or a difference in every feature.

advanced-native-2791.text: After the memorial, the organiser played a gentle song rather than a triumphant march. Its quiet tone hit the right note for the gathering.
Her calm welcome hit the right note at the farewell, which was both grateful and sad.
Hit the right note means suit the situation’s mood, not simply sing an accurate pitch.
A response can hit the right note without being every listener’s favourite.

advanced-native-2799.text: Most families now receive school updates through the app, although printed notices remain available. App alerts lead the way in daily communication.
The city’s low-floor buses lead the way in accessible transport because other districts now follow their design.
Lead the way can describe the main current option without proving who first invented it.
A team may lead the way locally without having invented an idea first in the world.

advanced-native-2800.text: The arts centre used to attract most visitors to its hall. Now most participants attend its online workshops, though the hall remains open. The centre of gravity has shifted online.
The centre of gravity has shifted toward community clinics, although the main hospital remains open.
The centre of gravity has shifted when the main focus moves, even if old activity continues.
A change in colour alone does not show that the centre of gravity has shifted.

advanced-native-2803.text: Members can request a video lesson whenever they need one, and a tutor replies within a day. The platform offers on-demand lessons; its tutors cannot produce perfect answers on demand.
The library’s on-demand audiobook service lets members start a title when they choose, without a fixed broadcast schedule.
An on-demand service responds to a request rather than arriving on a fixed automatic schedule.
Staff may provide a service on demand without promising immediate or perfect results.

advanced-native-2806.text: The storm alert appeared on our phones in a flash after it was sent, but residents still needed time to reach shelter.
The revised map appeared in a flash, but the team still had to check its details.
In a flash describes a very fast event, not necessarily a fast whole process.
A result can appear in a flash and still require careful checking.

advanced-native-2809.text: The volunteers could prepare the contact list while the bulletin was delayed, but they sat around waiting instead.
We do not need to sit around waiting for the printed timetable when the live schedule is already online.
Sit around waiting suggests idleness, not every kind of patient waiting.
A team can avoid sitting around waiting by doing useful preparation before news arrives.

advanced-native-2813.text: Once the photo forum removed its approval step, hundreds of submissions arrived in one afternoon. The change opened the floodgates to new posts.
The new hashtag opened the floodgates to hundreds of neighbourhood stories in one afternoon.
Open the floodgates means allow a sudden large flow, not literally release water.
Opening the floodgates to posts says nothing by itself about their quality.

advanced-native-2815.text: The same unverified rumour appeared in five neighbourhood chats by noon. It had done the rounds before the council made any announcement.
The outdated route map had done the rounds in local chats, so the organiser sent everyone the revised version.
When news has done the rounds, it has circulated widely, whether or not it is accurate.
A story doing the rounds may need an update when the facts change.

advanced-native-2827.text: The report cites one anonymous post but no documents. The editor asks for records before publication: informed trust, not blind trust.
The coach read the injury report before approving the player’s return; she wanted informed judgement rather than blind trust.
Blind trust accepts a claim without enough checking.
Avoiding blind trust means using evidence, not accusing someone without proof.

advanced-native-2829.text: Mira knew the scholarship result on Monday but had promised to wait until Friday’s school notice. She sat on it in silence for four days.
She had good news on Tuesday but sat on it in silence until the team could hear it together on Friday.
To sit on the news means withhold it for a time, not physically sit on an object.
Someone may sit on it in silence to honour a promise; the phrase alone does not judge the choice.

advanced-native-2830.text: When the choir heard it had won, the singers smiled and then burst into cheers and applause. Their relief spilled over into applause.
At the reunion, joy spilled over into laughter when the old friends recognised one another.
Joy can spill over into laughter when it becomes openly expressed.
An emotion spilling over in one group does not prove everyone nearby shares it.

advanced-native-2833.text: The venue manager said the theatre could use the hall, but the agreement was not signed. The director wanted to celebrate yet said she did not want to jinx it.
The museum liked our proposal, but the final letter has not arrived, so I do not want to jinx it by announcing the exhibition yet.
People may say they do not want to jinx it before a hoped-for result is final.
Jinx it expresses a superstitious worry, not proof that words change a decision.

advanced-native-2834.text: Nina meant to wait until the rehearsal ended before mentioning the surprise guest, but she blurted it out when a classmate asked about the extra chair.
I knew the party location was a surprise, but when she asked about the map, I blurted it out before I could stop myself.
To blurt it out is to say it suddenly before filtering the words.
Blurting it out need not mean the speaker intended harm or that the news was false.

advanced-native-2851.text: The chart begins in June, yet the report discusses a whole year. Keep your eyes open for omitted months before trusting that trend.
Keep your eyes open for the small date printed under each image before you place the photographs in order.
Keep your eyes open for a clue means stay alert to find it.
Keeping your eyes open for missing context does not prove anyone intended to mislead.

advanced-native-2853.text: A report says an app doubled learning in one week, but its chart compares different classes. If you accept the conclusion with your brain switched off, you may miss the unfair comparison.
Read the figures with your brain switched off and you may miss that the survey asked only five people.
A brain switched off is a metaphor for failing to think critically during a task.
Reading an important claim with your brain switched off differs from resting after work.

advanced-native-2854.text: A major harvest failure in one exporting country may raise grain prices in neighbouring markets. Economic pressure can spill across borders even when the failed crops stay in one place.
The shipping delay began at one port, but its effects could spill across borders to neighbouring hospitals waiting for supplies.
Economic pressure may spill across borders through trade links.
Saying effects spill across borders does not prove all countries are affected equally.

advanced-native-2855.text: The class knows how buses work in its own district, but the teacher asks students to look beyond their own doorstep and compare two neighbouring cities.
To understand the housing debate, we looked beyond our own doorstep and compared our district with a neighbouring town.
Looking beyond your own doorstep adds perspectives outside your familiar local area.
Beyond our own doorstep need not mean abandoning local evidence or travelling abroad.

advanced-native-2856.text: The discussion group reads only its own neighbourhood chat and assumes every district has the same bus service. Without outside accounts, members may be living in a bubble.
If we rely only on our own forum, we may be living in a bubble and miss how other families use the service.
Living in a bubble can mean hearing too few voices from outside one’s group.
A person living in a bubble is not necessarily ignoring others on purpose.

advanced-native-2870.text: A reporter asked for her view without warning, and Maya formed an opinion on the spot. She later read the full report before publishing a final comment.
The facilitator answered the timetable question on the spot because the confirmed schedule was open in front of her.
Answering on the spot means answering immediately, not necessarily without evidence.
An answer given on the spot does not imply that all later analysis is complete.

advanced-native-2876.text: During the flood warning, the operations team could change bus routes and assign drivers without waiting for another committee. It had its hands on the wheel.
The local organisers kept their hands on the wheel by approving route changes themselves while accepting safety advice.
Hands on the wheel means direct control over decisions.
Keeping hands on the wheel does not guarantee every outcome will be perfect.

advanced-native-2878.text: A student-built water filter won an international prize, and several local papers put the achievement in prominent stories. The win made headlines.
The local robotics team made headlines after its rescue device won a national design prize.
Make headlines means become prominent news, not merely receive one passing mention.
Making headlines does not by itself prove the event was positive or the reports complete.

advanced-native-2879.text: By morning, the rail strike was discussed on local radio, television and several news sites. It was all over the news, though the talks were still continuing.
The election timetable was all over the news this week, so volunteers prepared answers to questions about the dates.
All over the news means wide coverage across outlets, not necessarily a lead headline everywhere.
A story all over the news can still have details that require checking.

advanced-native-2880.text: The city funds a free reading fair because everyone can enter. By the same token, a free science fair open to everyone deserves consideration under the same access rule.
The museum waives entry fees for school groups to improve access. By the same token, it could consider waiving fees for local youth clubs under the same access goal.
By the same token carries one relevant reason from one case to a comparable case.
By the same token does not mean the second application is automatically approved.

advanced-native-2882.text: The coordinator sent the outdated timetable to families. She said she would take responsibility for the mistake and send a corrected version that afternoon.
I sent the old form, so I will take responsibility for the mix-up and email the corrected link today.
Take responsibility for a mistake means accept accountability rather than shift blame.
The stage manager owned the mistake in the cue sheet, but the crew still needed to confirm the corrected sequence.

advanced-native-2912.text: For months, the teacher has praised pupils first whenever they show effort; she uses stickers only occasionally. Praise has become her go-to reward.
The club’s go-to reward for regular helpers is a handwritten note, while an annual certificate marks exceptional service.
A go-to reward is the usual first choice, not the only reward available.
Calling something a go-to reward does not show it works for everyone.

advanced-native-2916.text: When the new game began, the room filled with cheers for a few minutes. It brought a burst of excitement, though the pupils soon returned to their quiet projects.
The announcement of a surprise exhibit brought a burst of excitement before visitors returned to the guided tour.
A burst of excitement is intense but brief.
A burst of excitement does not by itself prove lasting success.

advanced-native-2919.text: The toy shop offered two sturdy puzzles that children could use repeatedly instead of a box of twenty flimsy prizes. The parent chose quality over quantity.
We chose quality over quantity: three small workshops with individual feedback instead of twelve crowded talks with no practice.
Quality over quantity prefers stronger outcomes, not merely a smaller count.
Choosing quality over quantity can still require enough places for the people served.

advanced-native-2922.text: The flashing toy thrilled Mei on Monday, but by Friday she ignored it although it still worked. Such gadgets can lose their charm quickly.
The app lost its charm for commuters once its daily tips began repeating, although every feature still worked.
Something can lose its charm when interest fades.
A toy can lose its charm while still working perfectly.

advanced-native-2927.text: Lena has practised alone for years. Playing her first concert for an audience is a pretty big deal for her, even if the hall is small.
Getting the first acceptance letter was a pretty big deal to Noor after months of applications.
A pretty big deal can be personally important without being famous.
Calling something a pretty big deal does not mean it is famous.

advanced-native-2937.text: At dinner, the old friends discussed stories Ava did not know and never asked her a question. She began to feel like a spare part in the room.
The organiser gave each newcomer a small role so no one would feel like a spare part during the workshop.
Feeling like a spare part describes exclusion, not a person’s worth.
Someone can feel like a spare part when no one gives them a chance to join.

advanced-native-2943.text: The neighbours began with introductions, then small conversations grew without anyone directing each minute. The gathering found its own rhythm.
After a short welcome, the reading circle found its own rhythm as members began responding to one another.
A group finds its own rhythm when interaction becomes natural.
A group can find its own rhythm while keeping sensible preparation.

advanced-native-2947.text: The hosts hired photographers to film every gift but barely spoke to the guest of honour. It felt like putting on a show rather than caring for her.
They stopped putting on a show for the cameras and spent the afternoon helping the families who had come.
Putting on a show focuses on impressing observers rather than the person served.
A lovely room is not automatically putting on a show.

advanced-native-2949.text: The couple could pay for a simple meal, but the luxury venue would require a loan they could not repay. They decided not to spend beyond their means.
They chose a modest celebration rather than spending beyond their means on a venue that required a loan.
Spending beyond their means exceeds their available resources.
An expensive choice is not necessarily beyond their means when they can afford it.

advanced-native-2950.text: After years apart, the whole family gathered to celebrate her graduation. For her, seeing everyone together was one of those once-in-a-lifetime moments.
Hearing her father sing with her children felt like a once-in-a-lifetime moment, even in their small kitchen.
A once-in-a-lifetime moment feels exceptionally rare to the person involved.
A once-in-a-lifetime moment need not require an expensive celebration.

advanced-native-2967.text: The community festival paid for ramps so wheelchair users could reach every activity. Many residents called the accessibility work money well spent.
Repairing the school lift was money well spent because pupils who use wheelchairs could finally reach the science rooms.
Money well spent needs a worthwhile result, not just a low price.
Call spending money well spent only when it brings a useful result.

advanced-native-2969.text: The head office announced new shop hours without speaking to staff who would work them. The schedule felt imposed from above.
The volunteers resisted the rota because it had been imposed from above without asking who could work weekends.
Imposed from above focuses on missing participation in a decision.
A plan imposed from above is not automatically proven ineffective.

advanced-native-2973.text: After graduation, Jo invited only her sister and three close friends to dinner. She wanted to celebrate with a small circle of people she trusted.
She told a small circle of trusted friends first, then shared the announcement with the whole class the next day.
A small circle refers to a few close people, not a seating arrangement.
Sharing first with a small circle does not imply dislike of others.

advanced-native-2977.text: On Fridays after work, the team goes to a small restaurant and eats dinner there. They usually eat out once a week.
We eat out at the corner café on Fridays, but tonight we are cooking at home.
Eat out means dining away from home, often indoors.
Buying takeaway to eat at home is usually not eating out.

advanced-native-2982.text: At a bookshop, a customer kept asking the owner why she had closed for a private family matter. She said she did not want to discuss it. He needed to mind his own business.
We should mind our own business and let Amira decide whether she wants to talk about her family.
Mind your own business means stop interfering in private affairs.
Mind your own business can sound blunt as a direct command.

advanced-native-2984.text: The first plan needs three vans, four suppliers and two booking systems. The second uses one supplier and one collection point, so it has fewer moving parts.
The clinic chose one shared appointment list because it had fewer moving parts than sending patients through three separate desks.
Fewer moving parts means fewer elements to coordinate.
A plan with fewer moving parts can still need careful checks.

advanced-native-2985.text: The team needs two temporary assistants this month while it recruits permanent staff. In the short term, extra support will keep the desk open.
In the short term, the centre will extend two volunteer shifts while it searches for a permanent receptionist.
In the short term identifies a near-future period, not a fixed number of days.
In the short term, a temporary fix can coexist with a permanent plan.

advanced-native-2996.text: Mira asked for advice about the poster, but she chose its final design herself rather than join the design team. For that small choice, she preferred to go solo.
I will go solo on the optional sketch, but we will still build the main model together.
Go solo identifies an action or decision handled independently.
Going solo on one task does not rule out teamwork elsewhere.

advanced-native-3006.text: We have chosen suppliers before, but this order serves twice as many customers. A lot more is riding on it this time.
The scholarship decision affects several students now, so a lot more is riding on it than in last year’s trial.
When more people depend on the result, a lot more is riding on it.
The device’s public launch is tomorrow; a lot more is riding on it than on last week’s staff rehearsal.

advanced-native-3014.text: Mina chose a local job ten years ago, although she also had an offer abroad. She sometimes thinks about the road not taken and wonders how life there might have been.
He stayed in his hometown to teach, but he occasionally wonders about the road not taken: studying abroad.
The road not taken can be worth imagining without making the chosen life a mistake.
She thinks about the road not taken when she remembers the offer she declined.

advanced-native-3040.text: After comparing three suggestions, the class came up with a plan to trial double-sided printing. They have not tested it yet.
The volunteers came up with a new timetable, but they still need to ask the families whether it works.
A team can come up with a promising idea before it knows whether the idea will work.
She came up with a clearer sign after asking visitors where they got lost.

advanced-native-3046.text: Researchers found shipping records that may reveal an unknown migration pattern. By checking them against older maps, they could push the boundaries of understanding.
New evidence about the river could push the boundaries of understanding, provided other teams can confirm the pattern.
Mapping a newly found cave may push the boundaries of understanding in geology without answering every question.
A surprising claim will not push the boundaries of understanding until researchers test it.

advanced-native-3047.text: The team is excited about the project, but that enthusiasm is leading to late work every night. A weekly schedule helps keep it in check without ending the project.
Competition can motivate the players, but the coach must keep it in check so they still support one another.
Book buying can be enjoyable, and a clear budget can keep it in check.
Their enthusiasm was strong, but the team kept it in check with a finish time.

advanced-native-3048.text: The forecast shows rain all week, but the organisers insist the outdoor fair will have perfect sunshine because they want it to. That is wishful thinking.
I hope the show succeeds, but predicting a full house without ticket data would be wishful thinking.
A hopeful forecast becomes wishful thinking when it ignores clear evidence.
Checking the bookings can keep a sales target from becoming wishful thinking.

advanced-native-3050.text: New attendance figures showed that the old class timetable no longer worked, but the organiser clung to it for dear life and refused to adjust a single session.
The first survey idea was useful, but we should not cling to it for dear life after the pilot shows a clearer method.
An old plan may be valuable; when facts change, we need not cling to it for dear life.
She clung to it for dear life even after the trial showed the design would fail.

advanced-native-3057.text: The appeal went online last month, but nobody replied and the group never mentioned it again. It sank without a trace.
The concert notice sank without a trace online, so the organisers shared a clearer version through local groups.
A good idea may sink without a trace if the intended audience never sees it.
The first appeal sank without a trace, so the team changed how it reached people.

advanced-native-3065.text: The poem ends with the speaker opening a door but never says who is outside. That detail may leave room for interpretation if readers support their ideas with lines from the poem.
The last scene leaves room for interpretation because we hear the door close but never learn who left.
Leave room for interpretation allows more than one supported reading.
Leaving room for interpretation does not make every guess valid.

advanced-native-3068.text: Studying an unfamiliar farming system made the class question its assumption that every community grows food the same way. The topic stretched the mind.
A visit to the old harbour stretched the mind because the pupils began asking how workers lived, not just naming the ships.
Stretch the mind means challenge existing ways of thinking.
A task that stretched the mind need not be finished or perfect.

advanced-native-3071.text: Adults saw an empty box as rubbish, but the children imagined a puppet stage. They looked at the familiar object with fresher eyes.
The visiting pupils saw the old courtyard with fresher eyes and suggested using its quiet corner for reading.
With fresher eyes means viewing familiar things less habitually.
Looking with fresher eyes can suggest changes that still need testing.

advanced-native-3072.text: Before asking for a story outline, the teacher gives pupils five quiet minutes to let their minds wander and notice any ideas that come up.
During the break, I let my mind wander and then wrote down one useful idea for the class display.
A short pause can let their minds wander before pupils choose a direction.
She lets her mind wander during the sketching break, then returns to the task.

advanced-native-3081.text: The committee announced the rota as final without consulting volunteers. Several of them dug their heels in and refused even to discuss swapping shifts.
After the club changed the plan without asking us, some members dug their heels in and would not consider a compromise.
The residents dug their heels in when the plan was imposed without consultation.
Asking for an explanation is not the same as digging your heels in.

advanced-native-3082.text: The figures need correcting, but let me speak to Nina privately first. I do not want her to lose face in front of the clients; then we can share the corrected slide.
I pointed out the mistake in private because I did not want my teammate to lose face in front of the whole group.
A private correction can help a speaker avoid losing face while still fixing an error.
He lost face when the mistake was announced to the whole audience.

advanced-native-3083.text: When the new cost figures arrived, the councillor changed her vote. She said that weighing better evidence was not the same as backing down to pressure.
We backed down on the price after the buyer threatened to leave, but we should not pretend the change came from new evidence.
The union backed down after the other side threatened to leave the talks.
Revising a claim because of strong evidence is not automatically backing down.

advanced-native-3084.text: The teacher spoke at the pupil for twenty minutes without pausing. After a while he shut down, avoided eye contact and stopped answering even simple questions.
When the interview turned into a long lecture, the trainee shut down and stopped answering, so I suggested a short break.
He shut down when the talk became a lecture and stopped answering.
A short thinking pause is not the same as shutting down under pressure.

advanced-native-3092.text: I used to think the night crew had little to do. Seeing their full shift at the hospital turned an old opinion on its head; now I understand how much they handle.
Meeting the residents turned an old opinion on its head: I had assumed nobody wanted the park, but dozens of families use it each day.
The shelter visit turned an old opinion on its head: Mara now welcomes stray dogs rather than fearing them.
Changing a minor detail is weaker than turning an old opinion on its head.

advanced-native-3093.text: After I began caring for my father, my inner compass shifted. I used to accept every late meeting; now time with family matters more when I choose projects.
Volunteering changed my inner compass: I still value a steady income, but meaningful community work now guides my choices too.
An inner compass is the set of values that guides a person’s choices.
Her inner compass changed after she began caring for her father.

advanced-native-3102.text: If you cannot access your account, the support desk should be your first port of call. They can check the basics and send you to a specialist if needed.
When I needed advice about the application, the library desk was my first port of call, and the staff directed me to the right form.
For simple account problems, the help desk is the first port of call.
Your first port of call may refer you elsewhere rather than solve every issue itself.

advanced-native-3109.text: The building committee plans to change how heating costs are shared. Current tenants have skin in the game because their monthly bills will change, so we should hear their views first.
The clinic patients have skin in the game because the proposed hours will determine when they can collect medicine.
People have skin in the game when a decision will directly affect them.
The bus users have skin in the game because the proposed cut changes their journey.

advanced-native-3111.text: Choosing the community awards is a minefield. The criteria, the number of winners and even the order of announcements could upset different teams, so let us consult them first.
The merger talks are a minefield because job titles, pay and reporting lines all matter to different teams.
A sensitive discussion can be a minefield when many details could cause conflict.
A minefield calls for care, but it does not mean the topic must be avoided forever.

advanced-native-3112.text: The comment thread has become a personal argument. I will steer clear of it and answer customer questions through the support channel instead.
I steered clear of the gossip at work and asked the manager directly about the new rota.
Steer clear of a hostile argument when another channel can handle the real issue.
She steered clear of the rumour and checked the figures herself.

advanced-native-3113.text: If we move one group of volunteers to the front, we may open a can of worms. Other teams will ask why they were placed behind and whether the priority rule has changed.
Allowing one late entry opened a can of worms because other teams then questioned the deadline and the judging rules.
A narrow exception can open a can of worms when many related rules are unclear.
The refund question opened a can of worms about earlier payments.

advanced-native-3116.text: The sharing session was relaxed until someone joked about Lina’s mistake on stage. That remark soured the mood, and the group fell quiet.
The announcement itself was necessary, but the mocking tone soured the mood and made volunteers reluctant to speak.
A guest’s mocking comment about someone’s accent can sour the mood at a team dinner.
The cruel joke soured the mood and left the group silent.

advanced-native-3124.text: First the committee banned all visits to the garden. After complaints, it allowed visitors in at any hour with no limit. It swung from one extreme to another instead of trying a measured schedule.
The council swung from one extreme to another when it moved from no street stalls to unlimited permits overnight.
A policy can swing from one extreme to another when it replaces a total ban with no limits.
After an absolute ban, the group may swing the other way and reject every limit instead of choosing a workable balance.

advanced-native-3126.text: There are twenty workshop places. We will offer them on a first-come, first-served basis: complete registrations are processed in the order we receive them, until all places are filled.
The reading club offered its limited seats on a first-come, first-served basis and closed registration once the room was full.
Limited places may be offered on a first-come, first-served basis.
On a first-come, first-served basis, the earliest complete applications receive the places.

advanced-native-3129.text: I sent the completed application and all the documents yesterday. The office said it would reply next week, so for now I can only sit tight and hope for the best.
We have sent the final design to the judges, so we will sit tight and hope for the best until the results come out.
After completing the application, we may sit tight and hope for the best.
Do the required work first; only then sit tight and hope for the best.

advanced-native-3132.text: I was irritated when Ken interrupted me again, but I managed to keep a lid on it. I answered the question calmly and asked to finish my point.
I was annoyed by the delay, but I kept a lid on it and asked the receptionist for an updated time.
She kept a lid on it when irritation rose during the meeting.
He felt angry but chose to keep a lid on it and ask a clear question.

advanced-native-3134.text: The same loud warning has played every few minutes for an hour. People on the platform keep looking up and complaining. It is getting on everyone’s nerves.
The repeated reminder got on everyone’s nerves because it interrupted every speaker during the rehearsal.
A sound that repeats all evening can get on everyone’s nerves.
The long delay got on everyone’s nerves when no update arrived.

advanced-native-3136.text: The refund delay was frustrating, but the customer began shouting, stamping a foot and interrupting every answer. He threw a tantrum instead of explaining the receipt problem calmly.
The guest threw a tantrum when the table was unavailable, but the staff still checked the reservation record.
A valid complaint does not justify throwing a tantrum at staff.
He threw a tantrum by shouting and refusing to hear a reply.

advanced-native-3139.text: Ordering takes two taps, and delivery comes straight to the door. Many customers favour those features even while comparing prices. Their choices show how convenience-driven shopping has become.
The library introduced self-service returns after noticing a convenience-driven shift toward shorter visits.
Convenience-driven choices are shaped mainly by ease or saved effort.
The new ordering service reflects convenience-driven shopping habits.

advanced-native-3141.text: Messages arrived during breakfast, every meeting ran into the next, and I ate lunch while answering alerts. The whole day felt like life on fast-forward.
Since the project began, my week has felt like life on fast-forward, with meetings, alerts and travel leaving almost no quiet time.
Constant alerts can make a whole week feel like life on fast-forward.
Life on fast-forward describes a sustained rush, not one hurried trip.

advanced-native-3154.text: We have changed the volunteer rota three times without explaining why. People are still helping, but repeated confusion can drain goodwill and make them less willing to cover extra shifts.
Changing the plan every week drained goodwill among the organisers, even though most of them continued to help.
Repeated broken promises can drain goodwill even before people stop helping.
The unclear rules drained goodwill and reduced volunteers’ willingness to cover extra shifts.

advanced-native-3155.text: When the appointment changed again, I felt my voice getting sharp. I was losing my cool, so I stopped for a moment before calling back.
I was losing my cool when the bus was cancelled again, but I paused and asked for another route.
She was losing her cool when her voice became sharp.
I lost my cool briefly, then paused before answering.

advanced-native-3159.text: Mei was still explaining the timetable when Leo cut in impatiently and said, “Can you get to the point? We are running late.” The chair asked Leo to let Mei finish.
Nora cut in impatiently while I was explaining the route, so I asked her to let me finish the safety instructions.
He cut in impatiently before she had completed her explanation.
Wait for a pause rather than cutting in impatiently.

advanced-native-3162.text: The clinic has moved my appointment three times this month. I have not cancelled it, but my patience is being tested. I will ask for a firm date before arranging another day off.
After three cancellations, my patience is being tested, but I will ask for a confirmed date before deciding what to do.
Their patience is being tested by repeated delays.
Her patience was being tested, but she still asked calmly for a firm date.

advanced-native-3165.text: We carried the archive boxes up four flights of stairs for almost six hours. By the end, the move felt like a test of endurance, but we finished the last shelf together.
Cataloguing the donated books all weekend was a test of endurance, so we took turns and kept regular breaks.
The long climb was a test of endurance rather than speed.
Several hours of careful work can become a test of endurance.

advanced-native-3169.text: I felt angry when I read the criticism, but I did not want to react on impulse. I put my phone down for ten minutes, then wrote a question about the point I did not understand.
I nearly reacted on impulse to the complaint, but I read it again and asked one calm question first.
Pause before reacting on impulse to a difficult message.
She reacted on impulse and later reconsidered her decision.

advanced-native-3175.text: Ava is even-tempered. In close matches, she listens before answering, and when teammates disagree, she helps them discuss the next move without raising her voice. That is why I trust her to coordinate the group.
Our captain is even-tempered: she remains calm during close games and hears both sides of an argument.
She is even-tempered when a discussion becomes tense.
One polite reply alone does not prove someone is even-tempered.

advanced-native-3176.text: Noah is skilled at repairing equipment, but he can be hot-headed when colleagues question his work. Twice this month he snapped at them before hearing their concerns, and later he apologised to the team.
He can be hot-headed when a plan changes, but asking for a pause has helped him listen before replying.
He can be hot-headed when teammates question his plan.
One firm, well-considered reply does not make someone hot-headed.

advanced-native-3184.text: I want the playground open by Friday, but not at any cost. The safety checks are required, and if they take another day, we must change the opening date.
The museum wanted to reopen quickly, but not at any cost; it waited until the damaged stairway was repaired.
A deadline should not be met at any cost if safety is at stake.
Spending a small agreed amount is not the same as acting at any cost.

advanced-native-3186.text: The venue cancelled our booking, and the bus company cannot bring the students to the replacement site. Our plan is falling apart. We need to decide whether to postpone the trip.
Our project plan is falling apart: the sponsor withdrew, and the only suitable room is no longer available.
The event plan is falling apart because its essential arrangements have failed.
A small change with a workable backup does not mean a plan is falling apart.

advanced-native-3198.text: I know you are tired of band practice, Nia. I have your best interests at heart, so I suggest trying the shorter rehearsal plan for two weeks, then deciding whether to stay. Please tell me if the stress is still too much.
My mentor has my best interests at heart: she asked about my goals before suggesting a lighter course load.
She has your best interests at heart, even if you want to discuss her advice.
A mentor can have your best interests at heart without being right about every suggestion.

advanced-native-3199.text: Leo asked if his application letter was ready. I could have said it was perfect, but I wanted to tell him what he needs to hear: his experience paragraph needs one concrete example. He still has time to add it.
I told her what she needed to hear about the missing evidence, then helped her find a clearer example.
Before you commit to a weak plan, invite someone you trust to tell you what you need to hear.
She told him what he needed to hear and offered a practical next step.

advanced-native-3200.text: Ruth has been around the block. She has helped three teams through timetable changes, so I will ask what worked before. I will still check whether her advice fits our team.
My aunt has been around the block in small business, so I value her advice while checking it against my own plan.
She has been around the block and can share practical lessons.
Having been around the block does not make every suggestion right for a new setting.

advanced-native-3205.text: We could add another hour of study tonight, but let us take the long view. If you keep one evening free each week, you may be able to study steadily through the whole term without becoming exhausted.
The committee took the long view and kept basic training, even though cancelling it would have saved money this month.
Taking the long view means weighing future effects alongside today’s cost.
They took the long view without ignoring the immediate budget.

advanced-native-3211.text: I promised to cover the morning book-sale shift, and I will keep my word. I have booked an early bus, even though I would rather sleep in tomorrow.
I promised to return the borrowed camera on Friday, and I kept my word even though I had to leave work early.
She kept her word and delivered what she had promised.
To keep your word, first be clear about what you agreed to do.

advanced-native-3213.text: Kai can leave the company, but the first draft of his goodbye email calls every colleague useless. I told him not to burn bridges: explain the handover clearly and raise specific complaints separately.
I was angry about the change, but I did not burn bridges; I explained the issue privately and finished the handover.
A respectful handover helps you avoid burning bridges.
He burned bridges by insulting former colleagues in public.

advanced-native-3219.text: We are writing down the repair steps today. If a new team faces the same fault down the line, these notes may help them solve it faster. I do not know when that will happen.
A clear handover may save time down the line when another volunteer takes over the project.
The notes may be useful down the line.
Down the line names a later time, not a guaranteed date.

advanced-native-3228.text: At first I thought nobody wanted to help, but several volunteers told me they could not see which shifts were open. That is where the shoe pinches: the sign-up page hides the vacancies. We will make them visible.
We finally found where the shoe pinches: the booking form conceals the open times, so visitors assume the room is full.
A careful check can reveal where the shoe pinches.
Knowing the symptom is not the same as knowing where the shoe pinches.

advanced-native-3230.text: Our mentor’s advice was down-to-earth. Instead of asking us to redesign the whole garden, she suggested measuring the sunny patch today and using the seeds we already have for one test bed.
The coach gave down-to-earth advice: practise one short drill daily and check progress at the end of the week.
Down-to-earth advice offers a workable next step.
Her down-to-earth plan used resources the group already had.

advanced-native-3234.text: Eva did not get the place she hoped for. I cannot change the result, but I can be a shoulder to cry on. I told her I would listen if she wanted to talk, and we sat together for a while.
After the disappointing news, I needed a shoulder to cry on, and my cousin listened without rushing me.
A shoulder to cry on offers comfort, not a guaranteed solution.
He needed a shoulder to cry on after the setback.

advanced-native-3235.text: The exhibition team rejected my first poster and explained that the text was too small. I was disappointed, but I will not throw in the towel. I will enlarge the text and submit a revision tomorrow.
I nearly threw in the towel after the first rejection, but the feedback showed one change I could make before trying again.
One setback need not make a learner throw in the towel.
Pausing for safety is different from throwing in the towel.

advanced-native-3236.text: For the third time this month, delivery boxes have blocked the emergency exit. Enough is enough. We will record the dates and ask the building manager for a written safety plan.
After three missed safety checks, we said enough is enough and asked for a written inspection schedule.
After repeated failures, enough is enough can introduce a clear boundary.
Enough is enough; we need a specific plan to stop the problem.

advanced-native-3237.text: The evening course sounds useful, but I want to check its timetable against my work hours. The reply is due next week, so I will sleep on it and decide tomorrow morning.
The offer is appealing, but I will sleep on it because I have until Friday to decide and still need to check the timetable.
If the decision can wait, sleep on it before replying.
They slept on it and considered the offer again the next day.

advanced-native-3245.text: First, write down why you chose each answer. Then compare your reasons with the evidence in the passage. That review can sharpen your judgment next time; it does not mean every future answer will be right.
Comparing our forecast with the actual turnout sharpened our judgment about which event times work best.
Checking missed clues can sharpen our judgment.
The review sharpened her judgement without guaranteeing future perfection.

advanced-native-3273.text: The student entered the wrong return date, so another borrower got wrong information. We corrected it and found the calendar check was skipped. We turn mistakes into learning moments by checking dates before saving next time.
The team turned a mistake into a learning moment by correcting the timetable and adding a second check before publication.
We turn mistakes into learning moments when we repair harm and change the next process.
The teacher turned a mistake into a learning moment by practising the missed check.

advanced-native-3274.text: The child put the wrong start time on the notice. We can hear their explanation without letting children off the hook: they can correct the notice and tell families about the change.
The coach did not let the player off the hook after the missed handover; the player still contacted the waiting team and apologised.
A calm conversation and a fair repair task can coexist without letting children off the hook.
They did not let the volunteer off the hook, but chose a fair way to repair the error.

advanced-native-3280.text: The assistant skipped a safety check and damaged a projector. He blames an unclear checklist, though he saw the procedure demonstrated that morning. He has not reported the damage or arranged a repair. He is hiding behind excuses.
She was hiding behind excuses after losing the booking email, until she called the venue and corrected the date.
Do not hide behind excuses when a needed correction is possible.
He stopped hiding behind excuses and fixed the notice.

advanced-native-3283.text: The archive coordinator was assigned to check image permissions. She passed the request between teams without naming an owner. When she stopped dodging responsibility, she verified the permissions and corrected the record.
The editor stopped dodging responsibility for the missing credit and sent the corrected caption to the designer.
Dodging responsibility leaves an assigned task without an owner.
The stage manager stopped dodging responsibility and confirmed the missing sound check.

advanced-native-3286.text: After our argument, I realised I had shared Mei’s private message with others. I apologised, asked the group to delete the screenshot, and promised not to share her messages again. I am trying to make amends, though Mei may need time.
I made amends for the false accusation by correcting the meeting record and apologising to the colleague I had blamed.
Making amends means repairing harm, not demanding forgiveness.
After damaging the borrowed book, Jo tried to make amends by arranging a replacement.

advanced-native-3306.text: I opened my laptop to finish the application, but answered every new notification first. At five o’clock the form was still blank. I had drifted through the day without deciding what mattered most.
I was drifting through the day until I listed the two urgent calls and finished the first one before opening my messages.
A chosen rest day differs from drifting through the day when an important task remains.
Without a plan for the grant application, Priya drifted through the day answering minor emails.

advanced-native-3319.text: The festival plan assigns every volunteer a task every ten minutes. If a guest needs extra help, no one is free to respond. The schedule is squeezing out flexibility; we need some unassigned blocks.
Booking every room all afternoon squeezed out flexibility when one class needed to move during repairs.
A schedule can squeeze out flexibility if it leaves no room for reasonable changes.
Booking every studio hour squeezed out flexibility when a repair was needed.

advanced-native-3327.text: The library display opens Friday. Captions are done, and Thursday printing can finish the labels. The project is on track for opening, although we still need to confirm the final delivery.
Checking the supplier’s delivery date helped keep the project on track for its Friday opening.
Progress checks can keep a project on track without guaranteeing completion.
Confirming the supplier’s delivery date kept the project on track for opening.

advanced-native-3328.text: Rina is goal-oriented. Before each community event she defines one measurable aim, assigns tasks that support it, and checks what worked afterwards. She enjoys planning, but the goal guides the plan.
Our goal-oriented organiser set a recycling target and checked weekly collections before changing the pickup plan.
Goal-oriented planning ties actions and review to a clear aim.
Our goal-oriented editor sets a publication date and checks each milestone.

advanced-native-3329.text: The two lab technicians are training new staff and repairing equipment this month. They already have a lot on their plate. Before asking them to run the open day, we should ask what shift they could manage.
With weekend shifts and a family move, Dev has a lot on his plate, so the centre offered him a smaller optional role.
If someone has a lot on their plate, invite them thoughtfully rather than assuming.
Nora has a lot on her plate while caring for her father and covering weekend shifts.

advanced-native-3332.text: The students are worried about changing trains on their first trip. I sent the platform numbers and a simple transfer map to calm their nerves. I cannot promise there will be no delays, but they now know where to go.
The organiser shared the room number and check-in steps to calm our nerves before the unfamiliar event.
Useful details can calm their nerves without removing every uncertainty.
The rehearsal map calmed her nerves before she entered the unfamiliar theatre.

advanced-native-3334.text: Mara planned the school exhibition down to the last detail: she labelled each display cable, wrote an access route for deliveries, and assigned a backup key holder. The opening plan is thorough, though it may still need changes.
The team planned the concert down to the last detail, including labelled cables and a backup contact for the performers.
Planning down to the last detail covers small practical points.
For the charity dinner, Ana checked every place card down to the last detail.

advanced-native-3336.text: Our group has booked the return train, but Saturday’s weather may change our walking plan. We will play things by ear: if rain begins, we can visit the museum instead.
We will play things by ear after the morning walk, choosing an indoor stop if the forecast turns wet.
To play things by ear is to adapt the open parts of a plan.
With the outdoor court still wet, the players will play it by ear after lunch.

advanced-native-3338.text: Before the nature walk, a safe path was mapped out in advance. We checked bridge times, marked two rest stops and named a meeting point. If the bridge closes, we will use the approved alternative.
The loading plan was mapped out in advance, with entrance times and a backup lift confirmed before the move.
A route mapped out in advance gives the group a clear starting plan.
The gallery move was mapped out in advance, including lift access and a backup entrance.

advanced-native-3339.text: A local gallery offered me a short design job after another artist withdrew. I checked the deadline against my current work and accepted it. As a freelancer, I take opportunities as they come, but I do not accept every invitation blindly.
The photographer takes opportunities as they come, but checks each new commission against work already promised.
Taking opportunities as they come still requires checking commitments.
The illustrator takes opportunities as they come, after checking that each new job fits her deadlines.

advanced-native-3359.text: Residents say the crossing light changes too quickly. A council officer will look into the report by checking timing records and observing busy-hour crossings. No signal change has been approved yet.
The team will look into the missing deliveries by comparing signed receipts with the dispatch list.
To look into a report is to investigate it, not to assume it is true.
The librarian will look into the missing-book report before charging a replacement fee.

advanced-native-3377.text: I bought the expensive jacket on impulse because everyone praised it. A week later it still fits, but the purchase feels hollow: the excitement faded, and I did not need another coat.
The quick online praise felt hollow to Mina once she realised she had not shared credit with the rest of the team.
Something can feel hollow even when it looks successful from outside.
The trophy felt hollow when the captain realised two helpers had not been thanked.

advanced-native-3380.text: The draft budget gives seventy percent to transport; meals and materials share the remaining thirty percent. It is heavily tilted towards transport. Long distances may justify this, but we must check the other needs.
The grant is heavily tilted towards transport, so the committee checked whether the smaller meal and material budgets still met essential needs.
Heavily tilted towards describes an uneven share, not automatically an unfair one.
The training week is heavily tilted towards lectures, leaving little time for practice.

advanced-native-3385.text: These families saved from weekend shifts to buy a laptop. It is hard-earned money, so we compared repair cover and battery life as well as the sale price.
They compared the repair warranty before spending their hard-earned money on the second-hand bicycle.
Hard-earned money deserves a value check, not an automatic refusal to spend.
Her hard-earned money paid for a camera after she checked the warranty.

advanced-native-3391.text: The café pairs Cantonese milk tea with French pastries and uses old Hong Kong tiles beside a European-style counter. Its East-meets-West identity is visible in both the menu and the room, not only in its name.
The gallery’s East-meets-West identity appears in its local ink paintings beside European printmaking tools.
An East-meets-West identity needs visible, specific elements from both sides.
The exhibit’s East-meets-West identity appears in its paired textiles and furniture.

advanced-native-3393.text: The lane market has hand-painted signs, stalls that have been run by the same families for years, and vendors who remember regular shoppers. It is full of character, though the narrow path can be crowded.
The tiny theatre is full of character, with painted seat numbers and programmes made by local artists.
A place full of character has distinctive details you can name.
The old cinema was full of character, with handmade posters and carved doors.

advanced-native-3403.text: The plot has had no rain for weeks, and its tank is empty. Asking for the same water-heavy crop would mean squeezing water from a stone. We must secure irrigation or choose another crop.
Expecting the workshop to run without required safety equipment would mean squeezing water from a stone.
Without the essential resource, the demand can feel like squeezing water from a stone.
Demanding a concert without a sound system would mean squeezing water from a stone.

advanced-native-3405.text: Our emergency store contains safe drinking water and batteries. When a crisis hits and power fails across the district, those supplies can support residents until deliveries resume. We still have to check expiry dates.
When a crisis hits and ferries stop, the island’s stored medicine can cover urgent needs until transport resumes.
Preparation matters most when a crisis hits and normal systems fail.
Stored supplies can help when a crisis hits the island.

advanced-native-3406.text: Ferries stopped, but a temporary boat delivered bread and medicine to island shops and the clinic. That basic supply helped keep a society on its feet while travel remained difficult.
A reliable cold-chain network helped keep a society on its feet by delivering insulin to clinics during the port closure.
Essential food and health services can keep a society on its feet during disruption.
Reliable water delivery helped keep a society on its feet after the flood.

advanced-native-3407.text: Our committee has debated suppliers for a week. Now, when push comes to shove and the clinic must order tomorrow, we need one company that can deliver the medicine reliably. Price still matters, but delivery cannot be guessed.
When push comes to shove and the grant form is due, the team must choose which two projects it can actually fund.
When push comes to shove, discussion has to become a decision.
When push comes to shove, the organisers must confirm the accessible hall.

advanced-native-3410.text: Our workshop repairs bicycles well but now wants to add phone screens and appliance wiring. No one is trained for either new service. Without training, it risks being a jack of all trades and master of none.
A tiny repair shop offering six complex services without training risks being a jack of all trades and master of none.
Breadth helps, but without depth a group risks being a jack of all trades and master of none.
The agency hired a specialist rather than risk being a jack of all trades and master of none.

advanced-native-4237.text: Mia said the river was cleaner this year. Instead of correcting her, the tutor asked which measurements she compared and whether both samples were from the same season. His probing questions exposed a gap in her evidence.
The tutor asked probing questions about Mia's measurements instead of supplying the conclusion.
A thoughtful interviewer asks probing questions without assuming an answer.
Probing questions can help a student explain the evidence behind a claim.

advanced-native-4680.text: The group stayed at one hotel near the bus station for a week. Each morning they collected route maps there before visiting a different coastal town, then returned to plan the next day. The hotel became their base camp.
The hotel became our base camp: each morning we set out from there and returned to plan the next trip.
The community hall was our base camp for visits to three nearby villages.
A base camp can be a hotel when teams use it to plan and launch daily outings.

advanced-native-3412.text: The island once imported spare parts and exchanged farming methods with nearby ports. After the trade ban, neither goods nor technical advice could enter. Its economy became closed off, making repairs harder.
A region can become closed off when both trade routes and technical exchanges are cut, leaving clinics short of replacement parts.
An economy is closed off when important outside links stop, not merely when one tariff exists.
The remote port became closed off after losing both trade and training links.

advanced-native-3413.text: The new grant rule would exclude small neighbourhood groups from applying at all. It could shut the door on collaboration with organisations that know local needs. A lower-cost application route would keep that partnership possible.
A blanket ban might shut the door on joint lessons with the museum, even though supervised visits could meet the safety rule.
A ban may shut the door on cooperation if no fair route remains.
The revised policy kept access open instead of shutting the door on local groups.

advanced-native-3419.text: A large chain rented most stalls and cut prices. Two local repair shops lost customers; one gave up its lease. With affordable space shrinking, independent sellers risk being squeezed out.
Independent bookshops may be squeezed out when rising rent and exclusive leases leave them no affordable premises.
Being squeezed out requires real loss of room to operate, not merely a new rival.
The repair stall was squeezed out after affordable units disappeared.

advanced-native-3421.text: A port computer failure stopped containers for three days. Factories missed parts, and shops in several regions ran short of stock. The failure sent shockwaves far and wide through the supply network, beyond the port itself.
The rail shutdown sent shockwaves through the food network as farms, warehouses and city markets all missed deliveries.
A failure sends shockwaves when consequences spread through connected systems.
The warehouse fire sent shockwaves through regional food deliveries.

advanced-native-3429.text: The port delay added storage fees. One firm has enough cash reserves to cover three extra months, while the smaller supplier would struggle after two weeks. The larger firm has deep pockets, but it still wants the delay resolved.
The builder has deep pockets compared with its rivals, with cash set aside for months of unexpected repair work.
Deep pockets means relative financial capacity, not an endless budget.
The clinic with deep pockets still checked the storage bill.

advanced-native-3431.text: The lease offers tenants a monthly rent rebate, but adds a compulsory service fee nearly equal to that rebate. That lease gives with one hand and takes with the other; tenants should compare the final monthly bill.
The subsidy gave with one hand and took with the other: it lowered tuition but added a mandatory course fee of similar size.
An offer can give with one hand and take with the other when a new cost offsets the benefit.
The revised grant gave with one hand and took with the other through a matching fee.

advanced-native-3432.text: One server links growers, warehouses and shops. If that part shorts out, orders miss the warehouse and suppliers elsewhere suffer. Here 'shorts out' is a workflow metaphor, not an electrical fault.
When the shared dispatch system shorted out, four warehouses missed orders and moved to their backup lists.
If a shared link shorts out, connected teams may need a backup path.
The booking link shorted out, so staff used the paper list.

advanced-native-3435.text: After a ten-hour shift, Nia still had to finish an urgent incident report. Her manager then asked her to prepare tomorrow’s presentation tonight. That was one job too many, so they reassigned the slides to a rested colleague.
After managing the late delivery and the safety check, preparing another full briefing was one job too many for the coordinator.
One job too many depends on present capacity, not laziness.
The extra briefing was one job too many after a full shift.

advanced-native-3486.text: The transport committee asked wheelchair users to review a proposed bus route and suggest changes before it was approved. They now have a seat at the table.
Parents had a seat at the table when the school asked them to review the draft timetable before voting.
Have a seat at the table means genuine inclusion in a discussion.
Having a seat at the table does not guarantee veto power.

advanced-native-3495.text: Across a crowded station, a bright blue platform sign caught Nia’s eye. She followed it only after checking that its arrow pointed to the platform she needed.
The blue sign caught my eye beside the crowded noticeboard, so I stopped to read its opening hours.
Catch your eye means attract visual attention.
Something that caught your eye is not necessarily high quality.

advanced-native-3501.text: A gym ad promised one month free, but the fine print limited it to new members who signed a year-long contract.
The fine print says the free workshop is for first-time visitors, so regular members must book the paid session.
The fine print can narrow an attractive headline.
Read the fine print before judging an offer.

advanced-native-3508.text: On the museum site, choose Visit, then Access, then Captions; the transcript for today’s audio tour is only a few clicks away, though you still need to open and read it.
Once you open the course site, you are only a few clicks away from the timetable; check which week applies after you find it.
Only a few clicks away describes easy online access.
Only a few clicks away does not mean the task is already complete.

advanced-native-3510.text: The catalogue gave no date for the first exhibition, so the archivists had to dig through books of local records to find it.
We dug through books of shipping records for the vessel’s first voyage, but the date is still uncertain.
Dig through books means search printed volumes persistently.
People can dig through books without yet finding a certain answer.

advanced-native-3512.text: A broad search for local air quality produced a flood of information, but the class still had to check which figures came from reliable sources.
The new archive released a flood of information, so the researchers sorted its records by date before making claims.
A flood of information refers to quantity, not accuracy.
Sort a flood of information before using it as evidence.

advanced-native-3521.text: Mira leafed through the magazine before choosing an article; she looked at headings but had not read any story fully.
I leafed through the exhibition catalogue and marked two photographs to study more carefully later.
Leaf through means browse pages for an overview.
Leafing through a guide does not verify every detail.

advanced-native-3525.text: At the community fair, booth signs were missing and visitors wandered into several queues at once. The entrance became a free-for-all until volunteers added directions.
The public forum descended into a free-for-all after speakers ignored the time limit and shouted across the room.
A free-for-all is a disorderly situation without effective rules.
A situation may descend into a free-for-all, or be a bit of a free-for-all.

advanced-native-3529.text: A customer challenged a refund decision, then sent threats to the clerk’s personal account. The threats crossed the line.
The moderator crossed a line by mocking a speaker’s disability; disagreeing with the proposal itself would have been fair.
Cross the line means go beyond acceptable conduct.
A school may debate many rules, but some lines cannot be crossed when pupils’ private records are involved.

advanced-native-3547.text: The manager scheduled double shifts for weeks with no recovery days. By the final weekend, the kitchen team had been run into the ground.
The volunteers were run into the ground by six weeks of late-night sorting with no rest days.
Run someone into the ground means overwork them to exhaustion.
Do not praise a schedule that runs workers into the ground.

advanced-native-3548.text: The new policy requires five signatures to replace a broken pen. It risks tying every workplace in knots without improving safety.
The four-approval rule is tying the repair team in knots: a loose door handle now waits three days for a signature.
Tie a workplace in knots means impede work through excessive complexity.
A useful safety check need not tie a team in knots.

advanced-native-3550.text: Before the cousins shared a room, the family agreed on ground rules: ask before borrowing things and keep lights low after ten.
The art club set ground rules for sharing tools: return brushes clean and ask before using someone else’s paint.
Ground rules establish basic expectations for conduct.
Useful ground rules say what people should actually do.

advanced-native-3555.text: During the museum tour, two visitors disappeared into their phones and missed the guide’s instruction to meet at the east exit.
During the picnic, two cousins disappeared into their phones and missed the call to take a group photo.
Disappear into your phone describes lost attention to surroundings.
Someone can disappear into their phone without literally vanishing.

advanced-native-3557.text: Lunch-box sticker styles come and go, but pupils always need labels they can read quickly when collecting their food.
Social-media challenges come and go, but the club still checks safety before joining any new one.
Come and go describes trends that rise and fade over time.
A trend can come and go while a basic need persists.

advanced-native-3559.text: After the budget cut was announced, the meeting fell quiet. The experienced chair paused to read the room before bringing up the next item.
I read the room when the parents stopped smiling and asked about safety, so I answered their concern before showing the fun activities.
Read the room before choosing the tone or timing of a message.
Reading the room uses clues; it is not mind-reading.

advanced-native-3617.text: A burst freezer forced the neighbourhood bakery to close for ten days. After help with repairs, it reopened with a smaller menu and is gradually getting back on its feet.
After the cancelled performance, the choir used a smaller community event to get back on its feet while planning a new concert.
Get back on your feet means recover after a setback.
Getting back on your feet may take help and time.

advanced-native-3618.text: Many applicants listed the same software skills, but Mina showed how she tested her designs with users. That practical evidence sets her portfolio apart.
The team’s clear record of failed trials sets its science display apart from other displays with only final results.
Set something apart means make it distinct from comparable others.
A quality that sets work apart does not guarantee first place.

advanced-native-3627.text: The workshop fee was low, but the only bus left before it ended; for pupils in the outer district, the evening course remained out of reach.
Without the travel pass, the science camp was out of reach for pupils living beyond the ferry route.
Out of reach can describe a practical access barrier.
A course out of reach for someone is not necessarily beyond their ability.

advanced-native-3640.text: The garden need not be locked all week or left open overnight. Daytime access with evening closure shows the choice is not all or nothing.
The rehearsal choice is not all or nothing: new players can attend the first half before joining a full session later.
A choice can be not all or nothing when a workable middle option exists.
Not all or nothing does not make every compromise workable.

advanced-native-3673.text: When the riverside flats closed, Arun’s family moved across town. He missed his neighbours and familiar market, and felt uprooted despite the safer new home.
The fishermen felt uprooted after their harbour closed, even though the new pier offered better equipment.
Feeling uprooted can follow a loss of familiar community ties.
A safer home can still leave people uprooted.

advanced-native-3675.text: The conductor told Rae that one missed note proved she would never sing well. The sweeping comment knocked her confidence, although she kept practising.
One careless remark knocked my confidence before the speech, but practising with a friend helped me try again.
Knock someone’s confidence means reduce self-belief.
A remark that knocked your confidence does not prove skill vanished.

advanced-native-3689.text: A new clinic booking line could be a blessing or a burden: it shortens queues for people who can call early, but may shut out patients who share one phone.
The new volunteer app is a blessing or a burden depending on access: it organises shifts well, but some helpers cannot use it without mobile data.
An online booking requirement can be a blessing or a burden: it shortens queues for connected visitors but makes access harder for people without internet.
When a change is a blessing or a burden, identify who faces each effect.

advanced-native-3698.text: The theatre bought an accessible lift, but audience members still need clear directions to find it. Wayfinding is the other half of the equation.
The sports hall has ramps, but signs showing the step-free route are the other half of the equation.
The other half of the equation names another necessary factor.
The other half of the equation is a metaphor, not an exact percentage.

advanced-native-3700.text: The reusable-cup return scheme looked simple on quiet mornings, but at lunch queues formed and clean cups ran out. Under pressure, the cracks began to show.
The cracks began to show when the ticket desk faced its first large crowd and could not update changes quickly enough.
The cracks begin to show when hidden weaknesses become visible.
When the cracks begin to show, identify the specific problem.

advanced-native-3448.text: For the ten-minute welcome event, the organiser proposed printing a separate badge for every guest, then collecting and sorting them afterwards. I said that felt like too much fuss when a sign-in sheet would do.
For a five-minute prize draw, individually laminating every ticket feels like too much fuss; a numbered paper slip is enough.
Too much fuss weighs the procedure against the result.
Too much fuss can often be avoided by naming a simpler alternative.

advanced-native-3449.text: Every evening, Kai opens the class chat before beginning homework. After several months, he reaches for the chat even when there are no new messages. Once that habit sets in, starting work without checking feels strange.
Priya has written three lines in her notebook after each shift for four months. Once that habit sets in, reflecting on the day becomes part of closing the shop.
Once that habit sets in, repetition has made the action feel automatic.
Once that habit sets in, a cue can trigger the action with little thought.

advanced-native-3452.text: Our rehearsal ends at noon and the hall opens again at one. We can grab lunch at the café across the road and still return in time to set up the lights.
When the museum tour pauses at noon, we can grab lunch in the courtyard café before the next guide arrives.
We can grab lunch when the schedule leaves a short gap.
Grab lunch sounds casual, even when the meal is planned.

advanced-native-3455.text: The outdoor concert was meant to use the riverside stage, but the flood closed that entire area. Our stage plan has gone out of the window, so we are checking the indoor hall instead.
Once the archive building failed its safety inspection, our exhibition plan had gone out of the window, and we began looking for a temporary gallery.
A plan has gone out of the window when a key condition disappears.
When a school corridor becomes a practice area, its calm can go out of the window.

advanced-native-3458.text: The school garden lost several beds in the storm, and repairs will take weeks. It is not all doom and gloom, though: the greenhouse is intact, and volunteers can raise seedlings there while the beds are fixed.
The library branch must close one room for repairs. Yet it is not all doom and gloom: the mobile library will keep visiting the neighbourhood each week.
Not all doom and gloom acknowledges a setback before naming a real positive.
A concrete alternative makes not all doom and gloom credible.

advanced-native-3469.text: During the mural repair, the coordinator stood behind Mei and demanded a fresh update every five minutes. Mei said she could concentrate better without someone breathing down her neck while she mixed the paint.
The director checked every line over our shoulders, so we asked her to stop breathing down our neck while we rehearsed the new scene.
Breathing down your neck means intrusive pressure, not ordinary supervision.
Several imminent deadlines can be breathing down your neck even when nobody is standing nearby.

advanced-native-3472.text: We tested three caption styles with the same group of readers. The high-contrast version was easier for nearly everyone to read; it won hands down, although the others looked attractive.
After blind-testing the two recordings, the class understood the slower version much better; on clarity, it won hands down.
Hands down needs a clear basis for the comparison.
One choice can win hands down on a particular criterion without being perfect in every way.

advanced-native-3481.text: At the makers’ fair, visitors tried robotics, weaving and printmaking. Many returned to weaving because they could take a pattern home. They seemed to gravitate towards it without being assigned.
When given a choice of topics, the debate group gravitated towards local transport because members had collected their own journey stories.
People gravitate towards options they repeatedly choose when alternatives remain open.
Gravitate towards describes attraction, not a formal assignment.

advanced-native-3702.text: The office proposed a costly dashboard for tracking two monthly visitor queries. Staff already answer both by email on the same day. Without a recurring delay to fix, the dashboard feels like a solution in search of a problem.
