A clinic proposed a second booking portal, but staff found no missed appointments in the existing phone log; without a demonstrated gap, it sounded like a solution in search of a problem.
A solution in search of a problem lacks a demonstrated unmet need.
Before calling a tool a solution in search of a problem, check the existing process.

advanced-native-3706.text: In 1998, an engineer built a portable sign that updated bus arrivals over a wireless network. The local network could not cover bus stops then; decades later, similar signs became common. Her prototype was ahead of its time.
The first tactile museum label was ahead of its time only if it anticipated later accessible displays; we should compare its design with what museums use now.
Ahead of its time compares a design with the era that first received it.
Later adoption helps show why an idea was ahead of its time; early rejection alone does not.

advanced-native-3708.text: At Saturday’s repair fair, local radio mentioned the opening twice, hundreds queued for workshops, and photos spread online. It made a big splash, though later attendance is still unknown.
The first issue of the youth magazine made a big splash when its launch reading filled the hall and local papers ran interviews; the editors will track later subscriptions separately.
Make a big splash describes attention at an appearance or launch.
A campaign can make a big splash without proving lasting use.

advanced-native-3715.text: Many pharmacy patients now reorder medicine after work. The pharmacy added an evening online request form but kept the counter for those who prefer staff help. It can move with the times without excluding them.
The local archive moved with the times by adding searchable digital records after researchers requested remote access, yet it kept supervised access to fragile originals.
Move with the times means adapting to a demonstrated change.
A neighbourhood library can evolve with the times by adding online renewals while keeping in-person help.

advanced-native-3707.text: Many families asked about a neighbourhood solar-lantern trial. After the price was posted, fewer reserved one, though a small group still wanted it. The organiser said enthusiasm cooled down as the cost became clear.
Interest cooled down after the first archive visit produced little new material, although the researchers kept checking.
Interest cooled down when readers stopped recommending the serial after its early chapters, though some kept following it.
Enthusiasm can cool down after repeated delays without disappearing altogether.

advanced-native-3728.text: Two proposed library layouts were scored for wheelchair access. The north layout gained 82 points and the south layout 79, so the north option edges ahead on access. The committee will still check maintenance costs before deciding.
In the second trial, the quieter fan edged ahead on energy use by a narrow margin, but the team still checked repair costs before ordering either model.
Edges ahead marks a small, measured lead.
A team may edge ahead on one criterion without winning overall.

advanced-native-3735.text: After two colleagues fell ill, Nia handled their client calls as well as her own reports. She finished only the urgent work each day and postponed the rest. She was keeping her head above water, but the backlog showed she needed help.
With two nurses covering the extra evening calls, the clinic kept its head above water by answering urgent cases first, but managers arranged relief for the delayed follow-ups.
Keeping your head above water means coping, often only just.
A team can keep their heads above water while asking for more help.

advanced-native-3736.text: Interest in repairing old clothes has grown. The sewing centre added weekend lessons and extra machines for its waiting list. It can ride the wave by meeting this real demand, not merely posting about the trend.
As demand for reusable stage materials grew, the theatre cooperative rode the wave by opening a checked lending catalogue and training staff to inspect each return.
Ride the wave needs a growing trend and a concrete response.
A service may ride the wave without assuming the trend will last forever.

advanced-native-3738.text: The festival team admired a new projection wall and nearly ordered it after one demonstration. No one had checked power or access. They should not be carried away by it before those checks.
Although the new sorting machine impressed us, being carried away by it would mean ordering before operators test errors and delicate materials.
Carried away by it needs a clear idea or proposal for it to refer to.
Enjoying a proposal is fine; being carried away by it can make us skip checks.

advanced-native-3801.text: The museum booking line grew longer because the only ticket desk worked slowly. Many visitors voted with their feet and chose the smaller gallery nearby.
When the ferry cut its evening trips, some passengers voted with their feet and took the train instead.
Vote with one’s feet means show a choice by leaving or switching.
A complaint alone is not voting with one’s feet.

advanced-native-3803.text: The club ignored warnings that its ramp was too steep. Months later, that decision came back to haunt it when guests could not reach the award hall.
We skipped the translation check in spring, and that shortcut came back to haunt us when the autumn guide confused visitors.
Come back to haunt links an earlier action to later trouble.
A harmless memory alone does not come back to haunt someone.

advanced-native-3812.text: After paying rent and medicine, Amir had only enough for basic groceries. He was scraping by, with nothing left to save.
The grant let the music club scrape by for one more term, but it did not pay for new instruments.
Scrape by means manage essentials with little or no spare money.
Scraping by does not mean having no income at all.

advanced-native-3826.text: The community choir planned an outdoor concert, but the park was closed for repairs. It put those plans on hold until the venue reopened.
We put our plans on hold when the rehearsal room closed, and we will review dates after the repairs.
Put plans on hold means pause them for now.
Putting plans on hold neither guarantees resumption nor proves permanent cancellation.

advanced-native-3823.text: At a volunteer desk for clinic rides, people from two streets met. They kept arranging rides for one another’s families after the first event. The organiser said those continuing links strengthened the social fabric, beyond the ride total.
The new volunteer network strengthened the social fabric of the district by linking students with older residents.
Shared childcare arrangements can strengthen the social fabric when families keep helping one another over time.
In its annual report, the association explained how regular cross-team mentoring strengthened the social fabric of the town.

advanced-native-3829.text: The team now files twice as many forms, but new rules add the same amount of paperwork. The team is running just to stay in the same place.
The archive digitised fifty pages each week, but new donations arrived at the same rate, so the team was running just to stay in the same place.
Running just to stay in the same place contrasts effort with no net progress.
Running just to stay in the same place is less apt if the result clearly improves.

advanced-native-3864.text: A five-minute delay affected one train, but the signal failure stopped every line for two days. The second disruption was in a completely different league.
A small typo is inconvenient, but losing the whole archive is in a completely different league of seriousness.
In a different league marks a large difference in level.
Being in a different league need not mean better; state the dimension and direction.

advanced-native-3870.text: The manager announced a new rota without warning. Night staff were on the receiving end of the change: they had to rearrange childcare at short notice.
When the theatre cancelled the late bus without notice, volunteers were on the receiving end of that decision and had to pay for taxis.
On the receiving end identifies the person who experiences another party’s action.
Being on the receiving end does not imply agreement or deserved treatment.

advanced-native-3871.text: The exhibition includes drawings that also use digital animation. The line between the two sections is not clean-cut, even though each has a different main focus.
The difference between a rehearsal and a public preview is not clean-cut when invited guests can comment and changes are still possible.
A clean-cut distinction has a clear boundary.
A distinction that is not clean-cut can still preserve real differences.

advanced-native-3754.text: After weeks of staying indoors, Elsie spent Saturday visiting the flower market, greeting neighbours and walking through the park. She enjoyed being out and about again without planning a long trip.
The new community guide made it easier for residents to be out and about: they could find accessible paths between the clinic, market and park.
Being out and about describes active time outside the home.
You can be out and about locally; a long journey is unnecessary.

advanced-native-3766.text: When the class discussed accessible public spaces, the steep steps at the old station came to mind for Leena. She had used that station last week, but she checked the current entrance map before citing it as evidence.
When the committee asked for ways to reduce glare, the shaded bus shelter came to mind for Hana because she had measured its roof angle during last month’s survey.
Come to mind describes a thought occurring, not a verified conclusion.
Relevant memories can come to mind when a topic is raised.

advanced-native-3778.text: A buyer saw photographs of the refurbished chairs, but the seat fabric and frame joints were hard to judge on screen. She arranged a visit to see them with her own eyes before paying the deposit.
Before accepting the donated microscopes, the lab team went to see them with their own eyes and checked the lenses and stage controls against the inventory list.
See them with their own eyes stresses direct inspection rather than a description.
You may see them with your own eyes and still need a technical test.

advanced-native-3779.text: The school could not tell from a brochure whether two portable microphones would stay clear in a noisy hall. The supplier lent them for an afternoon, so teachers could try them out during rehearsal before placing an order.
The archivists borrowed two scanners to try them out on fragile paper; they measured jams and image clarity before recommending either model.
Try them out means use the items to test performance.
You can try them out and still decide not to buy either one.

advanced-native-3780.text: The cycling club ordered sample rain jackets. The size chart looked right, but members wanted to try on the jackets over their usual layers before ordering. They checked shoulder movement rather than trusting the label.
The dancers had to try on the new shoes before rehearsal so they could check heel support while moving, rather than rely on the size numbers alone.
Try on is for checking how wearable items fit or look.
You may try them on before deciding, even when the size label seems right.

advanced-native-3785.text: The theatre needs curtains by Friday. Two suppliers delivered on time in past seasons; a cheaper new seller has no record. The familiar suppliers look like safer bets for timing, though stock still needs checking.

For a time-sensitive exhibition, the established courier looked like a safer bet than an untested service because its tracking records showed reliable morning deliveries; the curator still confirmed this week’s schedule.
Safer bets are lower-risk choices on the stated evidence, not guarantees.
A safer bet still needs a final check of current conditions.

advanced-native-3791.text: At the museum, a guide noticed a visitor could not read the small captions. Beyond leading the tour, she prepared a large-print route sheet and checked it with the visitor. She went the extra mile to make the visit usable.
The bus-station volunteer went the extra mile for a traveller with limited vision by reading out the platform changes and waiting until the correct bus number was announced.
Go the extra mile means making helpful effort beyond normal duty.
A team can go the extra mile by checking whether the extra help actually works.

advanced-native-3798.text: The pottery class lost its kiln for a second week, so students could not finish their pieces. Some planned to grin and bear it, but Mara politely asked for a revised date or refund instead.
When the community shuttle skipped the accessible stop twice, riders did not have to grin and bear it; they recorded the dates and asked the operator to restore the published route.
Grin and bear it describes silent tolerance of an unpleasant situation.
You need not grin and bear it when a fair, polite remedy is available.

advanced-native-3799.text: At the youth concert, Ben found his reserved seat had been given to someone else. He was upset, but he did not make a scene in front of the audience. He spoke quietly to an usher, who found another seat and corrected the list.
The coach noticed the scoreboard was wrong, yet chose not to make a scene during the awards; she recorded the result and asked officials for a correction after the ceremony.
Make a scene means create a conspicuous public disturbance.
You can avoid making a scene and still ask for a correction.

advanced-native-3874.text: At the end of the hearing, the judge ordered no jail time under the agreed outcome. The defendant could walk free, though the report gave no reason beyond that ruling.
The article says the accused may walk free today, but it does not tell us why the court reached that decision.
Walk free reports a no-jail result in context.
Walk free alone does not explain the ruling or prove innocence.

advanced-native-3875.text: A library considered banning every group booking after one noisy party. The ban was too blunt an instrument: quiet study groups and disruptive events needed different responses.
Removing every visitor comment is too blunt an instrument when the problem is a small number of abusive messages.
Too blunt an instrument describes an indiscriminate response to a nuanced problem.
Calling a rule too blunt an instrument does not mean ignoring the problem.

advanced-native-3878.text: In the fictional case, the court imposed a prison term. The convicted person is now behind bars, rather than attending a community programme.
The story places the thief behind bars for the final chapter, while her accomplice remains outside prison.
Behind bars is distinct from a non-custodial programme.

advanced-native-3879.text: After missing classes for months, Lena began attending regularly, asked for help and kept a study routine through the whole term. Her friends say she is turning her life around.
Over several years, Niko turned his life around by keeping steady work and repairing relationships, though he still faces ordinary setbacks.
Turn one’s life around means a substantial positive change after difficulty.
A single good moment does not prove someone has turned their life around.

advanced-native-3888.text: The class wanted a modest thank-you card, but then ordered a huge stage and hundreds of balloons. Their teacher said they had gone overboard for a ten-minute farewell.
We can add flowers to the table, but let’s not go overboard and spend the whole month’s club budget on one dinner.
Go overboard means do more than a situation reasonably calls for.
A modest choice is not going overboard merely because it is optional.

advanced-native-3890.text: After a tiring week of rehearsals, Mei bought one inexpensive notebook simply because choosing it cheered her up. She joked that it was a little retail therapy.
I bought one cheap postcard as a bit of retail therapy after the long journey, but it was not a solution to every worry.
Retail therapy is informal shopping to try to feel better.
Retail therapy is not clinical treatment or a guaranteed cure.

advanced-native-3914.text: Only one class tried the courtyard game in April. By June, eight classes played it at lunch; the game was catching on across the school.
The new lunchtime debate game caught on after several clubs shared its rules, and attendance grew from six pupils to thirty.
An activity catches on when adoption spreads.
Catch on can also mean understand; context identifies the intended sense.

advanced-native-3916.text: The river festival invited neighbourhood boat builders to demonstrate their craft and used residents’ stories in its programme. Those details gave it strong local flavour.
The mural has local flavour because its painted shopfronts copy real signs from the old market street.
Local flavour can describe a place’s distinctive character in an event or work.
Local flavour need not mean literal taste or merely a local venue.

advanced-native-3926.text: The puzzle club was crowded on launch day, but after ten weeks it still had full tables and volunteer leaders. The organiser thinks the idea has legs.
The reading exchange has legs because borrowers have returned each month and the volunteers have secured another venue.
Have legs means show potential to continue after initial attention.
A trend does not have legs merely because it is popular today.

advanced-native-3927.text: A school posted a thirty-second sign-language clip on Monday. By Wednesday, clubs in twenty towns had shared it, and the idea caught fire online.
The recycling challenge caught fire over the weekend: fifty neighbourhood teams copied the first group’s plan by Sunday.
Catch fire means spread or gain attention rapidly.
Catching fire says little about how long the popularity will last.

advanced-native-3933.text: Three major projects fall due on the same Friday. Mei says she cannot relax even after studying all evening and feels weighed down by academic pressure.
Lina feels weighed down by academic pressure because four coursework deadlines overlap, so she asks her tutor to help set priorities.
Weighed down by academic pressure describes a felt burden from school demands.
Feeling weighed down by academic pressure does not measure a learner’s ability.

advanced-native-3934.text: Before her first debate, Tara felt tense. She took a quiet walk around the garden to shake the stress off, then returned to practise her opening.
A short stretch helped the dancers shake the stress off before rehearsal, but they still checked the difficult steps.
Shake the stress off means ease felt tension for now.
You can shake the stress off and still need to prepare.

advanced-native-3941.text: The junior organisers had to apologise for a cancelled workshop and arrange refunds themselves. Their mentor said taking responsibility in that way could build character.
Helping newcomers practise the safety rules may build character if the older students learn patience and listen to questions.
Build character can mean developing good qualities through specific actions.
A challenge may build character, but hardship alone proves nothing.

advanced-native-3947.text: Two neighbourhood groups had argued over garden space. After repairing the shared fence together, they still disagreed about planting but spoke more easily; the work helped soften the edges.
A joint cooking session helped soften the edges between the rival teams; they still competed, but they stopped insulting one another.
Soften the edges means ease a relationship’s sharpness or tension.
To soften the edges is not necessarily to settle every disagreement.

advanced-native-3961.text: The festival adverts promised six live stages, but only two opened and the rest were recorded screens. Several visitors found the event overhyped.
The “hands-on” science fair felt overhyped when visitors discovered that every machine was behind glass and could only be watched.
Overhyped means publicity created expectations the experience did not meet.
A popular event is not overhyped if it delivers what it promises.

advanced-native-3964.text: Mina enjoys travel programmes, but four hours of the same destination each evening left her tired of it. She said it was too much of a good thing.
The weekly art updates were useful, but ten alerts a day became too much of a good thing and members muted the channel.
Too much of a good thing means excess can make a benefit less enjoyable.
Too much of a good thing criticises the amount, not necessarily the thing itself.

advanced-native-4004.text: Nadia kept rehearsing how she might sound at the residents’ meeting. When she began asking neighbours what they needed, she got out of her own head and heard two concerns she had missed.
When Ravi stopped monitoring every facial expression he made and began explaining the repair steps to the customer, he got out of his own head.
Getting out of your own head means shifting attention away from self-focused worry.
A concrete conversation can help someone get out of their own head.

advanced-native-4010.text: During a six-month apprenticeship, Imani kept a weekly feedback call with her supervisor and practised between calls. Those conversations carried her all the way through the placement, even though she had to do the work herself.
Mira’s reading partner sent comments after every chapter and kept the appointments until the final presentation; that steady help carried her all the way through the research project.
Carry someone all the way through marks support lasting across the whole challenge.
Steady advice can carry her all the way through without doing her work.

advanced-native-4011.text: The town has several young violinists, but the rehearsal room is locked most evenings. A volunteer proposed opening it twice a week; otherwise their talent could go to waste without a place to play.
Without a chance to join the mapping project, the surveyor’s ability may go to waste even though she has already learned the equipment.
Talent can go to waste when it has no chance to be used.
Giving a skilled person suitable work means talent will not go to waste.

advanced-native-4015.text: The junior conservator returned to the archive after each failed pigment test, kept careful notes and asked for another sample. Her supervisor said she had a fire in her belly, even though no result was guaranteed.
Although the new researcher had to repeat the field survey twice, she still volunteered to compare the records each evening; she had a fire in her belly for the project.
Fire in the belly is a vivid way to describe persistent drive.
Look for repeated effort before saying someone has a fire in his belly.

advanced-native-4016.text: At the debate final, Elio lost the vote but thanked his opponent and listened to the feedback without interrupting. The panel noted how he carries himself after a setback, not just the score.
The exhibition manager listened to a visitor’s complaint, corrected the label and explained the change calmly; her team praised how she carries herself when work is challenged.
How she carries herself refers to observable demeanour and conduct.
Notice how a person carries themselves, but avoid judging their whole character from one moment.

advanced-native-4017.text: The coach asked Dario to repeat a drill. Dario shouted over her explanation and slammed the clipboard on the bench. He lost his temper; the request itself was ordinary feedback.
When the chair delayed the vote, Pavel lost his temper and yelled across the table; his colleague later asked him to apologise for the outburst.
Lose your temper means visibly losing control of anger.
A firm objection is different from losing your temper.

advanced-native-4020.text: The archive team indexed forty boxes in June. When the scanner began failing, it managed only three boxes a week; progress slowed to a crawl, though the work did not stop entirely.
Once the access road closed, progress slowed to a crawl on the garden renovation: deliveries continued, but only one small load arrived each week.
Progress slows to a crawl when advancement becomes extremely slow.
Even if progress slowed to a crawl, some work may still continue.

advanced-native-4024.text: After her first exhibition sold out, the ceramic artist still invited criticism of the glaze and tested new firing temperatures. She stayed hungry for improvement while appreciating what she had achieved.
The editor praised the finished issue, but the team stayed hungry for improvement and tested a clearer contents page for the next edition.
Stay hungry for improvement means keeping the wish to learn after success.
You can celebrate a win and stay hungry for improvement.

advanced-native-3968.text: A parent thought violin lessons had to start from the cradle. The teacher explained that beginners in primary school can still learn well with suitable practice.
The coach said that learning to balance on a board need not begin from the cradle; older beginners can practise safely too.
From the cradle means from the earliest period of life.
Starting from the cradle is not necessarily required for later learning.

advanced-native-3975.text: For thirty years, the school bell has played the same melody at lunch. Former students recognise it at once; it has become part of the furniture on campus.
The old clock in the station hall is part of the furniture for regular commuters; they expect its chime every morning.
Part of the furniture means long-established and familiar in a place.
Being part of the furniture does not guarantee universal approval.

advanced-native-3978.text: A club changed its logo, but members’ unresolved complaints about fees remained. The new design did not wipe the slate clean.
After both families settled the repair bill and apologised, they chose to wipe the slate clean and plan the next event together.
Wipe the slate clean means resolve or set aside past issues for a fresh start.
A new trend cannot wipe the slate clean while earlier problems remain.

advanced-native-3979.text: The annual orchestra concert remained the festival’s main draw, but a new puppet troupe filled a smaller hall and stole some of the limelight.
The veteran singer still closed the concert, but the new duet stole some of the limelight when its clip circulated widely afterward.
Steal some of the limelight means draw a share of attention from an established focus.
Stealing some of the limelight does not mean the original attraction vanishes.

advanced-native-3984.text: The archivist first thought the two dates were unrelated. On a second look, she noticed the same signature and delivery route, and the timeline clicked into place.
When the rainfall chart matched the reservoir log, the explanation clicked into place: the water level fell after three dry weeks.
Click into place means the pieces form a coherent whole.
A solution does not click into place merely because one word is understood.

advanced-native-3986.text: In the logic club, pupils compare several possible routes and explain why one works. The teacher says that kind of reasoning practice can sharpen the mind.
Checking how two maps differ sharpens the mind when it makes students compare details instead of guessing.
Sharpen the mind means train thinking through practice.
An activity can sharpen the mind without proving a medical benefit.

advanced-native-3997.text: After retiring, Nari still translates a short paragraph every morning to stay sharp. She says the daily habit helps her keep using the skills she already has.
The former chef tests one recipe a month to stay sharp, keeping her timing and tasting judgement in use.
Stay sharp means keep existing alertness or skill active.
Practising to stay sharp does not guarantee a person will never decline.

advanced-native-4000.text: After two hours on the coach, the passengers stopped at a rest area to stretch their legs. They walked for ten minutes before boarding again.
After the long workshop, the trainees stretched their legs in the courtyard for five minutes, then returned for the final session.
Stretch one’s legs means take a short walking break after sitting.
To stretch their legs, passengers need not finish the journey or join a workout.

advanced-native-4026.text: The fellowship asks applicants to submit two published studies and lead a community project. The bar is incredibly high, but several candidates still meet both published-work and leadership criteria.
For the restoration grant, the bar is incredibly high: teams must show tested materials, a full budget and a plan for public access.
The bar is incredibly high when entry standards are demanding.
Even when the bar is incredibly high, a qualified applicant may meet it.

advanced-native-4047.text: Sima’s school jumper and trousers fitted in September, but by spring the sleeves no longer reached her wrists and the trouser legs ended above her ankles. She had grown out of her clothes. Her family passed both to the uniform exchange.
The younger hikers grew out of their clothes over the year: their coats were tight and their trousers too short, so the club checked sizes before the autumn trip.
Grow out of clothes means become too big for garments that fitted before.
A change of taste alone does not mean someone grew out of their clothes.

advanced-native-4051.text: In the survey, some theatre volunteers chose durable plain uniforms while others valued a distinctive look. The importance they attach to fashion differs, even though both groups care about comfort.
The questionnaire asked people to rank comfort, cost and style, making the importance they attach to fashion easier to compare.
The importance they attach to fashion means the weight they give style in a decision.
Ask about competing priorities before judging the importance people attach to fashion.

advanced-native-4058.text: At the neighbourhood fair, visitors compared a broken lamp repaired for years with cheap lamps replaced after minor faults. The organisers used the contrast to discuss a throwaway culture and opened a repair desk.
The community hall began lending reusable banners after staff noticed a throwaway culture around seasonal displays: usable materials were being binned after one weekend.
A throwaway culture is a repeated habit of replacing usable goods.
Repair and reuse can challenge a throwaway culture.

advanced-native-4060.text: The library found four working lamps in storage. A volunteer suggested checking the plugs before staff cast them aside merely because the shades looked dated.
The club tested the old microphones before casting them aside; two needed only fresh cables and returned to use.
Cast them aside means reject or discard them rather than keep using them.
Check an item’s value before you cast it aside.

advanced-native-4061.text: At first, the workshop borrowed tools only for one event. Over months, members began checking the lending shelf before every purchase. A reuse mindset took hold and shaped the club’s routine.
Once a careful-recording mindset took hold in the lab, each technician checked the previous shift’s notes before restarting a test.
A mindset takes hold when it starts shaping repeated choices.
One isolated decision does not prove that a mindset has taken hold.

advanced-native-4068.text: The gallery posted short previews of its new night tours each week. The clips fed an appetite for evening visits, although the team still had to check whether viewers actually booked tickets.
The radio series about local architecture fed an appetite for walking tours, and the organisers later checked whether that interest became registrations.
Feed an appetite for something means increase desire for it.
Publicity may feed appetite for an event without proving sales.

advanced-native-4072.text: The two garden proposals both add shade and seating. In broad terms, they pursue the same goal, although one preserves the old trees and the other plans new planting.
In broad terms, both budgets protect the outreach programme, but only the revised version funds a weekend service.
In broad terms gives an overview rather than an exact identity claim.
After saying in broad terms, name the detail that still differs.

advanced-native-4103.text: For years the club filed memberships on paper. Even after a secure shared register solved lost forms in a trial, several officers refused to consider it. They had become set in their ways about record keeping.
The theatre crew had always stored props by room number; after a clear category system worked for three shows, some remained set in their ways and rejected it without testing.
Set in their ways means resistant to changing established habits.
Ask why someone rejects a new method before calling them set in their ways.

advanced-native-4120.text: A short demonstration of tide pools made the children ask how the creatures survive when the water recedes. It lit the fuse of curiosity; the teacher then gave them a field guide for deeper study.
A question about an unexplained stain on the old mural lit the fuse for the conservators’ investigation, which later involved months of pigment tests.
Light the fuse means trigger the beginning of a response.
A short question can light the fuse of curiosity without completing the whole inquiry.

advanced-native-4128.text: The printer’s first prototype failed a safety test. After the team found the loose cable and passed a repeat test, they got past the setback and resumed the exhibition build.
The rehearsal venue closed unexpectedly; after securing another accessible room, the ensemble got past it and kept the concert schedule.
Get past it means move beyond a specific, clearly identified difficulty.
A useful fix can help a team get past the setback and continue.

advanced-native-4140.text: At the ferry pier, Niko saw a child return a dropped scarf to a stranger just as the boat lights came on. He kept a mental snapshot of that small exchange, though he could not later recall the exact time.
The dancer kept a mental snapshot of the empty stage just before the audience entered, though she later checked the programme to confirm the sequence.
A mental snapshot is a vivid remembered image, not a complete record.
A date may need checking even when a mental snapshot feels clear.

advanced-native-4146.text: The repair club lends tools to several workshops. Its coordinator keeps track of return dates in a shared log and updates the entry whenever a borrower arranges an extension.
The exhibition team kept track of label revisions in a shared table, so printers could verify which version was current before producing signs.
Keep track of something means maintain an updated view of it.
A changing schedule needs checking if you want to keep track of it.

advanced-native-4161.text: After a long overnight shift, Mei remembered the equipment test but was unsure which readings came first. Her memory could become foggy when she was tired, so she checked the timestamped log before reporting the sequence.
Memory can become foggy after a hectic event; the coordinator recalled the closing speech but checked the programme before naming who spoke first.
Memory can become foggy without every event being forgotten.
When memory may become foggy, check a record before stating uncertain details.

advanced-native-4170.text: The oral-history recording invited the class to compare how two neighbours remembered the same flood. Listening closely nourished their minds by raising questions about evidence and memory.
A conversation about the novel’s unreliable narrator nourished her mind because she began questioning whose evidence the story left out.
Nourish the mind means enrich thought or imagination.
Thoughtful questions can nourish the mind without guaranteeing expertise.

advanced-native-4171.text: The reading club planned an event to help reluctant readers choose books they enjoyed. One proposal required every visitor to finish the same long novel. The chair said it missed the point entirely: the event was about choice.
The mentor wanted students to explain their reasoning, so an answer sheet giving only final numbers missed the point entirely.
Miss the point entirely means fail to grasp the central purpose.
Name the neglected purpose when saying a plan misses the point entirely.

advanced-native-4151.text: I outsource the rehearsal times to my phone: it alerts me the day before each session. I still listen to my playing and decide which passage needs work.
I outsource meeting times to my calendar, but I still decide which meetings deserve my attention.
Outsourcing dates to a calendar can free attention for choices that still need human judgment.
Do not outsource every detail to a phone; decide which reminders help and which facts you still need to know.

advanced-native-4172.text: Retired engineer Ada joined a local history walk each month and kept asking how old bridges had been built. Those questions helped her keep her curiosity alive beyond her former profession.
The community science group kept its curiosity alive by comparing each new water sample with earlier results and noting fresh questions.
Keep your curiosity alive means continue wanting to explore.
Regular questions can keep their curiosity alive at any age.

advanced-native-4174.text: The exhibition showed two maps of the same river drawn fifty years apart. Their different shorelines gave visitors food for thought about how a place changes and what each map leaves out.
The oral-history interview offered food for thought about whose voices the town archive had preserved and whose it had missed.
Food for thought is material that prompts further reflection.
An unanswered question can offer food for thought without proving an answer.

advanced-native-4175.text: Leena proposed shorter opening hours for one month, then an attendance review. The rushed minutes announced a permanent cut. Her trial condition got lost in translation, so she asked the chair to correct the minutes.
In the design handover, the note called the shelves ready, although Omar had requested a load test first. His condition got lost in translation, so the lead restored it before the shelves were used.
Get lost in translation can describe a condition lost as a message is passed between people or formats.
A nuance can get lost in translation between languages too; compare the original and the retelling.

advanced-native-4176.text: The team discussed a mural proposal for three meetings but never agreed on a site or budget. Without those decisions, the proposal went nowhere; they scheduled a site visit to break the impasse.
The grant idea went nowhere for months because no one prepared the cost estimate; the treasurer finally drafted one for review.
Go nowhere means fail to make useful progress.
Name the bottleneck before saying a proposal is going nowhere.

advanced-native-4180.text: The route leaflet still showed the museum’s former accessible entrance, which moved last month. That line went out of date, so staff corrected the map. Their practice of explaining each change clearly remained useful throughout.
The volunteer handbook went out of date when the sign-in desk moved to a different floor, so the coordinator revised the arrival instructions.
Go out of date means become obsolete or cease to be current.
A timetable may go out of date, while a useful communication skill may not.

advanced-native-4186.text: After preparing the same soup each Friday for years, Inez knew the recipe by heart: she could list the order of vegetables without opening the notebook, though she still checked the allergy label.
The café cook knew several recipes by heart and trained new staff by explaining each method before they opened the kitchen manual.
Know a recipe by heart means recall its main method from memory.
A cook can know recipes by heart and still check safety details.

advanced-native-4188.text: After the flood, the trained maintenance crew assessed the electrical risk; then volunteers rolled up their sleeves to clear safe debris from the community hall.
Once the conservator marked which boxes were safe to handle, the archive volunteers rolled up their sleeves and rehoused the documents.
Roll up your sleeves means get ready for practical work.
Check safety first, then roll up your sleeves on the tasks you can do.

advanced-native-4190.text: The outdoor display was due before noon, but the usual stand was damaged. The crew borrowed a stable replacement, checked its fixings and got the job done before visitors arrived.
The exhibition team got the job done by using the tested spare projector and checking the captions before the afternoon opening.
Get the job done means complete the required task effectively.
A plan helps, but only a completed result shows the team got the job done.

advanced-native-4205.text: The safety card says only “use care”. New volunteers need the exact shut-off steps, so that vague line does not cut it.
The one-line repair note does not cut it for new technicians because it leaves out the order of the tests.
Does not cut it means inadequate for a stated need.
A method may not cut it for one task yet remain useful for another.

advanced-native-4206.text: During the budget briefing, a phone rang just as Inez explained the final cost. She paused, said she had lost her train of thought, and checked her notes before continuing.
I lost my train of thought when the screen went blank, but the outline helped me return to the second point.
Lose one’s train of thought means temporarily forget the next link in an explanation.
Losing one’s train of thought need not mean forgetting the whole subject.

advanced-native-4208.text: In the design workshop, the newcomers were standing on the sidelines while older members built the model. The leader later gave each newcomer a small part to assemble.
The audience first watched from the sidelines, then the artist invited them to help arrange the tiles.
Watch from the sidelines means observe without taking part.
Standing on the sidelines does not by itself reveal why someone is not joining.

advanced-native-4211.text: At the craft fair, the child knew how to describe her model, but her uncle answered every visitor on her behalf. The tutor asked him to let her try next time.
The student was absent, so her partner presented the group’s chart on her behalf after receiving her notes.
On someone’s behalf means acting as that person’s representative.
Answering on their behalf can help or hinder, depending on whether they need the chance to try.

advanced-native-4219.text: After several booking errors, the arts centre came under the microscope. Trustees requested records and visitors asked how places had been allocated.
The festival organisers were under the microscope after a ticketing mistake, but the review had not yet decided who was responsible.
Under the microscope means subject to close scrutiny.
Being under the microscope does not prove wrongdoing.

advanced-native-4235.text: The tutor showed the class two conflicting receipts and asked which date matched the delivery log. After comparing both, the pupils chose one date, and the tutor confirmed it was correct. They had arrived at the answer themselves.
The group checked the labels against the map, which confirmed the final location; then they arrived at the answer without the guide naming it.
Arrive at the answer means reason one’s way to the correct conclusion.
Arriving at the answer oneself differs from hearing a tutor supply it.

advanced-native-4240.text: The reading group set a short target for each Friday and checked completed pages. Those checkpoints kept learning on track when members had other work.
A weekly checklist kept learning on track by showing the trainees which safety topics still needed practice.
Keep learning on track means maintain progress toward a goal.
Keeping learning on track does not mean every task is already finished.

advanced-native-4242.text: The meeting was meant to decide library opening hours, but it drifted off-topic into a debate about wall colours. The chair returned to the hours question.
The committee drifted off-topic while discussing lunch plans, so the chair brought everyone back to the emergency-exit map.
Drift off-topic means gradually move away from the intended subject.
An example that helps answer the question does not necessarily drift off-topic.

advanced-native-4193.text: The community concert starts in an hour, and the delivery van with the sound desk is delayed. When the heat is on, the stage manager checks the approved spare equipment and reorganises the sound check without skipping the safety test.
When the heat is on before the library sale, Amira assigns one colleague to check prices and another to prepare the queue, keeping both tasks accurate under a tight deadline.
When the heat is on means pressure rises at a demanding moment.
Name the deadline and decision when the heat is on.

advanced-native-4248.text: Rafi kept confusing the scale on two maps. A guide pointed to the distance bar on each one; the penny finally dropped, and Rafi could explain why the same centimetre meant different distances.
The penny dropped for the new archivist when the index key showed that the dates referred to donations, not publication; she could then sort the records correctly.
The penny drops when an earlier puzzle suddenly makes sense.
Show what clue appeared before the penny dropped and what the learner can now explain.

advanced-native-4250.text: During a workshop, the tutor compared Ivo’s draft with a polished example and joked about his intelligence in front of the group. Ivo stopped volunteering ideas; the public joke made him feel small.
Comparing Nia’s first attempt with a finished professional design in a mocking tone made her feel small; the mentor later apologised and gave one concrete revision privately.
Make a student feel small means make that learner feel belittled.
Specific feedback need not make students feel small when given respectfully.

advanced-native-4252.text: At the planning table, the chair interrupted every one of Noor’s suggestions with “That will never work” before hearing her reasons. Noor put away her notes and stopped proposing ideas; the repeated dismissals shut her down.
The organiser shut them down by laughing at their first suggestion, and the two apprentices withdrew their proposal before anyone could check it.
Shut them down means silence or discourage them from contributing.
A dismissive response can shut students down even before their evidence is heard.

advanced-native-4253.text: The community archive rejected the first label design because visitors could not read it. Priya asked for feedback, enlarged the type and submitted a second version without losing heart; approval was still pending.
After the first grant application was returned for missing figures, the youth group gathered the evidence and reapplied without losing heart; the decision would come later.
Without losing heart means continuing despite a setback.
Show the revision and new attempt when writing about acting without losing heart.

advanced-native-4263.text: The local-history walk used to draw questions at every stop, but the unchanged script now leaves most visitors silent and early departures have risen. The walk has lost its spark; the guide plans to add short object-handling stops.
The youth orchestra lost its spark after rehearsals became a fixed sequence with no chance for players to suggest interpretations; the conductor asked members what they wanted to explore.
Lose its spark means become less lively or engaging than before.
Look for a before-and-after change before saying an activity lost its spark.

advanced-native-4264.text: The weekly reading circle always began with a long lecture, and members rarely spoke. This month the host mixed things up by starting with pairs who compare one paragraph; she will check whether more people contribute.
To mix things up at the map workshop, the facilitator let small groups test routes before she explained the official key; she then asked which sequence supported understanding.
Mix things up means introduce variety into a familiar routine.
Describe the old routine and the new step when you say someone mixed things up.

advanced-native-4265.text: At the first volunteer meeting, several newcomers sat quietly. Amina welcomed each person by name, asked about their interests and got three groups chatting; her easy warmth lit up a room that had felt tense.
At the neighbourhood meal, Dev’s stories and attentive questions lit up a room of strangers: tables that had been quiet began exchanging memories.
Light up a room means make the social atmosphere warmer and livelier.
Show people’s reactions when describing how someone lit up a room.

advanced-native-4273.text: Parents thought the museum workshop had been cancelled because its room changed. The organiser showed the new room notice and confirmed the same start time; their replies showed that this cleared up a misunderstanding.
A revised timetable cleared up misunderstandings about the ferry: the last departure was at six, not five, and passengers confirmed the new time before booking.
Clear up misunderstandings means resolve mistaken beliefs through explanation.
Confirmation from listeners helps show that you cleared up a misunderstanding.

advanced-native-4280.text: On similar streets, a city team compared injury records before and after protected crossings were added. Injuries fell where they were installed, though other causes need checking. That gives a strong case for a trial near the school.
The accessible-entry survey made a strong case for testing a second ramp: users identified the same bottleneck on several days, and the team costed a temporary route before asking for approval.
A strong case connects a claim to relevant reasons and evidence.
A strong case can acknowledge uncertainty without losing its value.

advanced-native-4283.text: Three bus-stop designs were measured for step-free access. Design C had the gentlest slope and most turning space, so it took the crown for accessibility. It was not necessarily the cheapest.
In the school garden trial, the raised-bed design took the crown for wheelchair turning space after measurements across four layouts; the team still had to compare maintenance costs.
Take the crown means be judged best among alternatives on a stated measure.
Name the measure before saying a choice took the crown.

advanced-native-4304.text: A river rises in Country A and floods farms just across the boundary in Country B. The same water system shows how flood risks cross borders, though villages farther away may remain unaffected.
The same invasive insect was identified in orchards in Country M and neighbouring Country N, so the control challenge crossed borders and required both inspection teams to compare findings.
Cross borders means extend beyond one country’s boundary.
Identify the second country before claiming a problem crossed borders.

advanced-native-4305.text: A conservator identified the damaged pages while a digital archivist photographed each repaired section; they checked the record together every afternoon. They worked side by side to preserve the collection.
The school librarian and a language teacher worked side by side to build a reading guide: one selected accessible editions, the other tested the questions with pupils.
Side by side can mean cooperating closely on a shared task.
Show each contribution before saying the teams worked side by side.

advanced-native-4309.text: An online post said the town bridge would close tomorrow. The librarian checked the council notice: only the footpath beside it would close. This helped readers separate fact from fiction about the bridge.
The school newspaper separated fact from fiction by checking the timetable before reporting that the concert was delayed by one hour, not cancelled.
Separate fact from fiction means test claims against evidence.
State what remains unknown when you separate fact from fiction.

advanced-native-4322.text: Two friends expected different arrival times for a charity run. They checked the opening time, agreed to meet at the north gate at eight and chose who would bring water. They sorted out the details of a shared plan before leaving.
The walking group sorted out the details of their shared plan after comparing ferry times: all six members confirmed the eight-thirty departure and who would carry the route map.
Sort out the details of a shared plan means settle the practical arrangement together.
After you sort out the details of a plan, check that everyone agrees.

advanced-native-4328.text: During the gallery meeting, staff noticed the printed route map sent wheelchair users to a stair-only entrance. After checking the approved accessible path, the coordinator corrected the map there and then before the next group arrived.
When the workshop leader learned that the posted room number was wrong, she checked the booking email and changed the sign there and then, before attendees followed the old notice.
There and then means immediately at that point.
A checked correction can still be made there and then.

advanced-native-4330.text: During a scheduled medication count, the clinic clerk receives a non-urgent request for next month’s leaflet. She acknowledges it, promises a draft after the count and finishes the required check without dropping everything.
The translator acknowledged the non-urgent poster request and offered a review slot after finishing the live-caption check, responding without dropping everything.
Without dropping everything means responding while keeping current commitments in view.
Give a clear later time when answering without dropping everything.

advanced-native-4516.text: Digital forms are convenient, but paper forms still have their place when the network is down.
Short videos help, but detailed written guides still have their place when users need to check each step.
Have their place acknowledges value within a relevant context.
Match has its place and have their place to the subject.

advanced-native-4525.text: The library has extended weekend hours twice, yet the waiting list is not going away.
Even after the extra buses arrive, passengers will still need late service; that need is not going away this winter.
Not going away marks a need or issue that persists for now.
A problem that is not going away now can still improve later.

advanced-native-4529.text: The last ferry was cancelled after the bridge closed, leaving island residents stranded overnight.
If the night coach stops before the concert ends, it could leave rural visitors stranded without a return bus.
Leave someone stranded means no workable onward or return route.
A delay alone may not leave someone stranded if a practical alternative remains.

advanced-native-4535.text: With no single timetable, Lena pieced the route together from a train notice and a ferry board.
I pieced my weekend route together from the rail update, the local bus board and a hotel notice.
Piece X together combines separate parts into a workable whole.
You can piece together an account without claiming every gap is closed.

advanced-native-4538.text: The clinic now shares appointment notes with its pharmacy, so patients no longer repeat their details; care is more joined-up.
The housing team and repair desk now share case updates, giving residents a more joined-up service.
Joined-up describes coordination across connected parts.
A more joined-up service reduces needless repetition for users.

advanced-native-4540.text: One shared login takes the friction out of renewing a library card because readers no longer fill in the same form twice.
The new receipt scanner takes the friction out of expense claims by reading the date and amount automatically.
Take the friction out of names a process made easier.
Taking some of the friction out of a task does not remove every step.

advanced-native-4543.text: I filled in one form for the north clinic, then the south clinic told me to start again and could not see my booking. The system feels like a patchwork of rules, not one service.
The permit rules feel like a patchwork because each office asks for a different document.
A patchwork of services causes trouble when its parts leave gaps or give conflicting instructions.
A shared intake can make several offices feel less like a patchwork without removing their different roles.

advanced-native-4548.text: Maya can now play the whole piece, although last week she struggled with a section she had mastered before. Her progress is not a straight line.
The theatre’s attendance has grown this season, though a rainy month caused a dip; its recovery is not a straight line.
Not a straight line allows overall growth with setbacks.
Progress is not a straight line, so a brief dip does not erase a wider gain.

advanced-native-4553.text: The concert was cancelled, but the venue offered full refunds and a free recording; that took some of the sting out of the disappointment.
The workshop is delayed, but a clear new date and free transport will take some of the sting out of the change.
Take the sting out of softens an unpleasant effect.
Taking some of the sting out of a loss does not erase the loss.

advanced-native-4554.text: Small app fees are charged every week, and together they have become a constant drain on Imani’s wallet.
The weekly storage charge has become a constant drain on my wallet, so I am comparing cheaper options.
A constant drain on the wallet is a recurring cost.
A fee can be a steady drain on your wallet without emptying it at once.

advanced-native-4563.text: The school had not confirmed the ferry time, but booked the coach anyway, hoping for the best.
We have reserved the room without a weatherproof route; for now we are hoping for the best, but we need a backup path.
Hoping for the best acknowledges an uncertain result.
You can hope for the best while still checking risks and preparing a backup.

advanced-native-4580.text: Publishing the school meal costs stirred up questions about why two campuses charged different prices.
The audit stirred up questions about how repair requests are ranked, and the agency has promised to explain its method.
Stir up questions means prompt discussion, not settle it.
A finding can stir up questions without anyone intending trouble.

advanced-native-4599.text: The clinic wants more appointment slots without cutting consultation time; that is a balancing act for its schedulers.
The school’s timetable is a balancing act between longer science labs and enough time for language classes.
A balancing act names competing needs that must be reconciled.
Call it a balancing act only when both sides affect the decision.

advanced-native-4606.text: After ten years on stage, Ravi began training young actors; teaching opened a new chapter in his career.
Starting her first community clinic opens a new chapter for the doctor, who now leads a team as well as treating patients.
Opening a new chapter signals a meaningful new stage.
Opening a new chapter can build on what was learned in earlier work.

advanced-native-4612.text: The rehearsal studio is just around the corner from Nia’s flat, so she can walk there in two minutes.
The office is just around the corner from our new flat, so my commute will be short.
Just around the corner can mark spatial closeness.
A deadline just around the corner is near in time instead.

advanced-native-4336.text: The theatre team saved each approved script change with a date and the person responsible. Those entries leave a trail that helps the director see why the final scene changed, although an unrecorded conversation may still be missing.
A dated repair log left a trail from the first fault report to the final safety check, letting the centre manager trace what was fixed and when.
Leave a trail means create records or clues that can be followed.
A dated sequence helps a project leave a trail without proving every detail.

advanced-native-4337.text: After the museum briefing, a visitor asked for the exact repair date of a lift. The question caught her off guard because the date was not in her notes. She said she would verify it with maintenance rather than guess.
The late change to the venue entrance caught us off guard, but we checked the official notice before directing visitors.
Caught off guard means surprised before you can prepare.
You can be caught off guard and still choose to verify before answering.

advanced-native-4340.text: During the festival setup, messages flew back and forth between the stage and access teams as the rain plan changed three times in an hour. The coordinator then posted one confirmed route so volunteers would not follow an older version.
Questions flew back and forth during the online design review, but the chair ended by recording the approved colour code and who would update the sign.
Fly back and forth describes rapid repeated exchange.
After messages fly back and forth, confirm which version is final.

advanced-native-4344.text: At the community meeting, the chair pasted the same cheerful reply after each account of a difficult move without addressing any concern. The rush crowded out sincerity; she later invited specific questions and listened.
At the reunion, a pile of prewritten compliments crowded out sincerity: guests stopped asking one another real questions until the host slowed the activity and invited personal memories.
Crowd out sincerity means displace genuine attention or honest response.
A fast reply need not crowd out sincerity if it addresses the real concern.

advanced-native-4357.text: At the coin fair, Theo displayed a costly case, but Rina identified a rare printing error and explained its history from a catalogue. For the collectors, her knowledge was the real flex, not the price of the case.
At the map exhibition, explaining how an old route changed was the real flex; the ornate frame attracted visitors, but the archivist’s evidence held their attention.
The real flex is the genuinely impressive quality behind the display.
At a craft fair, patient repair skill can be the real flex beside costly tools.

advanced-native-4358.text: At the photography club, the chair always invited prize winners to speak first and ignored new members’ questions. Several members said awards were shaping the social pecking order, although the club had no formal rank list.
A social pecking order emerged quietly in the choir when long-serving singers always chose solos before newer members could audition.
A social pecking order is an informal hierarchy within a group.
The social pecking order may be visible in who gets heard first.

advanced-native-4366.text: A library’s poster shows how a new booking tool lets members reserve study rooms from home. It shines a spotlight on the benefits of remote booking, but members still need to check the tool’s access rules.
The trial video shines a spotlight on the benefits of the new caption tool by showing readers how to adjust text size, while a note links to its known limitations.
Shine a spotlight on the benefits means draw attention to advantages.
A brochure can shine a spotlight on its benefits while still listing limits.

advanced-native-4370.text: Before the grant interview, a youth group chose photographs of completed work and explained its measurable results. They put their best foot forward without inventing attendance figures, and kept the full report ready for questions.
For the open studio, the potters put their best foot forward by displaying their strongest finished pieces and a short record of the glazing tests.
Put your best foot forward means present your strongest genuine side.
A team can put their best foot forward with work it can verify.

advanced-native-4379.text: From nine until noon, a different bus arrived at the depot about every twenty minutes. Each one pulled in at a marked bay and stopped before passengers boarded. The announcer described repeated arrivals, not one bus parked for hours.
A bus pulled in beside the library at dusk, and the waiting volunteers boarded after it stopped.
The taxi pulled in beside the clinic before the passenger got out.
When a vehicle pulls in, it arrives at a stopping place; the phrase does not mean it has already left.

advanced-native-4616.text: The bakery tour was eye-opening because pupils learned that most wasted bread came from ordering too much dough.
The recycling centre visit was eye-opening: we discovered that sorting errors, not collection days, caused most delays.
Eye-opening describes an experience that reveals something unexpected.
An eye-opening finding changes understanding, not eyesight.

advanced-native-4620.text: The farm visit shook loose the pupils’ assumption that every crop grows in open fields; they saw herbs thriving indoors.
The volunteer exchange shook loose our assumptions about rural internet access when we found a thriving online homework club.
Shake loose an assumption means make a held belief less secure.
Shaking loose old assumptions need not overturn every belief.

advanced-native-4624.text: The theatre cannot announce dates until the safety report arrives, so planning has become a waiting game.
Until the repair certificate arrives, reopening the pool is a waiting game for the centre.
A waiting game is a process dominated by delay.
A process becomes a waiting game when a missing decision blocks the next step.

advanced-native-4632.text: The booking page copied the hotel logo, so Tariq let his guard down and entered his details before checking the web address.
When a booking message asks for a second payment, do not let your guard down just because it uses the hotel’s name.
Let your guard down means become less watchful.
Letting your guard down raises risk, but does not prove harm occurred.

advanced-native-4634.text: A burst pipe flooded the rehearsal room, and the evening plan changed in a heartbeat.
When the power went out, the cooking lesson moved outdoors in a heartbeat so the class could continue.
In a heartbeat emphasises how fast an action or change happens.
A plan can change in a heartbeat and still work well.

advanced-native-4635.text: The fake charity page promised a receipt, and Omar paid before checking its registration; he fell for the scam.
Do not fall for a fake donation scam just because the page displays a familiar logo; check the charity register first.
Fall for a scam requires being deceived, not merely contacted.
Someone can avoid falling for a scam by verifying a suspicious claim first.

advanced-native-4638.text: The hilltop lanterns appear on local signs and postcards, making them the town’s calling card.
The hand-painted trams are the district’s calling card, appearing on its map and festival banners.
A calling card is a recognisable feature that represents someone or somewhere.
A city’s calling card need not be its only attraction.

advanced-native-4644.text: This harbour has more than one face: fishing boats at dawn and busy food stalls after dark.
The museum has more than one face: a quiet study room upstairs and lively hands-on workshops below.
More than one face means several distinct aspects.
Show how a place has more than one face by naming two concrete experiences.

advanced-native-4385.text: During a cycling class, Jo tested sealed headphones at high volume and could not hear the instructor’s bell. The music blocked out important sounds, so she lowered the volume before the group left the yard.
In the rehearsal room, a heavy backing track blocked out important sounds, including the conductor’s count-in; the band reduced the track before trying again.
Block out important sounds means mask useful sounds from outside.
Loud music can block out warning sounds that are otherwise audible.

advanced-native-4393.text: The gallery entrance was too bright on sunny afternoons. A fabric shade took the edge off the glare, but visitors still needed to let their eyes adjust before reading the wall labels.
A thicker curtain took the edge off the streetlight glare in the bedroom, although a thin line of light still showed beside the window.
Take the edge off means reduce an unpleasant intensity.
A shade can take the edge off glare without making a room dark.

advanced-native-4395.text: For three weeks, the shared fridge door failed to close properly and spoiled food twice. The volunteers had put up with the fault while waiting for a part, but they finally moved the food and asked for a repair date.
The volunteers put up with the temporary detour for two weekends, but they asked the organiser to mark the route clearly until the path reopened.
Put up with means tolerate something unpleasant.
A team may put up with a delay temporarily while asking for a fix.

advanced-native-4398.text: Two neighbours were already arguing about a shared gate. When one posted an unverified accusation in the building chat, more residents took sides and the meeting became harder to arrange. The message added fuel to the fire.
The committee’s dispute about the budget was tense already; an anonymous rumour about missing funds added fuel to the fire before the accounts were checked.
Add fuel to the fire means worsen an existing problem.
An unverified accusation can add fuel to the fire in a tense group.

advanced-native-4401.text: When the volunteer app repeated every schedule change to all 80 helpers, a storm of notifications arrived within ten minutes. Several people missed the one confirmed start time, so the coordinator pinned a single final update.
A storm of notifications hit the clinic team when the rota app repeated each shift edit; the supervisor muted duplicates and posted one confirmed schedule.
A storm of notifications is a rapid overload of alerts.
One verified update can calm a storm of notifications in a group chat.

advanced-native-4407.text: After reviewing late-night complaints, the residence committee voted to bring in clearer quiet-hour rules: noisy repairs would stop after nine, and every flat received the new notice. The committee would review complaints after a month.

pronunciation.phonemesBefore: ˈæftɚ ɹᵻvjˈuːɪŋ lˈeɪtnˈaɪt kəmplˈeɪnts, ðə ɹˈɛzᵻdəns kəmˈɪɾi vˈoʊɾᵻd tə bɹˈɪŋ ɪn klˈɪɹɚ kwˈaɪətˈaʊɚ ɹˈuːlz: nˈɔɪzi ɹᵻpˈɛɹz wʊd stˈɑːp ˈæftɚ nˈaɪn, ænd ˈɛvɹi flˈæt ɹᵻsˈiːvd ðə nˈuː nˈoʊɾɪs. ðə kəmˈɪɾi wʊd ɹᵻvjˈuː kəmplˈeɪnts ˈæftɚɹ ɐ mˈʌnθ.

advanced-native-4407.text: The rehearsal centre brought in new quiet-hour rules after consulting nearby residents: drums must stop at eight, and booking confirmations now show the limit.

pronunciation.phonemesBefore: ðə ɹɪhˈɜːsəl sˈɛntə bɹˈɔːt ɪn njˈuː kwˈaɪətˈaʊə ɹˈuːlz ˈaftə kənsˈʌltɪŋ nˈiəbaɪ ɹˈɛzɪdənts: dɹˈʌmz mˈʌst stˈɒp at ˈeɪt, and bˈʊkɪŋ kɒnfəmˈeɪʃənz nˈaʊ ʃˈəʊ ðə lˈɪmɪt.
pronunciation.phonemesAfter: ðə ɹɪhˈɜːsəl sˈɛntə bɹˈɔːt ɪn njˈuː kwˈaɪət ˈaʊə ɹˈuːlz ˈaftə kənsˈʌltɪŋ nˈiəbaɪ ɹˈɛzɪdənts: dɹˈʌmz mˈʌst stˈɒp at ˈeɪt, and bˈʊkɪŋ kɒnfəmˈeɪʃənz nˈaʊ ʃˈəʊ ðə lˈɪmɪt.

advanced-native-4407.text: Bring in clearer quiet-hour rules means introduce a more specific noise policy.

pronunciation.phonemesBefore: bɹˈɪŋ ɪn klˈiəɹə kwˈaɪətˈaʊə ɹˈuːlz mˈiːnz ˌɪntɹədjˈuːs ɐ mˈɔː spəsˈɪfɪk nˈɔɪz pˈɒlɪsi.
pronunciation.phonemesAfter: bɹˈɪŋ ɪn klˈiəɹə kwˈaɪət ˈaʊə ɹˈuːlz mˈiːnz ˌɪntɹədjˈuːs ɐ mˈɔː spəsˈɪfɪk nˈɔɪz pˈɒlɪsi.

advanced-native-4407.text: A venue may plan to bring in new rules before they take effect.

advanced-native-4408.text: For a month, the clinic team had covered unexpected shift gaps. They began snapping over small handover questions and missing breaks. Their supervisor said they seemed frayed at the edges and arranged extra cover before the next rota.
After repeated last-minute programme changes, the volunteers were frayed at the edges; the coordinator shortened the next shift and protected a meal break.
Frayed at the edges means worn down by continuing pressure.
A team frayed at the edges may need breaks and practical cover.

advanced-native-4416.text: At the repair club, each experienced member spends ten minutes learning a newcomer’s name and helping with a first task. Regular members say the welcome ritual is social glue because newcomers return and ask questions more readily.
Shared meal planning became social glue for the volunteer crew: members from different shifts began learning one another’s names and arranging cover when someone was absent.
Social glue is a practice that helps hold relationships together.
Regular shared work can become social glue when members connect.

advanced-native-4652.text: The rent survey shone a light on hidden repair costs that tenants had been paying themselves.
The attendance report shines a light on which evening classes working parents cannot reach; the centre still needs to respond.
Shine a light on reveals an issue for examination.
A report can shine a light on a gap before anyone fixes it.

advanced-native-4655.text: Weekend workshops brought young makers into the quiet repair hall and breathed fresh life into the space.
The evening performances breathed fresh life into the old square, bringing residents back after years of quiet.
Breathe fresh life into marks a place or activity becoming lively again.
Breathing fresh life into a venue does not repair every defect.

advanced-native-4656.text: Hundreds of spectators poured into the small stadium after the gates opened.
When the free concert ended, families poured into the nearby food hall, and staff opened another serving line.
Pour into describes a large group arriving at a place.
People can pour into a venue without causing an accident.

advanced-native-4658.text: As the parade crowd left the square, the medic tried to reach the stage against the flow; it felt like swimming upstream.
Keeping a repair café open while nearby shops switch to disposable goods feels like swimming upstream, but volunteers continue.
Swimming upstream means moving against a strong opposing force.
A project can be swimming upstream and still keep making progress.

advanced-native-4664.text: Thousands visit the tiny cliff path each weekend, wearing away the soil they came to admire. They may be loving the path to death.
The small garden is loved, but repeated shortcutting has worn its flower beds away; visitors may love the garden to death.
Love a place to death describes popularity that damages it.
To love a site to death, visits must cause real harm, not just be numerous.

advanced-native-4670.text: The festival app lists hundreds of talks, films and workshops; visitors face a sea of choices.
The library catalogue gives us a sea of choices, so I will filter by language and publication year first.
A sea of choices means a very large range of options.
A sea of choices can contain good options; filters help compare them.

advanced-native-4673.text: The app ranks parks using only photo uploads, but some users treat its list like gospel and never check access hours.
Do not treat the restaurant score like gospel; its sample is small, so read recent inspection details as well.
Treat X like gospel means accept it without questioning.
Not treating a source like gospel does not mean assuming it is false.

advanced-native-4679.text: The speaker was told noon, but the driver was told one o’clock. A quick call cleared up the crossed wires.
The guide and coach driver got their wires crossed over the pickup time, so they called to confirm the correct hour.
Crossed wires means a communication mix-up.
People can have crossed wires without anyone lying.

advanced-native-4682.text: The venue has step-free access and the right capacity, so the main boxes are ticked; the organiser will still inspect the sound system.
The hall ticks the boxes for seating and access, but we must test the microphones before confirming the booking.
Tick the boxes means satisfy listed requirements.
Even if boxes are ticked, quality beyond the list may need checking.

advanced-native-4685.text: The studio’s unclear cancellation policy put several parents off booking a class.
The unclear refund rule puts new members off joining, so the club will rewrite it in plain language.
Put people off means discourage them from an action.
Putting some users off does not mean every user refuses.

advanced-native-4691.text: More apprentices completed training and found local jobs this year, giving the repair programme a bright future if funding continues.
With more students enrolling and two new mentors, the workshop has a bright future if its equipment funding holds.
Bright future means promising prospects, not certainty.
A bright future is more credible when supported by evidence.

advanced-native-4700.text: The clinic launched a glossy website, but its appointment line still disconnects most callers; the redesign is window dressing until access improves.
A new sign is window dressing if the library still has no evening entrance for wheelchair users.
Window dressing is appealing surface without needed substance.
Call a change window dressing only after naming the unresolved core issue.

advanced-native-4707.text: After the long hike, Jun slept like a log and did not wake when light rain hit the tent.
After the overnight journey, I slept like a log even while my friends quietly packed their bags.
Sleep like a log means sleep very deeply.
Sleeping like a log is about depth, not a medical diagnosis.

advanced-native-4709.text: The guesthouse faces the festival square, with performances and food stalls outside all evening; guests are right in the thick of things.
Our information desk is right in the thick of things beside the main exhibition entrance, so volunteers hear questions as visitors arrive.
In the thick of things means close to the centre of activity.
Right in the thick of things adds emphasis, not danger.

advanced-native-4444.text: The treasurer promised clearer event accounts. She posted itemised receipts and answered members’ questions. Her actions can sometimes speak louder than words because members can check the figures.
A mentor said he would support the new technicians, then protected a weekly practice hour and reviewed their work; actions can sometimes speak louder than words when support is this visible.
Actions can sometimes speak louder than words when they support a promise.
Visible follow-through shows why actions can sometimes speak louder than words.

advanced-native-4445.text: Leah had designed the poster, but the small type was hard to read. She disliked admitting the problem, yet swallowed her pride, asked a younger designer to review it and enlarged the text before printing.
The curator swallowed her pride when a student identified a label error; she checked the archive, credited the student and corrected the display.
Swallow your pride means set aside ego to do what is needed.
A leader may swallow her pride and accept a useful correction.

advanced-native-4450.text: At the university canteen, Hana tasted a soup seasoned with the same herb her grandfather used. It was a taste of home for her, although it had been cooked in a city she had never visited before.
The toasted seed flavour gave Arun a taste of home during the school trip because it reminded him of breakfasts his father used to make.
Food can taste of home when its flavour recalls familiar people and places.
A familiar spice may offer a taste of home far from family.

advanced-native-4462.text: Nora kept a repaired wooden box from her first theatre tour. Her crew had painted a small star on it after a difficult final show, and she could name everyone involved. The box came with a story attached, not just a worn surface.
The brass key came with a story attached: its owner could explain how a closed station became a reading room and why volunteers kept the key.
