Come with a story attached means carry a known personal or cultural history.
An old object can come with a story attached when its history is known.

advanced-native-4466.text: The storytelling night began so older residents could share local memories. The organiser cut each story to fifteen seconds for sponsor clips. Regulars worried the event would lose its soul because nobody could finish a memory.
The local music night could lose its soul if neighbours stop playing together and the programme becomes nothing but sponsor videos.
Lose its soul means lose the purpose that gave something meaning.
A festival can lose its soul when shared work becomes mere display.

advanced-native-4470.text: The neighbourhood magazine moved online and added audio interviews. It kept its roots by letting long-time residents edit the local-history section and check the place names before publication.
The craft journal kept its roots after launching a video channel: older makers still taught the signature knot and checked every demonstration.
Keep its roots means preserve a real connection to origins.
A community troupe can keep its roots alive when long-time members continue teaching the original songs.

advanced-native-4474.text: The old observatory dome had been closed for years because its gears jammed. Volunteers repaired the mechanism and began weekly sky sessions for schools. The restoration gave the dome a new lease of life.
The repaired public piano gained a new lease of life when neighbours began weekly lessons and lunchtime performances in the station hall.
A new lease of life is renewed activity after decline.
Repairs can give a closed space a new lease of life when people use it again.

advanced-native-4481.text: The museum still required printed booking emails after switching to digital tickets. People without printers were turned away even though staff could check a code on screen. A trustee called the entry rule stuck in the past.
The archive felt stuck in the past when it made researchers travel for a printed index already available securely online; the director then revised the access rule.
Stuck in the past means failing to adapt to a real present need.
Keeping a useful tradition does not make a group stuck in the past.

advanced-native-4488.text: A neighbourhood reading circle moved into a radio programme when its meeting room closed. Readers now record short passages and discuss them by phone. The circle changed shape, but its shared reading continued.
The local debate changed shape when it moved from a stage panel to small tables, but residents still compared proposals and recorded questions.
Change shape means take a different form.
An event can change shape and still keep its central purpose.

advanced-native-4492.text: The community workshop has used the same adjustable benches for twenty years. Their joints can be tightened and damaged boards replaced without discarding the frame. The benches were built to last, though they still need maintenance.
The school’s drafting tables were built to last: even after many classes, staff could replace the hinges and keep the sturdy tops in service.
Built to last means made for long useful service.
Replaceable parts can show why an item was built to last.

advanced-native-4497.text: The restored station hall kept its carved ticket windows and patterned floor tiles. Visitors praised its old-world charm, while the operator also installed a step-free entrance.
The reading room’s old-world charm came from its carved shelving and stained glass, not from the broken heater that staff later repaired.
Old-world charm is appeal from older design or craftsmanship.
A building can keep old-world charm while improving access.

advanced-native-4499.text: The portable projector had a steel case, thick corner guards and a handle that needed two people to lift. The technician laughed that it was built like a tank, though its weight made setup slower.
With its thick steel shell and protected switches, the ticket machine looked built like a tank; two workers still needed a trolley to move it.
Built like a tank means exceptionally solid and often bulky.
A machine built like a tank may resist knocks but be hard to carry.

advanced-native-2831.text: The theatre has chosen its new director, but the name will remain under wraps until the board tells staff on Monday.
The chef’s new menu is under wraps until the tasting event, although the dishes have already been tested.
Under wraps means not yet shared publicly.
A decision can be final while its announcement remains under wraps.

advanced-native-3806.text: Each missed bus leads to a late shift and lost pay; the reduced pay then makes the next bus pass unaffordable. The worker is trapped in a cycle of transport costs and lost wages.
The shop keeps borrowing to cover its rent, and interest raises the next payment; it is trapped in a cycle of debt and interest.
Trapped in a cycle of X requires a recurring hardship pattern.
Trapped in a cycle of debt means one round of hardship helps cause the next.

advanced-native-3813.text: A free bicycle-repair course gives delivery riders a hand up: they can maintain their own bikes and keep earning after the course ends.
The library’s free digital-skills workshops offer older residents a hand up when they need to book services online.
A hand up is help that enables further progress.
A hand up offers a path or skill, not a guarantee of success.

advanced-native-3814.text: A paid apprenticeship and steady childcare let Asha keep a full-time job over several years. Those changes helped her family break out of poverty.
With reliable transport and a permanent contract, the workers are beginning to break out of poverty after years of unstable pay.
Break out of poverty means escape an enduring low-income condition.
A single payment may help without proving that a family has broken out of poverty.

advanced-native-4078.text: The mountain clinic stocked up on bandages before the road closed for repairs, so it could keep treating patients all week.
The volunteer centre is stocking up on bottled water ahead of the summer sports day.
Stock up on supplies before they are needed.
Stocking up on supplies does not itself imply panic buying.

advanced-native-4079.text: The repair shop has a three-week waiting list for bicycle mechanics; their skills are in demand.
Experienced captioners are in demand because several theatres are recruiting them this season.
In demand means wanted by many people.
Being in demand alone does not establish price or quality.

advanced-native-4087.text: The trainer filled every blank on the practice sheet before the apprentices tried it; she spoon-fed them the solutions.
Instead of spoon-feeding the trainees every answer, the supervisor asks them to compare two possible repairs and explain their choice.
Spoon-feeding learners means supplying answers instead of requiring their thinking.
A useful hint need not spoon-feed students every answer.

advanced-native-4095.text: Nora expected a quiet weekend at the cabin, but construction started outside at dawn and continued all day. The stay was nowhere near what she imagined.
The rehearsal turned into a full public performance, nowhere near what the dancers had expected when they signed up for a private practice.
Nowhere near what someone imagined signals a large expectation gap.
Being nowhere near what you imagined does not mean the experience had no value.

advanced-native-2237.text: After school, Ellis watched clips during meals, skipped his usual football game and kept checking videos while friends visited. His leisure began to revolve around a screen, so he agreed to set aside time for the game and meals.
For a month, the club members’ breaks revolved around a screen: even their shared lunch became a time to scroll rather than talk.
Revolve around a screen means organise much of life around viewing.
Leisure can revolve around a screen when other activities repeatedly disappear.

advanced-native-2273.text: Maya found a charity’s claim in a poster. She treated it as a starting point, then checked the annual report and asked how the figure had been calculated before citing it in class.
The short interview was a starting point for the historian, who then compared the speaker’s memory with dated letters and a train record.
A starting point is an initial basis for further inquiry.
A poster can be a starting point if you check its underlying evidence.

advanced-native-2275.text: The event flyer listed the new venue but not the step-free entrance. The editor realised the short version had left things out that some visitors needed, so she added the access line before printing.
The first report left things out about the trial’s access rules, so the team added who could join before sharing it more widely.
Leave things out means omit information from an account.
A brief notice may leave things out that readers need to act.

advanced-native-2276.text: A tutor’s first explanation of the water cycle used only abstract terms. She then drew arrows showing evaporation, clouds and rain. The sequence became easier to grasp when students could explain where the water went.
A simple timeline made the museum’s restoration process easier to grasp; visitors could now tell which repairs came before the final reopening.
Easier to grasp means easier to understand.
A diagram can make a difficult sequence easier to grasp.

advanced-native-2279.text: A cycling group asked the council for a safer crossing. Its request was grounded in facts: a traffic count and three dated incident reports showed the junction was busy at school leaving time.
The committee’s flood warning was grounded in evidence from two measured river levels, although the members said the timing of the peak remained uncertain.
Grounded in facts means supported by checkable evidence.
A claim grounded in evidence can still have limits.

advanced-native-2281.text: The youth orchestra waited for the audition results. Mari felt hopeful after her solo, anxious when the first names were read, then relieved when her group qualified. The afternoon was an emotional ride.
The debate result made Lena proud at first, nervous during the recount and grateful when both teams congratulated each other; it was an emotional ride rather than a single happy moment.
An emotional ride involves changes in strong feelings over time.
An emotional ride needs events that turn hope into fear or relief.

advanced-native-2282.text: In the radio play, the actor paused just before revealing whose footsteps were outside the door. The quiet gap heightened the drama because listeners had time to worry about who might enter.
The podcast let the witness finish describing the empty platform before revealing the delayed train announcement; that order heightened the drama without inventing a new event.
Heighten the drama means increase a scene’s emotional tension.
A pause or reveal can heighten the drama when the outcome matters.

advanced-native-2289.text: Two cafés opened nearby. One kept meals affordable; the other used premium events to fund free music lessons. Turnover alone could not settle which succeeded: they were playing different games.
A public library and a specialist archive both lend material, but one aims for quick everyday access and the other preserves rare records; they are playing different games.
Playing different games means pursuing different goals or rules.
When groups are playing different games, compare each against the outcome it values.

advanced-native-2309.text: The community mural was painted, but the team still had to confirm the artist credit and obtain permission for the launch photograph. Those loose ends had to be settled before the public page went online.
The repairs were complete, but loose ends remained: the manager still needed a warranty copy and the caretaker had to confirm the new key list.
Loose ends are unresolved details, not the whole unfinished project.
Name the loose ends and the person who will settle them.

advanced-native-2311.text: For years, Amira did not know why her mentor had suddenly left. A letter from the mentor explained the move and thanked her for their work. Reading it gave Amira a moment of closure, though she still missed him.
When the archived note finally explained the cancelled exhibition, Noor had a moment of closure; she understood the decision even though she still wished it had gone ahead.
A moment of closure resolves some emotional uncertainty.
A moment of closure can coexist with sadness or disappointment.

advanced-native-2313.text: In a fictional play, a daughter rehearses an apology but cannot say it when her father answers the phone. The event is invented, yet it captures emotional truths about pride, fear and the wish to repair a bond.
The animated story is set on another planet, but it reveals emotional truths about a newcomer wanting acceptance while hiding uncertainty from friends.
Emotional truths are insights about feelings, not factual plot claims.
Fiction can reveal emotional truths through recognisable relationships.

advanced-native-2324.text: A short play shows a father proud of his daughter’s new job but uneasy that she will move away. Later scenes let him support her while admitting he will miss her. That mixture gives the simple plot emotional depth.
The comic gained emotional depth when the usually cheerful guide admitted both pride in the team and fear of letting it down over several chapters.
Emotional depth comes from nuanced feelings that develop.
A simple plot can have emotional depth without a shocking twist.

advanced-native-2329.text: An advert says the new bottle keeps water cold twice as long as the old one. The company’s own tests show only a small gain under one condition. The benefit may be overstated, although the new bottle does perform slightly better there.
The travel notice described the new shuttle as always punctual, but three late runs in its first week made that promise look overstated.
Overstated means stronger than the evidence warrants.
An overstated claim may still contain a smaller truth.

advanced-native-2336.text: After the community garden closed, Leo told everyone he was fine but stopped joining their calls. He later admitted he had been holding everything in because he did not want to burden his friends.
Arun realised he had been holding everything in after the workshop closed; he finally told his cousin he was disappointed and asked only for a quiet conversation.
Holding everything in means keeping feelings unspoken.
Someone can stop holding everything in by choosing a trusted listener.

advanced-native-2337.text: A school film ends with a quiet apology. In the edit, repeated thunder sounds and three slow-motion replays make the apology harder to hear. The ending feels overcooked because the effects drown out the simple exchange.
The dance finale felt overcooked when three projections competed with the soloist’s final movement, leaving viewers unsure where to look.
Overcooked can criticise an artistic choice that adds too much.
An overcooked ending may lose the subtle feeling it meant to strengthen.

advanced-native-2339.text: The audience knew Mara as a comic host, but in the play she adopted the cautious pauses and clipped answers of a shy archivist. Viewers stopped waiting for her usual jokes; she seemed to disappear into a role.
During the reading, Jun changed his familiar brisk speech into a careful, uncertain voice, and the audience followed the anxious courier; he had begun to disappear into a role.
Disappear into a role describes convincing transformation in acting.
To disappear into a role, behaviour must shift audience focus to the character.

advanced-native-2348.text: The council first discussed a park path only by construction cost. A resident asked them to view it through the lens of accessibility: could a wheelchair user reach the toilets without steps? The new question did not make cost irrelevant.
Looking at the library redesign through the lens of education led the team to ask whether young readers could find the materials they needed, not just whether shelves were cheaper.
Through the lens of public health names a perspective that changes what we ask.
A plan viewed through the lens of accessibility still needs other checks.

advanced-native-2585.text: Tara enjoyed painting, but every friend in her feed posted costly fashion hauls. She nearly spent her art-course savings to match them, then realised she was caught up in social pressure and kept the course money.
Arun almost changed his subject choice because his friends mocked the course he wanted; he recognised he was caught up in social pressure and asked the adviser about his own goals.
Caught up in social pressure means letting others’ expectations drive a choice.
Someone caught up in social pressure can still pause and reconsider.

advanced-native-2657.text: A small ceramics page usually had a few dozen views. After a museum shared one repair video, it reached hundreds of thousands in two days. The clip blew up overnight, though orders remained modest.
The choir’s rehearsal clip blew up overnight after a school network shared it, but the members waited to see whether viewers would also attend the concert.
Blow up overnight means gain wide attention very fast.
A post that blows up overnight may not keep that audience.

advanced-native-2785.text: The town festival will include craft workshops, short films and an evening folk concert. Music is part of the mix, but visitors can attend the workshops without going to the concert.
The youth centre still offers board games, but they are part of the mix alongside tutoring and outdoor walks.
Part of the mix means one element among several.
Name the other components when you say something is part of the mix.

advanced-native-2859.text: By lunchtime, Mei had seen dozens of election alerts from different angles. She could no longer tell which article she had read fully and felt she was drowning in headlines, so she chose two reports to examine.
After the storm, I was drowning in headlines from several districts and kept confusing warnings with damage reports, so I opened the official updates one area at a time.
Drowning in headlines means overwhelmed by headline volume.
Someone drowning in headlines can sort and verify a smaller set.

advanced-native-2868.text: Leah had not been searching for the missing festival notice. While checking an unrelated article in the library archive, she ran into it in a scanned newsletter and saved the reference for the organiser.
The missing label was in a repair manual; I ran into it while looking for a wiring diagram.
Ran into it can mean unexpectedly encountered the named item.
To say you ran into it, first make clear what it refers to.

advanced-native-2920.text: The original safety card had twelve decorative icons and buried the exit route. The revised card kept one clear map and three steps; volunteers found the route faster. For these instructions, less really is more.
The ticket page removed three repeated banners but kept price and access details, and readers found booking information sooner; less really is more in this layout.
Less is more when cutting clutter improves the result.
Less really is more only if essential information remains.

advanced-native-2924.text: After the trainees completed the repair course, their instructor offered the community room and arranged snacks for a small celebration. She decided to throw a party for the group on Friday.
The reading club will throw a party for its retiring librarian in the small hall, with former members invited to share a short memory.
Throw a party means organise a celebration.
The person who throws a party arranges it rather than just attends.

advanced-native-2956.text: The club considered announcing a trip before checking the accessible bus. A volunteer warned that if families paid deposits and the transport failed, organisers would be picking up the pieces afterwards by arranging refunds and new travel.
After the rushed app update confused users about the new booking time, the team was picking up the pieces afterwards by restoring old reservations and sending corrected notices.
Pick up the pieces means deal with damage after a bad outcome.
Avoid a rushed promise if others must pick up the pieces afterwards.

advanced-native-2961.text: A costly health fair had banners, cameras and a long opening speech, but no appointment desk or written guidance for visitors. Several people left without knowing where to seek help. It felt more show than substance.
The park project’s illuminated model impressed visitors, but with no confirmed accessible path in the actual plan it risked becoming more show than substance.
More show than substance contrasts display with actual value.
A polished launch can be all glitter and no substance if the promised help is still missing.

advanced-native-3487.text: A celebrity’s surprise wedding led every evening news page, while a new flood-warning map received only a short item. The wedding grabbed the headlines, though the map mattered more to some residents.
The visiting chef’s new restaurant grabbed the headlines across town, while a quieter report on library hours appeared only inside the papers.
Grab the headlines means dominate prominent news attention.
A story that grabs the headlines is not automatically the most important.

advanced-native-3564.text: The central office changed branch hours without asking counter staff about queues, then sent each branch the fixed schedule. The change came from the top down; staff could report problems during the trial.
The museum changed volunteer shifts from the top down when senior staff sent a completed roster before asking gallery guides about visitor patterns.
From the top down describes a decision led by authority above.
A plan set from the top down may still change after feedback.

advanced-native-3572.text: For the school hiking route, pupils could suggest sights they wanted to visit, but trained leaders chose the safe path after checking weather alerts. The leaders remained in the driver’s seat on safety while listening to pupils.
The apprentices suggested ways to display the tools, but the workshop manager was in the driver’s seat on electrical safety after reviewing the wiring report.
In the driver’s seat means holding the key decision power.
Someone in the driver’s seat can still listen to others.

advanced-native-3658.text: The repair café opens every Saturday, but Mina only visits now and then when she has a small item to mend. Last month she went once and this month she has not yet been.
We still walk along the old harbour now and then, especially when an exhibition gives us a reason to revisit it.
Now and then means occasionally, not constantly.
An activity done now and then need not follow an exact schedule.

advanced-native-3676.text: The choir lost its hall and members were disappointed. A library room let them rehearse acoustic pieces and welcome neighbours. They called that opportunity a fresh start rather than a setback, though storage still needed work.
The cooking club found a fresh start rather than a setback in a shared kitchen, teaching neighbours while managing bookings.
A fresh start rather than a setback needs a concrete new path.
Calling change a fresh start rather than a setback need not deny difficulty.

advanced-native-2514.text: A library replaced confusing shelf labels in April. In May, volunteers counted fewer books returned to the wrong shelves. The improvement showed up in the weekly figures, although the team still needs to check other possible causes.
After the repair team sealed the window, the difference showed up in the following week’s lower heating readings.
A difference shows up when a later measure makes it visible.
People may show up at a meeting; an effect shows up in the figures.

advanced-native-2578.text: At the community garden, new volunteers planted beside a mentor who checked their watering plan. Those joint shifts served as training wheels: by the fourth week, the volunteers could plan a bed on their own.
The sample invoice served as training wheels while the trainees learnt to check real bills.
A labelled mixing bowl can act like training wheels for a novice baker who later measures without the labels.
A sample form served as training wheels for the first application, but the learner completed the next one alone.

advanced-native-3505.text: The small ceramic bowl has tiny painted scenes around its rim. The display invites visitors to linger and notice them.
The garden path invites visitors to linger near the night-blooming flowers, where their scent is strongest.
A small detail can invite visitors to linger without forcing them to stay.
An image can invite visitors to linger; name the details rather than claiming everyone reacts alike.

advanced-native-3647.text: At the workshop, mentors offered regular check-ins while letting teenagers choose their own projects. One organiser called that giving them roots and wings.
The makerspace gave learners roots and wings by pairing them with a mentor while allowing them to design their own tools.
Roots and wings combine dependable support with room to explore.
Roots and wings do not prescribe one family arrangement or a sudden break in contact.

advanced-native-3726.text: The library lost its largest donation, but smaller pledges and a new fundraising date remain. The loss is not a death sentence for the library.
The cancelled exhibition slot was not a death sentence for the project; the artists found a second venue and still had to confirm its costs.
A setback need not be a death sentence if a credible next option remains.
Not a death sentence is strong; separate a possible future from a guaranteed outcome.

advanced-native-3788.text: The repair café used photos of neighbours fixing old radios to project an image of practical cooperation. Organisers still surveyed visitors to see whether the message came across.
The volunteer team projected an image of openness by publishing its meeting times, then invited newcomers to report whether joining felt easy.
A poster can project an image, but real experiences test whether it fits.
A group may project an image that differs from what its actions establish.

advanced-native-3841.text: A regional training scheme offers evening classes and travel grants, making better-paid jobs more accessible to workers who cannot leave daytime work. It aims to support upward mobility.
Affordable evening courses can support upward mobility when people can attend them without losing their daytime income.
Upward mobility needs accessible routes, not only inspiring stories.
Upward mobility may become more possible through an opportunity, but the outcome is not guaranteed.

advanced-native-4147.text: Mira left a bright ribbon beside her lunch box to remember the form. Her teacher compared the cue to tying a string around your finger.
A coloured tag on the folder served the same purpose as tying a string around your finger: it reminded the team to review the form before sending it.
Tying a string around your finger is a reminder, not the completed task.
Tying a string around your finger illustrates how a visible cue helps only when someone acts on it.

advanced-native-3142.text: When the lighthouse warning flashed, the keeper called the harbour office at once.
The caretaker turned off the tap at once when water began leaking, then called maintenance.
Call for help at once when the agreed warning appears.
At once may also mean simultaneously; the surrounding events reveal which sense fits.

advanced-native-3308.text: The outdoor lecture was planned for the courtyard, but sudden rain moved everyone into the library. The day did not follow a script.
Life does not always follow a script: our picnic moved indoors after the park closed, but we kept the group meal.
Life does not always follow a script, but a revised plan can still be clear.
The festival team keeps a rain plan because life rarely sticks to the script.

advanced-native-3394.text: At the visitor centre, Dara picked up a trail map from the information desk before the walk.
I picked up a booklet about the old harbour at the information desk, but I checked the price before leaving.
You can pick up a map at the centre, but ask whether there is a fee.
Pick up a booklet names obtaining an item; identify the object and setting before choosing a sense.

advanced-native-2413.text: At the school exhibition meeting, the designer asked whether the label could be read from a wheelchair, and the access officer suggested a lower position. Their back-and-forth led to a revised display plan before printing.
The back-and-forth between the two librarians revealed that they were using different dates for the same event.
A short back-and-forth with the caretaker settled where the notice should go.
The back-and-forth was useful because each side heard the other’s missing detail.

advanced-native-2467.text: A travel app claimed its routes were always step-free. A tester checked three listed stations and found two without lift access. The claim fell apart under closer inspection, so the team changed the wording.
The slogan fell apart under closer inspection when the label showed that the supposed zero-sugar drink contained syrup.
A broad claim can fall apart under closer inspection when one omitted detail changes the result.
Check the figures before claiming that an argument falls apart under closer inspection.

advanced-native-2505.text: The volunteer desk tried to answer calls, file forms and welcome arrivals at the same time. Attention was thinly spread, and two visitors waited without directions; the coordinator assigned one person to each task.
We spread our attention too thin across five poster designs and failed to proofread the date on the final one.
When attention is thinly spread, a small check can be the first thing lost.
Do not spread your attention too thin when a safety decision needs a careful check.

advanced-native-2473.text: The neighbourhood library still lends books, but this year it began lending gardening tools and teaching basic repairs. It is branching out into practical-skills services; staff will review demand before buying more equipment.
The local history society branched out into guided walking tours after years of archiving photographs, but it began with one small trial route.
A small bakery branched out into classes only after checking that customers wanted them.
Selling more of the same product is growth, but it is not necessarily branching out into a new area.

advanced-native-2513.text: A theatre sold tickets before confirming wheelchair access. The seats were later changed and refunds offered, but the mistake cast a long shadow: some audience members still checked access independently the next season.
The data leak cast a long shadow over the service, because users were still changing passwords months after the fix.
A decision can cast a long shadow if people remain cautious after the apology.
Show the later consequence before saying an old error casts a long shadow.

advanced-native-2531.text: A neighbourhood food bank changed its opening hours twice, but its rule to serve people without judging them stayed constant. That rule held everything up as volunteers adjusted the rota and kept the service welcoming.
The access pledge held everything up when the festival changed sites, because every team still checked entrances before announcing a venue.
A clear founding principle can hold everything up through several practical changes.
If a missing form holds everything up, it is delaying work rather than supporting it.

advanced-native-2627.text: Rafi received a small travel allowance for a four-day trip. He blew it all at once on the first evening’s souvenirs and then had to ask for a bus fare on day three.
She almost blew it all at once at the market, but kept enough of the grant to replace a damaged tool later.
He blew it all at once on a flashy stand and could not buy the cables the next day.
Before you blow it all at once, check what the money must still cover.

advanced-native-2668.text: The class compared a local lullaby with a lullaby from another region, then asked why each community used different rhythms. The lesson opened ears and minds: pupils heard new sounds and reconsidered what a bedtime song could be.
The guest drummer’s lesson opened ears and minds: the class heard a new rhythm and learnt why it marked a harvest celebration.
A whistle-language demonstration can open ears and minds when visitors learn how messages travel across a valley.
If a class only turns up the volume, it has not necessarily opened ears and minds.

advanced-native-2677.text: For decades, older workers taught new staff the harbour’s hand signals. The last instructor retired without training a successor, and an important thread was broken: the next team knew the rules on paper but not the shared signals.
When the final gardener left without teaching anyone how to save the rare seeds, an important thread was broken between the old and new volunteers.
An important thread is broken when a practice reaches no one in the next generation.
An important thread is broken only if teaching stops, not merely because the meeting place changes.

advanced-native-2700.text: The cinema added captions to every late showing, not only one special event. The change sent the message that deaf viewers belonged in its regular audience, though managers still asked them whether the captions worked well.
By publishing the selection criteria before auditions, the orchestra sent the message that applicants deserved a fair process.
A visible policy can send the message that a neglected group matters.
An action may send the message, but audience reaction still has to be checked.

advanced-native-4310.text: The tenants had to choose between two roof repairs, but no one had shown them the costs or the leak report. At the meeting, Mei said they were walking through fog until those details arrived.
Without the flood map, our planning team is walking through fog about where homes can be built.
When the organiser hid the rehearsal dates, the new cast felt like they were walking through fog.
Clear allergy labels stopped shoppers from walking through fog about what the meal contained.

advanced-native-4368.text: The cycling club's advert hardly mentioned bike specifications. It showed newcomers laughing together after a ride and sold a feeling of belonging to a group.
The poster sells a feeling of welcome by showing neighbours greeting first-time visitors.
The garden advert sold a feeling of peace with slow shots of a shaded bench.
A repair shop can sell a feeling of relief in its advert, but customers still need a clear written estimate.

advanced-native-4386.text: On the train, Ada's headphones made a sound bubble around her audiobook. She could focus on the story, but she turned the volume down before the station announcement.
My headphones create a sound bubble for editing music, but I pause the track when the stage manager calls.
The library headset made a sound bubble around the language lesson, yet the student still checked the closing time.
A quiet rehearsal mix can feel like a sound bubble; keep an ear open for the conductor's signal.

advanced-native-4390.text: At the school recital, Ben spent the whole final song adjusting his phone camera. He kept the video, but later could not describe the choir's live ending; he had missed the moment.
I nearly missed the moment at the concert while checking messages, so I put my phone away for the final song.
Filming the whole meal might make Sam miss the moment when his grandfather tells the recipe story.
I did not miss the moment at the exhibition: after one photo, I listened to the artist explain the work.

advanced-native-4448.text: At the harbour food fair, an elder showed how workers once dried fish before long voyages. The snack tasted familiar to her family; she called it edible history because the method carried a memory of that work.
The festival bread is edible history because its grain mix recalls how families baked during the old harvest season.
A baker's festival bun can be edible history when its shape recalls an old neighbourhood celebration.
The preserved-vegetable dish was edible history for the family, though its recipe told only one part of their past.

advanced-native-4576.text: After the clinic introduced an online appointment calendar, Nila could see open times without waiting on the telephone. She said it was hard to go back to the old call queue, though the phone line still worked.
After the recipe app sorted ingredients for me, it was hard to go back to searching through loose pages.
The new caption search made it hard to go back to finding each interview quote by hand.
Once the team could share live edits, it was hard to go back to emailing separate copies, though email remained possible.

advanced-native-4588.text: Leila cares for her father after her morning shift and has only one free evening a week. For her, time is a luxury, so the committee offered a shorter volunteer slot instead of assuming she could attend every meeting.
For the school meal team, time is a luxury during the morning rush, so clear labels save repeated checks.
For the night-shift nurse, time is a luxury, so the workshop offered a short recorded session.
When volunteers have care duties, time is a luxury; flexible tasks can help them stay involved.

advanced-native-4611.text: For one weekend, a bus driver joined a mountain sketching retreat with no timetables to manage. That break let her leave ordinary life behind for a while, although her driving shift resumed on Monday.
At the lakeside painting weekend, I left ordinary life behind for two days and returned to my shop on Monday.
On the night train, she left ordinary life behind for a few hours, knowing her shift began after the trip.
A two-day garden retreat lets the team leave ordinary life behind without pretending their obligations have vanished.

advanced-native-4689.text: The coastal town copied and pasted a mountain city's winter market plan. Its open-air stalls offered no shade, even though local visitors came during hot afternoons. The organisers changed the layout after hearing those complaints.
A city bakery cannot copy and paste the harvest festival recipe whose meaning comes from one village's farming history.
A copied festival plan failed because the town did not adapt it to its shorter daylight hours; it was copy and paste planning.
Borrow the courtyard idea, but do not copy and paste the other school's lunch schedule if your pupils leave earlier.

advanced-native-3340.text: The community workshop has a venue, but the bus timetable will change next month. The organisers will pin the start time down after the new timetable is published.
The library can pin the date down once the visiting author confirms her travel plans.
We can pin the date down once everyone has confirmed their availability.
Pinning everything down too early can leave no room for new information.

advanced-native-4012.text: Lena missed the regional swimming team by a few seconds. After a day to reflect, she got back up and returned to morning training with a revised start technique.
The chess club lost its sponsor, but it can get back up by testing a smaller tournament before seeking new funding.
Getting back up means trying again after a setback, not proving the next attempt will succeed.
She got back up by returning to practice with a clearer plan.

advanced-native-4038.text: Maya works late on Thursdays, yet she keeps turning up for the evening language class. She has attended every week this term and asks for help when a word is unclear.
Even before he could paint a full mural, Jun kept turning up for the community art sessions each weekend.
Keep turning up points to repeated attendance, not a promise of quick success.
Mina kept turning up for practice through the winter and learned from each session.

advanced-native-4315.text: A museum sign said “Closed for repairs today.” The coordinator meant only the east gallery, but visitors thought the whole museum was shut. It came across the wrong way, so she named the room in a new notice.
A short note about a delayed parcel could come across the wrong way unless the shop explains the new delivery date.
An invitation without a clear time may come across the wrong way.
If a comment came across the wrong way, explain the intention without blaming the reader.

advanced-native-3151.text: The community centre still accepts online bookings, but a missing approval code means staff must phone each applicant before confirming a place. That extra step is sand in the gears of an otherwise working system.
Incompatible file formats were sand in the gears of the river survey, because volunteers had to convert each report before combining the results.
A missing handoff can be sand in the gears even while the service keeps running.
Find the sand in the gears before asking the whole team to work faster.

advanced-native-3513.text: The city library replaced one long archive introduction with six bite-sized audio guides. Each guide lasts four minutes and covers one collection, though visitors may still need help with unfamiliar terms.
The archive team turned its long scanning guide into bite-sized cards, one for naming files and another for checking image quality.
Bite-sized lessons reduce the amount presented at once; they do not make every idea easy.
The editor made the guide bite-sized by separating the checks into short cards.

advanced-native-4241.text: At the neighbourhood planning meeting, two groups began speaking over one another. Mei held the room together by giving each side two minutes and returning everyone to the map of the proposed route.
When the workshop questions scattered, the facilitator held the room together by returning each speaker to the shared design sketch.
A good moderator can hold the room together without demanding agreement.
She held the room together by returning each contribution to the question everyone had come to discuss.

advanced-native-4396.text: The delivery team moved metal shelves beside the reading room while pupils were studying. The shelves made an unnecessary racket, so the manager moved the work to after closing time.
The loose trolley wheels made a racket outside the clinic, so the staff moved the supplies by hand until the wheels were repaired.
The bins made a racket before dawn, so the collection time was changed.
Before saying the volunteers made a racket, explain who heard the noise and when.

advanced-native-2507.text: Our community archive put interview notes into an app that deletes each draft at midnight. For a record we need next month, that is like writing on water; we should export the notes before they disappear.
Relying on a disappearing message for the exhibition inventory would be like writing on water, so I will save a dated copy.
If equipment checks are recorded only on fading stickers, the audit trail may be like writing on water.
Save the field measurements before the temporary display closes; otherwise the work may be written in water.

advanced-native-2750.text: Mina kept the paper badge from her first community play, even though it no longer opened any doors. It became a keepsake because it reminded her of rehearsing with her brother.
I kept the tiny paper crane as a keepsake from the workshop because it reminds me of what we made together.
A pressed flower became a keepsake of their first school exhibition.
A museum label may have archival value, but it becomes a personal keepsake only when someone connects it to a lived memory.

advanced-native-3025.text: Mina stopped showing the bold paintings she loves because she thinks the judges prefer quiet landscapes. Her tutor says she can learn from their advice without erasing herself.
A mentor told Ravi that adapting to the lab did not mean he had to erase himself; he could ask for quiet work time and still join the group review.
A useful compromise makes room for others without asking you to erase yourself.
If joining a group means you must erase yourself, discuss a clearer boundary.

advanced-native-3148.text: Our rehearsal leader usually explains mistakes calmly. After three nights of poor sleep, she snaps at small slips. The late schedule has shortened her fuse, so we are ending practice earlier this week.
Back-to-back travel days shortened their fuse, so the guides agreed to rotate the early briefing instead of blaming each other for every delay.
Lack of rest can shorten your fuse even if you are usually patient.
Name the pressure that shortened their fuse before judging the reaction alone.

advanced-native-3276.text: The gallery rule says visitors cannot bring in large bags, but it does not say what counts as large. Staff give different answers at the door. The rule is soft around the edges until a size limit is stated.
The rehearsal policy was soft around the edges because it allowed 'late use' without saying when the building had to close.
A rule is soft around the edges when borderline cases receive different answers.
If a policy is soft around the edges, define the missing limit before enforcing it.

advanced-native-3504.text: The museum audio guide keeps speaking as visitors hurry between rooms. Facts wash over them, and few can recall a detail. I suggest stopping at one display and discussing what they heard.
During the workshop, the commentary washed over me until I put my phone away and wrote down one question about the process.
When instructions wash over you, pause and repeat one key step.
A lecture may wash over them if they listen while doing another demanding task.

advanced-native-3656.text: At the repair cafe, the trainer demonstrates the first shift and stays nearby for questions. Then the new volunteers choose how to divide the next tasks. She wants to support them without smothering them.
The cycling instructor supported her without smothering her: he checked the brakes, then let her choose a safe route for the next ride.
Support them without smothering them: teach the safety step, then leave a real choice.
A good mentor can support her without smothering her during a first independent task.

advanced-native-3867.text: At the volunteer network, a coordinator hid several donations and reported false totals over months. That pattern poisoned trust among the teams. They now plan independent counts and public monthly records.
Unexplained changes to the research log poisoned trust between the two labs, so they agreed to keep a dated shared record from now on.
Repeated secret changes can poison trust even if a group keeps meeting.
If dishonesty poisoned trust, open records are one step toward repair.

advanced-native-3414.text: Our research group now refuses to read studies from other labs and declines every joint workshop. It could cut itself off from fresh thinking. We can still judge ideas carefully after hearing them.
The food cooperative cut itself off from fresh thinking when it stopped asking growers about new ways to reduce waste.
Fresh thinking disappears when a team cuts itself off from outside ideas.
Do not cut yourself off from new ideas; hear them first, then decide what fits.

advanced-native-2321.text: The curator reviewed twenty interviews about the exhibition. She distilled the interviews into three recurring concerns, but kept one disagreement visible in the summary.
The flood team distilled the reports into two urgent access problems, then checked whether smaller streets were missing from the summary.
Distil the research into a concise result, and keep the limits of the evidence visible.
Distilling the notes into themes should not erase a minority view.

advanced-native-2904.text: At a meeting, Mina was wrongly accused of altering the figures. The team corrected the record the next day, but months later she still avoids presenting. The accusation left scars.
Repeated ridicule can leave scars long after a rehearsal ends, even when no injury is visible.
Leave scars can describe lasting emotional effects even when no physical mark is visible.
A correction can help after words leave scars, but it does not by itself prove that confidence has recovered.

advanced-native-2914.text: The club agreed a monthly supply limit. Each week someone added a few unplanned items, and the total is now above that limit. The club is sliding into overspending.
After several rushed handovers, the repair team slid into skipping checks, so the supervisor restored a signed handover list.
Sliding into overspending names a gradual drift shown by repeated small changes, not a single planned exception.
If a team slides into skipping checks, state the pattern and restore the missing control.

advanced-native-2929.text: Rain is forecast tomorrow, and the volunteer garden has one sunny afternoon. The planting beds are ready, but the path is still too muddy. They will make the most of it by planting the ready beds today.
The trial bus route lasts one month, so we should make the most of the chance by testing the journeys we need and recording any access problems.
Make the most of it refers to using an available chance well; it needs a clear it and a sensible priority.
Making the most of the time does not require doing every task at once or ignoring practical limits.

advanced-native-3644.text: At the playground, Imani tries a new climbing route while her father stays on a nearby bench. When she feels unsure, she returns to ask him a question, then chooses her next route herself. He is a secure base for her exploration.
After months of dependable help in class, Eli trusted his teacher as a secure base on their first school trip; he knew he could ask for help, then interviewed the museum guide himself.
A secure base stays available for help while a child explores; it does not make every choice for the child.
A secure base lets a child return for reassurance and then try the next step independently; support and exploration work together.

advanced-native-4019.text: Lena usually cooks for six friends. Catering for 200 guests is a different game altogether: she now needs allergy labels, separate serving stations and a timed food plan.
Turning a five-household delivery round into a citywide service is a different game altogether: we would need routes and a way to handle missed deliveries.
A different game altogether names a substantial change in demands, not merely a new location.
A different game altogether calls for naming new responsibilities instead of assuming earlier success is enough.

advanced-native-3963.text: The museum audio tour has twelve dense sections. Priya enjoys it in smaller doses: she listens to two sections in a short visit, then comes back another day for more.
I will study the new vocabulary in smaller doses so I can check each group before moving on.
In smaller doses describes the amount taken at one time, not necessarily the final total.
Taking demanding material in smaller doses can make it easier to return to.

advanced-native-3360.text: The youth centre expected to run only sports clubs next term. Strong interest in music is changing the script: staff are considering music sessions as well, but have not approved them yet.
The longer waiting list is changing the script for next year’s garden plan, although extra plots are not approved yet.
Changing the script means a new factor is altering what people expected to happen.
A new interest may change the script for a career without settling the final decision.

advanced-native-3594.text: Visitors see the gallery’s finished displays. Behind them, a conservation team repairs fragile objects, records damage and prepares pieces for each exhibition. The curator calls that team an engine room of the museum.
The caption team is an engine room of the news service: it prepares accurate subtitles before each morning bulletin.
An institution or team can be an engine room of a wider service when its continuing skilled work produces useful results.
A backstage operations team can be an engine room of an event without setting every policy.

advanced-native-3834.text: Mara’s work rota changed three times this week. She began answering shift messages during family dinner, so the scheduling pressure was spilling into her home time.
The delayed permit is spilling into the community workshop schedule: volunteers cannot open the room on Saturday.
When a problem spills into another part of life, its effects cross an identifiable boundary.
A skill learned in class can spill into a community project when students put it to use there.

advanced-native-3903.text: Nadia has a half-formed plan for a weekend repair club: she knows whom she wants to invite, but has not chosen a place or date.
The proposal is half-formed: we know who could help, but we still need to agree on a safe place to meet.
A half-formed idea deserves questions before it becomes a promise.
Calling a plan half-formed need not dismiss it; it names the work still to be done.

advanced-native-4122.text: Tariq missed one pottery session when he was ill, then returned each week and tried the wheel again. He kept showing up, and his bowls gradually became steadier.
I can keep showing up for the choir rehearsals and practise the difficult passage between meetings.
Keep showing up describes repeated participation, not flawless attendance.
When people keep showing up and practising, they create chances to improve without a guaranteed schedule.

advanced-native-4207.text: The volunteer brief sounded confusing until the coordinator unpacked the task: first check the list, then label each box, and finally record anything missing.
Before we start rehearsing, let us unpack the plan into who speaks first, where we stand, and when the lights change.
Unpacking a task makes its parts visible; it does not complete them.
When you unpack the plan, name what comes first and what each person still needs to do.

advanced-native-4511.text: For routine library notices, the team sends an email by default because most readers have opted in. Urgent closure alerts still go by text message. Email is the default choice, not the only channel.
For ordinary questions, the help desk is the default choice, but an emergency should go straight to the duty officer.
A default choice describes usual practice, not a ban on exceptions.
Name the condition that justifies switching away from the default choice.

advanced-native-4539.text: At the theatre entrance, Sam fumbled with his ticket while holding a wet umbrella. The usher waited, then pointed to the barcode on his phone.
I fumbled with the envelope at the counter until I set down my bag and could use both hands.
Fumbling with a ticket shows awkward handling, not a lack of money or a bad motive.
A free hand can help someone who is fumbling with a key.

advanced-native-4589.text: The repair appointment was meant to take forty minutes, but three repeated checks stretched it to four hours. The customer called it a drawn-out visit and asked what caused the delays.
The drawn-out registration process took three days rather than one because applicants had to submit the same form twice.
Drawn-out adds the idea of unwelcome prolonging, not merely length.
For a drawn-out process, name the original expectation and what extended it.

advanced-native-4702.text: The family shelter has a small reading room away from the busy corridor. After a difficult appointment, Jo sat there with a book and called it a haven for an hour of quiet.
For the night-shift volunteers, the small tea room became a haven where they could rest quietly between calls.
A haven offers a felt refuge from pressure; it need not remove the pressure forever.
A little haven works for someone when its actual conditions allow them to rest.

advanced-native-2262.text: After a week of organising the neighbourhood move, Elena had stopped joining her usual evening chats. On Sunday she laughed with her friends and started sketching again; she said she was beginning to come back to herself.
After the long registration drive, Mei began to come back to herself when she resumed her morning walks and jokes.
Coming back to yourself concerns familiar ease or identity, not a return to an address.
Coming back to yourself may begin with a familiar habit, without proving that recovery is complete.

advanced-native-2506.text: The festival coordinator is tracking menu changes, pickup times and two volunteer absences. Each time she answers one message, she loses track of another. “I have too many tabs open in my head,” she says, and starts a single task list.
With bills, a clinic appointment and a school form competing for attention, I have too many tabs open in my head.
Too many tabs open is a mental-load image: several thoughts compete for attention.
When you have too many tabs open mentally, name the competing tasks and choose one next step.

advanced-native-3682.text: After one failed practice session, Jo kept calling herself hopeless at public speaking. She later explained the project clearly to two visitors, which gave her reason to rewrite the story she was telling herself.
After completing two guided tours, I can rewrite the story I tell myself about speaking to strangers.
New evidence can help you rewrite the story you tell yourself without erasing an earlier mistake.
Rewriting the story you tell yourself means naming both the difficulty and what you have since managed to do.

advanced-native-2816.text: A false post said the community library would close on Friday. Staff checked the timetable: it closes on Saturday. The false post spread widely; as volunteers share the verified notice, the truth is catching up.
The verified route map is now reaching riders after the wrong diagram spread; the truth is catching up with the first notice.
The truth catches up only when a verified correction begins reaching people after a false claim.
Posting a correction is a step; whether the truth catches up with everyone still needs evidence.

advanced-native-3630.text: The community swim course waived half its enrolment fee, but Tessa still pays for two bus trips and pool access each week. Those costs may bite because they leave less for her monthly food budget.
The evening art class has a low entry price, but transport costs may bite for learners who must travel twice a week.
A cost bites when its effect is felt in a budget or earnings, not merely because the price looks high.
A discount can help while remaining fees may bite; name the payments and their actual effect.

advanced-native-4257.text: During the long map briefing, Chen noticed that his attention drifted from the route to the noise outside. He asked for a short pause, then found the marked stop on the map again.
When my attention drifts during a complex recipe, I return to the last numbered instruction before continuing.
Attention can drift during a long explanation even when the listener wants to learn.
Short checks and a clear return point can help when attention drifts, without calling anyone careless.

advanced-native-4410.text: At the night market, a quiet-hour rule stopped the buskers. Residents slept better, but traders said the silence was sucking the life out of the market. The council is trying an earlier music slot instead of a full ban.

pronunciation.phonemesBefore: æt ðə nˈaɪt mˈɑːɹkɪt, ɐ kwˈaɪətˈaʊɚ ɹˈuːl stˈɑːpt ðə bˈʌskɚz. ɹˈɛzᵻdənts slˈɛpt bˈɛɾɚ, bˌʌt tɹˈeɪdɚz sˈɛd ðə sˈaɪləns wʌz sˈʌkɪŋ ðə lˈaɪf ˌaʊɾəv ðə mˈɑːɹkɪt. ðə kˈaʊnsəl ɪz tɹˈaɪɪŋ ɐn ˈɜːlɪɚ mjˈuːzɪk slˈɑːt ɪnstˈɛd əvə fˈʊl bˈæn.
pronunciation.phonemesAfter: æt ðə nˈaɪt mˈɑːɹkɪt, ɐ kwˈaɪət ˈaʊɚ ɹˈuːl stˈɑːpt ðə bˈʌskɚz. ɹˈɛzᵻdənts slˈɛpt bˈɛɾɚ, bˌʌt tɹˈeɪdɚz sˈɛd ðə sˈaɪləns wʌz sˈʌkɪŋ ðə lˈaɪf ˌaʊɾəv ðə mˈɑːɹkɪt. ðə kˈaʊnsəl ɪz tɹˈaɪɪŋ ɐn ˈɜːlɪɚ mjˈuːzɪk slˈɑːt ɪnstˈɛd əvə fˈʊl bˈæn.

advanced-native-4410.text: Removing the open-mic slot would suck the life out of our small poetry evening, even if it made the timetable easier.
Suck the life out of means drain the energy from a place or activity, not literally stop it.
A necessary rule can still suck the life out of an event if it removes every lively part; a balanced alternative may keep its purpose.

advanced-native-4648.text: A pier bookshop had few weekday buyers. Weekend visitors placed enough orders for it to remain open, so the owner said the visitors kept the shop alive during the quiet season.
Without regular preorders, the family bakery would close during the bridge works. Those orders keep the shop alive until local trade returns.
Paid orders can keep a shop alive now without guaranteeing its future after a contract ends.
Neighbourhood preorders kept the store alive while street repairs reduced walk-in trade.

advanced-native-3312.text: For the craft day, advance sign-ups help us plan how many helpers to invite. But the rule says volunteers cannot switch rooms once the doors open, even if one room fills up. That handcuffs the team when numbers change.
The grant calendar keeps the theatre on track, but a ban on changing rehearsal dates could handcuff the project if a lead performer falls ill.
To handcuff the team figuratively is to severely restrict its choices; the source does not suggest literal cuffs or a legal ban.
A useful plan can handcuff the team if it bars a reasonable adjustment; explain both the benefit and the blocked choice.

advanced-native-3073.text: At a play workshop, the children turned cardboard boxes into a pretend weather station. The leader said they were less tied down by adult assumptions about what a box should be, although the scissors still had to be used safely.
Our art club used to copy one picture for every mural. We are less tied down by that model now, so members can propose new scenes while keeping the wall-safe paint rule.
During play, children may be less tied down by familiar logic while still respecting safety rules.
A design team can feel tied down by an old template even when it is free to test new ideas.

advanced-native-4308.text: Two schools held a joint mapping workshop. Teachers exchanged contacts and planned to compare maps next term. The organiser said it planted the seeds of future cooperation, though no joint course was agreed.
After their first harvest event, the gardeners and cooks met twice to compare compost results. Those follow-ups planted the seeds of a shared soil-care routine, now being tested in one plot.
An early exchange can plant the seeds of cooperation without guaranteeing a lasting partnership.
A neighbourhood workshop planted the seeds of a joint project; the teams will decide its next steps later.

advanced-native-3849.text: The museum receives thirty new tour requests each week, up from ten, but its guides can still lead twelve tours. Requests now outpace the team’s ability to offer tours, so it is training more guides.
The clinic's appointment requests now outpace its ability to offer visits, so the team is reviewing hours before promising new slots.
Rising requests can outpace a team’s ability to respond; a large queue alone does not establish the rate comparison.
If requests outpace a team’s ability to respond, name both sides and explain a realistic next step without claiming that all service has stopped.

advanced-native-4513.text: The evening workshop ends after the last bus leaves. Volunteers can attend online from home, and both formats cover the same material. For anyone relying on that bus, the online session may make more sense.
With a heavy display case to move and a loading ramp at the rear, the rear entrance may make more sense than the front stairs; check the route before delivery.
An option may make more sense when a particular constraint favors it; name that constraint instead of claiming the option is always best.
“Make more sense” can describe a clearer explanation or a wiser practical choice. In advice, compare the options and say what would change the recommendation.

advanced-native-2676.text: The town orchestra had split into three rehearsal groups after losing its hall. When a new hall opened, the conductor set up joint rehearsals to stitch the orchestra back together.
The youth theatre split into separate casts after losing its stage. Joint rehearsals helped stitch the theatre back together when the stage reopened.
After the debate club split into separate teams, a shared project helped stitch the club back together.
The school's music programme had split into separate clubs; joint rehearsals could stitch it back together.

advanced-native-2331.text: The actor barely speaks during the long close-up, but the camera holds on her face. Her stillness and small changes of expression give her a quiet screen presence that keeps us watching.
Even in silence, the performer has screen presence that gives the long shot its tension.
Her quiet screen presence makes the close-up worth holding.
Screen presence can come from a small reaction rather than a loud performance.

advanced-native-2495.text: At the busy repair desk, Nia remembers which parts fit each model. She finds the right replacement quickly, so her memory is a real advantage when customers are waiting.
Knowing two routes is a real advantage when the main road is blocked.
Reliable evidence can be a real advantage when preparation time is short.
A skill is a real advantage only when it helps with the task at hand.

advanced-native-2694.text: Mara opens the library app, chooses a study room and confirms the time. She books the room with a few taps on her phone instead of queueing at the desk.
The museum app lets visitors choose a tour with a few taps on the screen.
A few taps can replace a phone call for a simple booking.
The phrase a few taps describes the screen actions, not the whole activity afterwards.

advanced-native-3454.text: On weekdays, Jun’s parents chop vegetables and cook rice in their own kitchen. Jun packs the home-cooked food and eats it for lunch at school.
They brought home-cooked food to the picnic after preparing it in their kitchen.
Home-cooked food can be shared somewhere other than home.
Takeaway eaten at home is not automatically home-cooked food.

advanced-native-3732.text: At first, the puzzle club checked the clues before asking for hints. Now several members open the answer app immediately and rarely test an idea. Their coach worries that this habit could make them mentally lazier.
If we stop checking the reasons behind each answer, quick hints could make us mentally lazier.
A shortcut may make us mentally lazier only if we stop evaluating its answers.
Using a tool need not make us mentally lazier when we still explain our reasoning.

advanced-native-3739.text: The workshop is replacing its paper rota with a shared calendar. Staff first test it on one shift, report problems and vote on the final layout. Those choices help them stay in control of the change.
A small trial and regular feedback help the team stay in control of the change.
The museum guides stayed in control of the change by voting on the visitor route before it was introduced.
A trial lets volunteers stay in control of the change without promising a perfect result.

advanced-native-4537.text: The clinic route looks short on a map, but Mina must cross a busy road to change from train to bus, then wait ten minutes for another bus. With a stroller, she finds those awkward transfers tiring.
The direct shuttle saves patients from awkward transfers at the crowded station.
Awkward transfers can outweigh a small saving in total travel time.
A same-platform change may avoid awkward transfers for travellers with limited mobility.

advanced-native-4555.text: The stadium car park will close before the evening match. Priya will leave the car at home and take the train from her neighbourhood station instead.
For the street festival, we can leave the car at home, take the train and walk from the station.
We can leave the car at home when a direct bus serves the event.
Leaving the car at home for one trip does not mean giving up driving forever.

advanced-native-3601.text: At the archive, three senior curators alone can read the restoration notes. Until the notes are shared, the method remains in the hands of only a few.
The maintenance procedure is in the hands of only a few until the guide is shared.
The records stayed in the hands of only a few until the team created a public guide.
Expertise may be valuable, but it should not remain in the hands of only a few when others need to learn.

advanced-native-3694.text: The town used to require every shop to close at six. After a cooperative introduced shared late deliveries, evening markets became normal. The cooperative rewrote the rules for local trading.
The exchange programme rewrites the rules for borrowing tools in this neighbourhood.
A small design tweak rarely rewrites the rules of an entire industry.
The shared workshop rewrote the rules for who could use expensive equipment.

advanced-native-3723.text: At the science fair, the model bridge lit up and moved in perfect rhythm. It dazzled people during the demonstration, although the judges still had to test its strength.
The colourful prototype can dazzle people before anyone checks how well it works.
A polished slide can dazzle people without answering their practical questions.
A clear experiment may dazzle people and still withstand careful testing.

advanced-native-3725.text: A rural clinic began treating an infection that had previously left many children disabled. The new treatment changed the fate of families who once faced lifelong care costs.
Reliable transport can change the fate of pupils who used to miss months of school.
A lasting chance to study can change the fate of a child more than a one-day gift.
Medical access changed the fate of patients who once had no effective treatment.

advanced-native-3775.text: Mia selected two notebooks and entered her delivery address. When she pressed the final checkout button, she placed an order; the shop will confirm it by email.
You place an order when you submit the purchase request, not when you open the shopping page.
Saving an item in a basket is different from placing an order.
The club placed an order for thirty badges and is waiting for confirmation.

advanced-native-3839.text: Two coastal towns opened year-round arts studios and affordable flats. Those combined opportunities pull people in like magnets, though not every visitor decides to move.
Free workshops and affordable studios pull people in like magnets during the festival.
Strong reasons to visit can pull people in like magnets without making them stay.
Shared gardens and evening classes pull people in like magnets from nearby streets.

advanced-native-3844.text: A seaside town opened new offices three years ago, and its population has risen every year since. The town keeps swelling as more workers settle nearby.
The volunteer list keeps swelling because neighbours join after each workshop.
The guest list keeps swelling, so the venue may need more seats.
Numbers kept swelling for months before the organisers added another session.

advanced-native-3850.text: The housing office missed its repair target for three consecutive months, and residents now wait longer. Service quality begins to slide when small delays become routine.
Attendance begins to slide when weekly cancellations become normal.
A few setbacks do not prove that an entire service has begun to slide.
Customer confidence began to slide after repeated missed deadlines.

advanced-native-3893.text: A museum visitor had never considered pottery classes. After seeing students shape clay in a short film, she wanted to try one herself. The film stirred desire for a first lesson.
A glimpse of the rehearsal can stir desire to hear the whole concert.
A vivid story can stir desire to explore a subject someone had ignored.
Stirring desire does not mean a viewer has already decided to buy.

advanced-native-3901.text: Lena had planned to buy a used bicycle for months. A repair shop then posted a video showing how easily old bikes can be restored. The video amplified an existing desire rather than giving her a new one.
The new workshop details amplified an existing desire among volunteers who had already signed up.
A reminder can amplify an existing desire without creating a new need.
The exhibition preview amplified an existing desire to visit among people who already held tickets.

advanced-native-3909.text: The community centre tested its new wayfinding sign with first-time visitors and enlarged the route text. It was built with clarity in mind.
The new timetable was built with busy commuters in mind, so the next bus time is easy to find.
The guide was built with first-time visitors in mind, so each step is clearly numbered.
A product can be built with speed in mind and still be easy to understand.

advanced-native-3942.text: Two exchange students could not explain every chess move in the same language, but they understood each other through the game. Chess gave them a shared language.
In the cooking workshop, preparing the same dish gave the visitors a shared language.
A game can offer a shared language before its players know many of the same words.
For the visiting group, music became a shared language, not proof that every misunderstanding had ended.

advanced-native-3944.text: The local and visiting choir members began by rehearsing separately. After they exchanged songs and practised together, the distance between them shrank.
After the teams cooked together twice, the distance between them shrank.
The distance between them shrank when the neighbours began planning together.
The distance between them is shrinking, though they still disagree about some details.

advanced-native-3981.text: Mina tried a logic puzzle that made her test several possible answers before finding one that worked. She called it a workout for the brain.
Comparing the clues was a workout for the brain, even though the puzzle was short.
A new strategy question can be a workout for the brain when it asks us to weigh alternatives.
Before the exam, a brief reasoning game gave the class a workout for the brain.

advanced-native-4028.text: The regional orchestra welcomes many young players, but only six places are available in its final ensemble. At that stage, the road narrows sharply.
Many people enter the open auditions, but the road narrows when only three parts remain.
The road narrows when the number of available places falls in the final round.
The road narrows sharply for applicants, but the result for any one person is still open.

advanced-native-4029.text: A young violinist showed skill, but the local programme ended before she could practise with a teacher. Her promise may never fully bloom if she cannot find another chance to train.
Her promise may never fully bloom if the workshop closes before she can build her skills.
The young inventor’s promise may never fully bloom if she cannot test her designs.
His promise may never fully bloom while he is shut out of performances, though another chance could change that.

advanced-native-4055.text: The projector stopped working before the talk, so Nora called three suppliers and checked the storeroom. She was hunting for a replacement cable.
They hunted for a spare microphone by calling nearby schools and checking the storage room.
We hunted for a spare key in the places where it was last used.
They are hunting for a replacement part, but they have not found one yet.

advanced-native-4070.text: The club spent most of its small budget on accessible transport rather than decorations. This plan is a snapshot of the club’s priorities for this event.
The volunteer budget offers a snapshot of their priorities for this weekend.
A spending plan can be a snapshot of their priorities for one project.
The list gives a snapshot of her priorities today, not a complete account of her values.

advanced-native-4081.text: During the field trip, Ravi used his small camera to record routes, signs and interviews. By the end of the week, it felt like an extra limb.
After months of sketching on the same tablet, it felt like an extra limb to her.
Her camera felt like an extra limb during the long reporting project.
By the third week, the interpreter’s headset felt like an extra limb during long interviews.

advanced-native-2356.text: At the puppet show, children cheered for the daring journey, while grandparents grew quiet at a song from their youth. The show spoke different emotional languages to the two groups.
The mural spoke different emotional languages to the pupils and their grandparents.
The same photograph can speak different emotional languages to a newcomer and a former resident.
A performance spoke different emotional languages to the two families without dividing them.

advanced-native-2579.text: Before the school trip, the coach sent parents a message confirming that the delayed bus had been replaced. The update saved them a lot of worry, although arrival would still be late.
A confirmed pickup message could save the parents a lot of worry during the delay.
A precise collection time can save a lot of worry for someone waiting at home.
The nurse’s short status update saved the family a lot of worry without promising a diagnosis.

advanced-native-2712.text: For this month’s radio set, Leo chooses only acoustic folk songs, even though he knows other genres well. He is choosing to stay in one musical lane for now.
For the festival set, the group stayed in one musical lane and played only folk songs.
A themed playlist can stay in one musical lane without limiting its maker forever.
She did not stay in one musical lane: her next set moved from jazz to traditional songs.

advanced-native-3086.text: The head teacher first rejected a later library closing time. After hearing how it would help working families, her stance may soften, though she has not decided yet.
After seeing the revised plan, the chair softened her stance but requested another review.
The council softened its stance after residents presented a workable alternative.
Their stance may soften with more evidence, but agreement is not guaranteed.

advanced-native-3275.text: The chess club announced that missing three sessions would trigger a warning, but nobody recorded absences. Soon the rule began to lose its teeth.
Without regular checks, the equipment rule may lose its teeth even if the sign remains.
A safety warning can lose its teeth when the promised inspection never happens.
The club’s code lost its teeth after leaders stopped responding to repeated breaches.

advanced-native-3321.text: Two groups were booked into the same meeting room. The organiser said, “We will sort it out after checking both groups’ times,” but neither group had moved yet.
We have not resolved the clash yet, but we can sort it out after checking the schedule.
If the forms conflict, we will sort it out after checking the original requests.
The team sorted it out by confirming both delivery dates with the supplier.

advanced-native-3346.text: The swimming club set a goal of forty pool lengths by June. The number gives beginners something to aim at, though no one has reached it yet.
The small weekly target gave the new members something to aim at without guaranteeing success.
A clear delivery date gives the team something to aim at during the project.
The score target gave the players something to aim at, not proof they had reached it.

advanced-native-3351.text: The exhibition team held four planning meetings and changed the poster twice, but it still had no venue. “We are not getting anywhere,” the leader said.
They were not getting anywhere with the booking form until they agreed on one design.
